It is also a specific place. Yāqūt said: "Poets have mentioned it frequently and confused that Liwā with the sand, so it is hard to separate them; and it is a valley of the valleys of Banū Sulaym."

dervis-irab:73-77.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ كادُوا لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ عَنِ الَّذِي أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ لِتَفْتَرِيَ عَلَيْنا غَيْرَهُ) The wāw is resumptive, and إن is the lightened form of the heavy one, and is inoperative; it is also permissible, though rare, for it to operate, as has preceded. كادوا: incomplete past verb, among the verbs of approximation, and the wāw is its noun. The lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), and the clause يفتنونك is the khabar of كادوا. عن الذي: attached to يفتنونك, which has been made to contain the sense of "turn you away", and for that reason it was made transitive with عن. The clause أوحينا is a ṣila, and إليك is attached to أوحينا. لتفتري: the lām is the lām of reason, and تفتري is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after the lām of reason; علينا: attached to تفتري; the agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; and غيره is the direct object. (وَإِذاً لَاتَّخَذُوكَ خَلِيلًا) The wāw is a conjunction, and إذن is a particle of response (jazāʾ); its answer is implied with the conditional لو, i.e. "and if you had followed their wish and carried out their proposals, for the fulfilment of which they tried to bring you down". The lām prepares for the oath, the implied form being "by Allah, they would have taken you". The kāf is the first direct object and خليلا the second direct object. (وَلَوْلا أَنْ ثَبَّتْناكَ لَقَدْ كِدْتَ تَرْكَنُ إِلَيْهِمْ شَيْئاً قَلِيلًا) لولا is a particle of prevention because of existence. أن and what is in its scope is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "had it not been for Our making you firm and Our protecting you". The lām is the answer to لولا, and قد is a particle of affirmation. كاد and its noun; the clause تركن is its khabar; إليهم is attached to تركن; and شيئا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, with the sense of leaning (rukūn), i.e. "a little of leaning". (إِذاً لَأَذَقْناكَ ضِعْفَ الْحَياةِ وَضِعْفَ الْمَماتِ ثُمَّ لا تَجِدُ لَكَ عَلَيْنا نَصِيراً) إذن is a particle of answer and response, its answer also implied with the conditional لو, i.e. "and if you had followed their wish and carried out their proposals, for the fulfilment of which they tried to bring you down". The lām prepares for the oath. أذقناك: verb, agent and direct object. ضعف is a second object, and الحياة is the muḍāf ilayhi; an omitted element must be posited, i.e. "double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death". ثم is a conjunction of delay, and لا is negative. تجد: imperfect verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "you". لك: attached to تجد; علينا: attached to نصيرا; and نصيرا is the direct object. (وَإِنْ كادُوا لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ لِيُخْرِجُوكَ مِنْها) The wāw is a conjunction; إن is the lightened form, and it is permissible to make it inoperative or operative. كادوا is among the verbs of approximation, and the wāw is its noun. The lām is the distinguishing lām, and the clause يستفزونك is the khabar of كادوا. من الأرض: attached to يستفزونك; وليخرجوك: attached to يستفزونك; and منها is attached to يخرجوك. The pronoun returns to the land, which is the land of al-Madīna.
(وَإِذاً لا يَلْبَثُونَ خِلافَكَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا) The wāw is a conjunction, and إذن is a particle of response and consequence that is inoperative. لا is negative. يلبثون: imperfect verb, nominative. خلافك, i.e. خلفك ("behind you"), is an adverbial attached to يلبثون, and on it is the saying of the poet:
عفت الديار خلافهم فكأنما ... بسط الشواطب بينهن حصيرا
(The abodes became effaced behind them, as though the strip-splitters had spread a mat among them.)
The poet describes their abodes after them as being effaced and heaped with refuse for lack of sweeping and of anyone to tend them. Al-shawāṭib are the women who split the shaṭb of the date palm, i.e. its green fronds, making them into a mat. إلا is a particle of restriction. قليلا is an adjective of an omitted adverbial, i.e. "a little time", or an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a brief stay"; so it is an adverbial or a mafʿūl muṭlaq. (سُنَّةَ مَنْ قَدْ أَرْسَلْنا قَبْلَكَ مِنْ رُسُلِنا وَلا تَجِدُ لِسُنَّتِنا تَحْوِيلًا) سنة is made accusative as an emphatic maṣdar, i.e. "Allah established that as a custom". Al-Farrāʾ preferred that it be accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "like the custom of Allah"; and according to this parsing one should not pause at قليلا. Others preferred that it be made accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "follow the custom"; there is no objection to that, as all the views are equal.

* Rhetoric:
- The story of Thaqīf and its proposals:
In these verses are various kinds of rhetoric, and to establish them it is necessary to relate the story of their revelation. It is related that Thaqīf said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We will not enter into your cause until you give us qualities in which we can take pride over the Arabs: that we not be tithed, that we not be mustered, that we not bow (nujabbā) in our prayer, that every usury owed to us be ours and every usury owed by us be waived for us, that you let us enjoy al-Lāt for a year until we take what is offered to it, and when we have taken it we shall break it and become Muslim, and that you declare our valley sacred as you declared Makka sacred; and if the Arabs say 'Why did you do this?', then say 'Allah commanded me to.'" They came with their document and he wrote: "In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate. This is a document from Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah, to Thaqīf: they are not to be tithed and not to be mustered." They said: "And not to bow." The Messenger of Allah was silent. Then they said to the scribe: "Write: and not to bow", while the scribe was looking at the Messenger of Allah. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb stood up, drew his sword and said: "You have kindled the heart of our Prophet, O company of Thaqīf; may Allah kindle your hearts with fire!" They said: "It is not you we are speaking to; we are speaking to Muḥammad." Then it was revealed. Some of the vocabulary must be explained. Their words لا نعشر (in the passive) mean that a tenth of our wealth is not taken from us; ولا نحشر (also passive) means that we are not driven to fight; ولا نجبّى في صلاتنا (also passive), from al-tajbiya, which is, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, that a person stands in the posture of one bowing; Abū ʿUbayda said it occurs in two states, one of which is that he places his hands on his knees, and the other that he falls on his face kneeling, which is prostration. What is meant is "we do not bow and do not prostrate". The story is curious and illustrates important matters.
A- The persistence of the people, their insolence and their persistence in arrogance and haughtiness.
B- The forbearance of the Prophet ﷺ and his taking the people with gentleness and winning-over, in which is the utmost of tact and statecraft.
C- The firmness of ʿUmar and his boldness, and not without reason was he named al-Fārūq. As for the aspects of rhetoric in the verse, they are:
1- Elaboration (iṭnāb) in mentioning this episode, which establishes for you the shrewdness and resourcefulness of the statesman, who takes his people with gentleness and patience and does not let his soul be dissipated in grief while he sees persistence in error and insistence on folly.
2- Exaggeration in minimizing the approach (kaydūda), because the mere gentleness that statecraft requires and the winning-over of the people were held against the Prophet, since a fault grows great according to its doer, in accordance with what is reported, that the good deeds of the righteous are the evil deeds of those brought near.
3- The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya) in أذقناك ضعف الحياة; parallels to it have often preceded.
4- Omission: the punishment was omitted out of honour for the station of the Prophet ﷺ. In origin it is a described noun, i.e. "a double punishment in life and a double punishment in death"; then the described noun was omitted and the attribute, namely "double", put in its place, and then the attribute was annexed as the described noun is annexed, so it was said "the double of life and the double of death", as if it were said "We would have made you taste the pain of life and the pain of death".
- Ibn Hishām has an enjoyable section on كاد, which he gave in the sixth chapter of his book al-Mughnī, in warning against matters that became well known among the parsers while the correct view is the opposite:
«Eighteenth: their saying that for كاد, its affirmative is a negation and its negative an affirmation. So when it is said «كاد يفعل» its meaning is that he did not do it, and when it is said «لم يكد يفعل» its meaning is that he did it. The proof of the first is «وإن كادوا ليفتنونك عن الذي أوحينا إليك» and his saying:
«كادت النفس أن تفيض عليه»
(The soul all but flowed out over him.)
and the proof of the second is «وما كادوا يفعلون».
This became so well known among them that al-Maʿarrī made it a riddle, saying:
أنحويّ هذا العصر ما هي لفظة ... جرت في لسائي جرهم وثمود
[Translator's note: the printed text reads «لسائي»; the sense requires «لساني» ("my tongue"), and the second hemistich «لسان جرهم» is probably what is meant.]
إذا استعملت في صورة الجحد أثبتت ... وإن أثبتت قامت مقام جحود
(O grammarian of this age, what is the word that ran on the tongues of Jurhum and Thamūd? When used in the form of denial it affirms, and when affirmed it stands in the place of denial.)
The correct view is that its ruling is the ruling of all other verbs, in that its negation is a negation and its affirmation an affirmation. The explanation is that its meaning is approximation, and there is no doubt that the meaning of «كاد يفعل» is "he came near to doing", and that the meaning of «ما كاد يفعل» is "he did not come near to doing"; so its predicate is always negated. As for when it is negated, it is clear, because if approximation to the act is negated, then the occurrence of that act is negated by reason. Its proof is «إذا أخرج يده لم يكد يراها», and for this reason it is more eloquent than saying «لم يرها», because one who has not seen may have come near to seeing. As for when the approximation is affirmed, it is because informing of the nearness of a thing by custom implies its non-occurrence; otherwise the information would be of its occurrence and not of the approach to its occurrence, since it is not good in custom to say of one who has prayed "he approached prayer", even if he did not pray until he approached prayer. There is no difference in what we have mentioned between كاد and يكاد. If «وما كادوا يفعلون» is raised against this, though they did do it, since what is meant by the act is the slaughter and the Exalted said «فذبحوها», the answer is that it is information about their state at the beginning of the matter, for they were at first far from slaughtering it, by the evidence of what is recited to us of their obstinacy and their repeated questions. Since the like of this became frequent for one from whom approximation to the act was first negated and who then did it afterwards, someone imagined that this very verb is what indicates the occurrence of that very act. It is not so: the occurrence of the act is understood from other evidence, as it was understood in the verse from His words, the Exalted, «فذبحوها».»

dervis-irab:78-81.t:
* Vocabulary:
(لِدُلُوكِ الشَّمْسِ): That is, from the time of its decline. One says dalakat al-shams meaning it set, and it is also said, it declined. Its derivation is from al-dalk (rubbing), because a person rubs his eyes when looking at it. If dulūk means declining, then the verse includes the five obligatory prayers; and if it means setting, then the noon and afternoon prayers are excluded from it. The origin of this root, that is, whatever has dāl and lām as its first and second radicals, indicates change and movement from one place to another. Thus al-dalba is the singular of al-dalb, a tree with large leaves, no flowers and no fruit, which rises upward in the air as if it had moved from below to above; and from this their saying: «هو من أهل الدّربة، بمعالجة الدّلبة» ("he is one of the people of skill, by working the plane tree"), and from it are made the clappers (nawāqīs), that is, he is a Christian. He watered his land with the dūlāb (water-wheel), with fatḥa on the dāl, and they water with water-wheels, used to carry water from one place to another to irrigate the land. Dalaja comes from al-dalja, which is night travel and moving by night from one place to another; and from it is dalaja and "his eyes streamed", and "how is a western dālij", meaning one who goes back and forth with the bucket from the well to the trough; and "he spent his night dalluj". The poet said:
كأنها وقد براها الإخماس ... ودلج الليل وهاد قياس
شرائح النبع براها القوّاس
(As if she, after the five-day thirst-stages and the night travel had worn her thin, were slivers of nabʿ wood, which the bow-maker pared down.)
Dalaḥa, with the unpointed ḥāʾ, means he walked heavily; dildala aʿḍāʾahu dildalatan means he moved his limbs in walking; and tadaldala fī mashyihi means he shook and swayed in his walking. Dalasa l-ẓalām, "the darkness", is well known, and "he went out in the dalas and ghalas (the darkness before dawn)"; dallasa l-muḥaddith fī ḥadīthihi means the hadith transmitter brought in it something other than the real thing, as if he moved from one event to another, and from this comes the tadlīs of the seller who hides the faults in what he sells and shows its good points. "A land the floods have dalaṣathā" means they moved it from one state to another and made it smooth, and from this comes dirʿ dilāṣ (a smooth, glossy coat of mail). Abū l-Ṭayyib said:
لأمة فاضة أضاة دلاص ... أحكمت نسجها يدا داوود
(A coat of mail, flowing, a pool of glossy sheen, whose weaving the hand of David made firm.)
Dalaʿa and adlaʿa lisānahu means he put his tongue out of his mouth; dalaʿa bi-nafsihi and indalaʿa means he came out and went slack from distress or thirst, as the dog lolls its tongue. Figuratively: indalaʿa l-sayf min ghimdihi wa-indalaqa (the sword sprang from its scabbard), and indalaʿat alsinat al-nīrān (the tongues of flame leapt out). Al-mudallaʿ is one raised in luxury and ease, and the noun is al-dalāʿa; it is a colloquial expression, hence an eloquent colloquialism. Dalafa means he walked like one in fetters; one says "the old man and the fettered man dalafa, dalīfan and dulūfan", which is faster than creeping; shaykh dālif and ʿajāʾiz dawālif. Ṭarafa said:
لا كبير دالف من هرم ... أرهب الناس ولا كلّ الظفر
(Not a creeping, decrepit old man who frightens people, nor one whose claw is blunt.)
And "he came creeping with his load" because of its heaviness. Dalaqa ʿalayhim al-sayl means the flood poured upon them; dalaqat ʿalayhim al-khayl and indalaqat; dalaqū ʿalayhim al-gharra means they launched the raid on them; dalaqa l-baʿīr shiqshiqatahu means the camel brought out its throat-pouch; and "he struck him and his belly's intestines spilled out". Dalaka l-shayʾ means he rubbed it with his hand, which has already been mentioned. Dallahu ʿalā l-ṭarīq means he guided him on the road, and he is the dalīl of the desert. Dallat tadillu, and she is "of beautiful coquetry", that is, she displayed all the charms of her body to captivate others. Dalliha fulān dalhan means he was bewildered and lost his mind from worry or love, so there is in it a figurative movement. Adlaytu dalwī fī l-biʾr means I lowered my bucket into the well; dallā rijlayhi min al-sarīr means he dangled his legs from the bed; tadallat al-thamara min al-shajara means the fruit hung from the tree, ready to move from it; adlā bi-ḥaqqihi wa-bi-ḥujjatihi means he presented it, as if moving it to the place of debate. It would take us long to speak if we were to pursue what is in this wonderful root.
(غَسَقِ اللَّيْلِ): Al-ghasaq is darkness. It is also said to be the entering of the first part of the night, as al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said; and it is also said to be the blackness of night and its darkness. Its origin is from flowing: one says ʿasaqat al-ʿayn when its tears flow, as if the darkness poured down upon the world and flowed over them. In al-Asās: "They say 'from the ghasaq to the falaq', which is the entering of the first of the night when the darkness mixes; ghasaqa l-layl yaghsiqu ghasaqan; and Banū Tamīm say aghsaqa." Ibn Qays said:
إن هذا الليل قد غسقا ... واشتكيت الهمّ والأزقا
(This night has grown dark, and I complain of worry and of straits.)
And Jassās said:
أزور إذا ما أغسق الليل خلّتي ... حذار العدى أو أن يرجّم قائل
(I visit my beloved when night darkens, for fear of enemies or lest some speaker cast aspersions.)
(فَتَهَجَّدْ): Al-hujūd is leaving sleep for prayer, and there is disagreement among the lexicographers about it. It is said that it means sleep; it is also said that hujūd is shared between the sleeper and the one who prays. Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: "tahajjada: he prayed at night, and tahajjada: he slept", and this is the view of Abū ʿUbayd and al-Layth. The pattern tafaʿʿala comes for removal, as in taḥarraja, taʾaththama and taḥawwaba. In al-Asās: "Hajada l-rajul hujūdan wa-tahajjada: he left sleep for prayer (فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِ); and bāta fulān mutahajjidan: alone. Hajjadnā: we let him sleep." Labīd said:
قال هجّدنا فقد طال السّرى ... وقدرنا إن خنى الدهر غفل
(He said, "Let us sleep, for the night journey has been long, and we have power [over time], if time's treachery is heedless.")
And in al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: "Al-hujūd is sleeping by day, al-hujūʿ is sleeping by night, and al-tahajjud is night prayer."
(نافِلَةً): Redundant.

* I'rab:
(أَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِدُلُوكِ الشَّمْسِ إِلى غَسَقِ اللَّيْلِ) (أقم الصلاة) is an imperative verb, a latent agent whose implied form is "you", and a direct object. As to the lām in (لدلوك), there are two views. One is that it means "after", that is, after the declining of the sun, like their saying "I wrote my letter for three nights remaining" [Translator's note: «كتبت كتابي لثلاث خلون»], and the meanings of the lām will come in the section on Benefits. The second is that it is in its basic sense, that is, "on account of its declining"; yet the unity of time and the unity of the agent are both absent in «أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس»: the agent of standing is the addressee, while the agent of declining is the sun, and their times differ, since the time of performing the prayer comes after the time of declining. For that reason it is put in the genitive with the lām of cause. It is also said that it is for the beginning of the range, and that in the speech a muḍāf is omitted. In every case the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (أقم). As to (إلى غسق الليل), there are two views: one is that it is also attached to (أقم), as the limit of performing the prayer; the second is that it is attached to an omitted ḥāl from (الصلاة), that is "perform it extending to the darkness of the night".
(وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كانَ مَشْهُوداً) The wāw is a conjunction. (قرآن) is conjoined to (الصلاة), or is accusative as an incitement (al-ighrāʾ). The first means "and perform the dawn prayer", the prayer being expressed by recitation, which is one of its pillars; the second means "and upon you is the recitation of dawn", that is, hold to it. The first is less strained, and further, the omission of verbal nouns, which are operative, has not been heard of. The clause (إن قرآن …) is a reason for the command; (إن) and its name, and the clause (كان مشهودا) is its khabar; (مشهودا) is the khabar of (كان) and its name is latent, its implied form being "it".
(وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِ نافِلَةً لَكَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (من الليل) is attached to (تهجد), that is, "keep vigil with the Qur'an for part of the night". You may also attach it to an omitted verb, that is "stand a standing at night". Al-Ḥawfī said: (من) is attached to a verb indicated by the meaning of the speech, its implied form being "and stay awake part of the night with the Qur'an". The fāʾ is a conjunction; (تهجد) is an imperative verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "you"; (به) is attached to (تهجد); (نافلة) is a ḥāl; and (لك) is an adjective of (نافلة), that is: pray, the prayer being supererogatory for you. It is also permissible for (نافلة) to be a maṣdar like al-ʿāfiya and al-ʿāqiba, in which case it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, the meaning being "perform a supererogatory act". I do not know how some parsed it as an object of (تهجد), when it is an intransitive verb, unless it is said that he embedded in it the meaning of "worship", and how little we need that.
(عَسى أَنْ يَبْعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقاماً مَحْمُوداً) (عسى) is among the verbs of hope, and hope on Allah's part is certain to be fulfilled. The name of (عسى) is latent, and (أن يبعثك) is its khabar. (ربك) is the agent of (يبعثك), or the matter is one of tanāzuʿ (competing governors). (مقاما) is accusative as an adverbial, that is "in a station", or a mafʿūl muṭlaq, because (يبعثك) here means "He will establish you", or a ḥāl, that is "possessing a station". (محمودا) is an adjective of (مقاما).
(وَقُلْ رَبِّ أَدْخِلْنِي مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ وَأَخْرِجْنِي مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ) (رب) is a vocative from which the vocative particle has been omitted. (أدخلني) is a verb of supplication, a latent agent, and the yāʾ is a direct object. (مدخل صدق) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq because it is a maṣdar mīmī, and its annexation to (صدق) is the annexation of the described to its description, or is for clarification. (وأخرجني مخرج صدق) is conjoined to the corresponding clause.
(وَاجْعَلْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ سُلْطاناً نَصِيراً) (واجعل) is conjoined to (أدخلني) and (أخرجني). (لي) is the second object of (اجعل) and (سلطانا) is the first object of (اجعل). (نصيرا) is an adjective. (ومن لدنك) is a ḥāl, because it was an adjective of (سلطانا), or it is attached to whatever the first is attached to.
(وَقُلْ جاءَ الْحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ الْباطِلُ) That is: say when you enter Mecca as a conqueror. The clause (جاء الحق) is the content of the saying, and (زهق الباطل) is conjoined to it.
(إِنَّ الْباطِلَ كانَ زَهُوقاً) (إن) and its name, and the clause (كان) is its khabar, and (زهوقا) is the khabar of (كان).

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «وقل جاء الحق وزهق الباطل ان الباطل كان زهوقا»:
The art of the appended clause (al-tadhyīl), which is when the poet or prose writer appends to his speech, after it is complete and silence upon it is fitting, a sentence that confirms what precedes and increases its emphasis, and which runs in the manner of a proverb to add confirmation. The difference between it and takmīl (completion) is that takmīl comes to a meaning that needs perfecting, while tadhyīl adds nothing except confirmation and emphasis of the first statement. This verse is among the greatest proofs of it, since the last sentence is the appended clause that came out in the manner of a circulating proverb. Among its poetic examples is the saying of al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī:
ولست بمستبق أخا لا تلمّه ... على شعث أيّ الرجال المهذّب
(You will not retain a brother whom you do not set right in his disarray; which man is refined?)
That is, the one whose deeds are free of fault and whose qualities are pleasing. The first part of the verse indicates by its implication the negation of the perfect among men, and its second part is a confirmation and affirmation of that, since the question in it is one of denial, that is, there is no refined man among men. The scholars of badīʿ agreed that his saying «أي الرجال المهذب» is one of the best tadhyīl in poetry, because it came out as a proverb, and hence they said that al-Nābigha was the best poet of people by a quarter of a verse.

* Benefits:
1- The glad tidings were fulfilled, the command of Allah came, and Muḥammad entered Mecca as a conqueror, as is well known in the history of the Sīra. Jibrīl said to Muḥammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he came down with this verse on the day of the conquest: "Take your staff, then throw it." So he went to the idols one by one, prodding each in the eye with the staff and saying, "The truth has come and falsehood has vanished", and the idol fell on its face, until he had thrown them all down. There remained the idol of Khuzāʿa on top of the Kaʿba, made of yellow glass. He said, "ʿAlī, throw it down." So he climbed up, threw it and smashed it, to the end of this unique story.
2- The meanings of the prepositional lām:
Ibn Hishām in Mughnī l-Labīb gave twenty-two meanings for the prepositional lām, whereas others were content to mention only twelve and denied that it has these other meanings. The following is a useful summary of that: 1- Ownership, as in «لله ما في السموات».
2- Quasi-ownership. Ibn Hishām made this class two: specification, as in al-sarj lil-dābba ("the saddle is for the mount"), and entitlement, which occurs between a meaning and a person, as in «العزة لله» and "the command is Allah's".
3- Transitivisation to the direct object, as in «فهب لي من لدنك وليا». Ibn Hishām and others preferred to exemplify it with "mā aḍraba Zaydan li-ʿAmr" ("how much Zayd beats ʿAmr!"), because ḍaraba is originally transitive, but when the verb of wonder is built from it, it is moved to the pattern fuʿula with ḍamma on the ʿayn and becomes intransitive; it is then made transitive by the hamza to Zayd and by the lām to ʿAmr.
4- Cause, as in the saying of Abū Ṣakhr al-Hudhalī:
وإني لتعروني لذكراك هزة ... كما انتفض العصفور بلّله القطر
(A tremor comes over me at remembering you, as the sparrow shakes when the rain has wetted it.)
That is, on account of my remembering you.
5- Emphasis, which is the redundant lām, and it has kinds, among them:
a- The lām interposed between a transitive verb and its object, as in the saying of Ibn Mayyāda al-Rammāḥ praising ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān:
وملكت ما بين العراق ويثرب ... ملكا أجار لمسلم ومعاهد
(You ruled what lies between Iraq and Yathrib, a rule that gave protection to a Muslim and a covenanted person.)
That is, it protected a Muslim and a covenanted person.
b- Among them is the lām thrust in between the two terms of a genitive construct, as in the saying of Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā:
سئمت تكاليف الحياة ومن يعش ... ثمانين حولا لا أبا لك يسأم
(I am weary of life's burdens, and whoever lives eighty years, lā abā laka, grows weary.)
The original is «lā abāka mawjūd» ("your father is not to be found"), an expression that can carry praise or blame, and what follows it is put in the genitive by annexation.
c- Among them is the lām of calling for help (lām al-mustaghāth), which is redundant according to the verifiers, by the evidence that dropping it is sound.
6- Strengthening an operator that has become weak, either by being derivative in operation, like the maṣdar, the active and passive participles and the forms of intensity, as in «مصدقا لما معهم» and «فعّال لما يريد», or by being postponed after its object, as in «إن كنتم للرؤيا تعبرون», the original being «إن كنتم تعبرون الرؤيا»; when the verb was postponed and its object put before it, its operation became weak and was strengthened by the lām. Ibn Hishām in al-Mughnī made it redundant, but the sounder view is that it is not.
7- Agreement with (إلى), that is, for the end of a range, as in «كل يجري لأجل مسمى», that is, «إلى أجل مسمى».
8- The oath, which is specific to the Name of Majesty because it is a substitute for the tāʾ, as in: lillāhi lā yuʾakhkharu l-ajal ("by Allah, the appointed term is not delayed").
9- Wonder, as in lillāhi darruk, meaning "how abundant is your gift!" It is most often used in the vocative, as in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
فيا لك من ليل كأن نجومه ... بكل مغار الفتل شدت بيذبل
(O what a night! It is as if its stars were fastened to Yadhbul with every tightly twisted rope.)
10- Result, consequence or outcome, as in «فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا» and the saying of Abū l-ʿAtāhiya:
لدوا للموت وابنوا للخراب
(Bear children for death and build for ruin.)
For death is not the reason for bearing children, nor is ruin the reason for building, but their consequence and outcome became that. Al-Zamakhsharī denied it and said: "The verified view is that it is the lām of cause, and that the causality in it is figurative, not literal."
11- Posteriority, as in «أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس», already mentioned, because the time enters, and we know it, by the declining, so the prayer is not performed except after the declining, which is the sun's inclination from its zenith. From it also is the saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: «صوموا لرؤيته وأفطروا لرؤيته» ("Fast at its sighting and break the fast at its sighting"), and the saying of Mutammim ibn Nuwayra:
فلما تفرقنا كأني ومالكا ... لطول اجتماع لم نبت ليلة معا
(When we parted, it was as if Mālik and I, despite long companionship, had never spent a night together.)
12- Superiority, that is, agreement with (على) in the literal sense, as in «يخرون للأذقان», plural of dhaqn, meaning upon them; and figuratively, as in «وإن أسأتم فلها», that is, «فعليها».
13- Agreement with (في), as in «قل إنما علمها عند ربي لا يجليها لوقتها إلا هو», that is, "none discloses it in its time except Him".
14- Agreement with (عند), as in the reading of al-Ḥajūrī «بل كذبوا بالحق لما جاءهم» with kasra on the lām and lightening of the lām, that is, "at its coming to them".
15- Agreement with (مع), as in the saying of Mutammim ibn Nuwayra mentioned above: «فلما تفرقنا …» etc.
16- Agreement with (من), as in "I heard a cry from him" [«سمعت له صراخا»], and the saying of Jarīr:
لنا الفضل في الدنيا وأنفك راغم ... ونحن لكم يوم القيامة أفضل
(Ours is the excellence in this world, though your nose be in the dust, and on the Day of Resurrection we are better than you.)
That is, «ونحن منكم أفضل».
17- Conveying, as in «قل لعبادي», and its rule is that it governs the noun of the hearer of a saying.
18- Agreement with (عن) when used with speaking, as in «وقال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا لو كان خيرا ما سبقونا إليه».
19- Bestowal of possession, as in: "I gave Zayd a dinar."
20- Cause, as in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
ويوم عقرت للعذارى مطيتي ... فيا عجبا من كورها المتحمل
(And on the day I hamstrung my mount for the maidens, O what a wonder, its saddle borne and carried!)
Among them is the lām that enters in form upon the imperfect, as in «وأنزلنا إليك الذكر لتبين للناس», and the verb after it is put in the accusative by an implied (أن).
21- Emphasis of negation, which is the lām that enters in form upon a verb preceded by (ما كان) or (لم يكن), as in «وما كان الله ليطلعكم على الغيب». Most grammarians call it the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd).
22- Clarification, already mentioned, which we repeat here in detail. It is of three kinds:
a- The one that distinguishes the object from the agent. Its rule is that it occurs after a verb of wonder or an elative that convey love or hatred; you say "mā aḥabbanī" and "mā abghaḍanī". If you say «li-fulān» ("to so-and-so"), you are the agent of love and hatred and he is their object; if you say «ilā fulān», the matter is the reverse.
b and c- The one that makes clear an agency not confused with objecthood, and the one that makes clear an objecthood not confused with agency, where what accompanies each is either not known from what came before it, or is known but its clarification is resumed to strengthen and emphasise the clarification. In all this the lām is attached to an omitted element. An example of the one clarifying objecthood: saqyan li-Zayd and jadʿan lahu ("may Zayd be given to drink", "may he be maimed"). This lām is not attached to the maṣdar nor to their implied verbs, because both are transitive, nor does it strengthen an operator weak by derivation; it is a lām that clarifies the one for whom or against whom the invocation is made.
There was disagreement over His saying, the Exalted, «هيهات هيهات لما توعدون». It is said that the lām is redundant and (ما) is the agent; it is also said that the agent is a latent pronoun referring to the resurrection and the bringing forth, so that the lām is for clarification. The discussion of the lām is long, and it is referred to the longer works.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying: ﴿سُبْحَانَ ٱلَّذِي أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلاً مِّنَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ﴾ (glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque): the whole sanctuary (al-ḥaram) is a mosque, meaning Mecca and its sanctuary. ﴿إِلَىٰ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلأَقْصَى﴾ (to the Farthest Mosque): Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis). ﴿ٱلَّذِي بَارَكْنَا حَوْلَهُ﴾ (whose surroundings We have blessed): with fruits and rivers.
His saying: ﴿لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ آيَاتِنَآ﴾ (to show him some of Our signs) means the Prophet ﷺ, when He took him by night to show him wonders that night. He was shown the prophets, so that he described them to the people of Mecca. They said: "We have camels on the road to Syria; tell us about them." So he told them signs and marks. They said: "When will they arrive?" He said: "On such-and-such a day, at sunrise, led by a grey (awraq) camel." They said: "These are signs by which we shall know whether he is truthful or lying." So they went out early beyond the ʿAqaba pass to meet them. One said: "By Allah, here is the sun, it has risen, and it has not come." Another said: "By Allah, here is the caravan, led by a grey camel, just as Muhammad ﷺ said." Yet they still did not believe.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَدْعُ ٱلإِنْسَانُ﴾ (and man prays): the wāw has been dropped from it in pronunciation but not in meaning, since it is in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ); its dropping is due to its meeting the vowelless lām. Similar are ﴿سَنَدْعُ الزَّبَانِيَةَ﴾ (We will call the guards of Hell), likewise ﴿وَسَوْفَ يُؤْتِ اللّهُ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (and Allah will give the believers), His saying ﴿يَوْمَ يُنَادِ المُنَادِ﴾ (the day the caller calls), and His saying ﴿فَمَا تُغْنِ النُّذُرُ﴾ (but warnings do not avail). Had they been written with yāʾ and wāw it would have been correct. This is part of the speech of the Arabs. The poet said:
كفاك كفٌّ ما تُليق درهما * جُوداً وأخرى تُعْطِ بالسيف الدَّما
(Your two palms: one that, out of generosity, does not hold on to a dirham, and another that gives blood with the sword.)
And one of the Anṣār said:
ليس تخفى بشَارتى قَدْر يومٍ * ولقد تُخْفِ شِيمتى إعْسَارِى
(My cheerfulness is not hidden for a single day, and my character does hide my poverty.)
His saying: ﴿وَيَدْعُ ٱلإِنْسَانُ بِٱلشَّرِّ دُعَآءَهُ بِٱلْخَيْرِ﴾ (and man prays for evil as he prays for good): He means: like his praying for good, in appealing to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for something whose answering the one who prays would not like, such as his praying against his child; so he is not answered in the evil even though he prayed for it. That too is one of Allah's favours, Mighty and Majestic, upon him.

farraa:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿فَمَحَوْنَآ آيَةَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾ (and We erased the sign of the night): Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Mindal ibn ʿAlī told me, from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, from Abū Ḥarb ibn Abī al-Aswad al-Dīlī, tracing it back to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: it is the smudge that is on the moon.

farraa:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿وَكُلَّ إِنْسَانٍ أَلْزَمْنَاهُ طَآئِرَهُ﴾ (and every human being — We have fastened his omen to him): that is his deeds: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. (وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُ) (and We will bring forth for him): Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it with nūn, and others read it with yāʾ with fatḥa: (وَيَخْرُجُ لَهُ) (and there will come forth for him) — his omen; among them Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan. Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read (ويُخرِج... له كِتاباً), meaning: and He brings forth for him his deeds as a book. All of them are good.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱقْرَأْ كِتَٰبَكَ﴾ (read your book): in it — and Allah knows best — (يُقَال) ("it will be said") is suppressed. It is like His saying ﴿ويَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ أدْخِلُوا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ (and on the day the Hour arrives: "Admit the people of Pharaoh…"), and like His saying ﴿فَأَمَّا الذِينَ اسْوَدَّتْ وُجوهُهُمْ أَكَفَرْتُمْ﴾ (as for those whose faces turn black: "Did you disbelieve…?"); the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: so it will be said: "Did you disbelieve?"
His saying: ﴿كَفَىٰ بِنَفْسِكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيباً﴾ (sufficient is your own self against you this day as an accountant): in everything in the Qurʾān such as His saying ﴿وكَفَى بربّك﴾ (and sufficient is your Lord), ﴿وكفى بالله﴾ (and sufficient is Allah) and ﴿كَفَىٰ بِنَفْسِكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ﴾, if you dropped the bāʾ the word would be nominative; as the poet said:
ويخبرنى عن غائب المَرْء هَدْيُه * كفى الهَدْىُ عَمَّا غَيَّب المرءُ مُخبِرا
(A man's conduct tells me about what is hidden in him; conduct suffices as an informant about what a man conceals.)
The bāʾ may only come in on the nominative when its owner is being praised by it; do you not see that you say: كفاكَ به (it suffices you), نهاكَ به (it restrains you), أكرِم به رجلاً (how noble a man he is), بِئس به رجلا (how bad a man he is), نعم به رجلا (how excellent a man he is), طاب بطعامك طعاماً (how good your food is as food), and جَاد بثوبك ثوباً (how fine your garment is as a garment). If it were not praise or blame it could not come in; do you not see that one who says "your brother stood" (قامَ أخوكَ) or "your brother sat" (قعد أخوك) may not say قام بأخيك or قَعَد بأخيك — unless he means that someone else stood with him and sat with him.

farraa:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿أَمَرْنَا مُتْرَفِيهَا﴾ (We commanded its affluent ones): al-Aʿmash [99a] «[Translator's note: "99 ا" is a manuscript folio marker.]», ʿĀṣim and men from the people of Medina read ﴿أَمَرْنا﴾ with the light form. Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna told me, from Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj, from Mujāhid: ﴿أمَرْنا﴾ with the light form. Some explained ﴿أَمَرْنَا مُتْرَفِيهَا﴾ as (commanding them) to obedience, ﴿فَفَسَقُوا﴾ (but they transgressed), i.e. when the affluent person is commanded to obey, he turns instead to transgression. In the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: (بعثنا فيها أكابر مجرميها) (We raised up in it the chief of its criminals). Al-Ḥasan read ﴿آمَرنا﴾, and ﴿أَمِرْنا﴾ is also reported from him, but we do not know whether that was preserved from him correctly, because we do not know its meaning here. The meaning of (آمرنا), with the long vowel, is: We made (them) many. Abū al-ʿĀliya al-Riyāḥī read (أمَّرنا مُتْرَفيها) (We gave authority to its affluent ones), and that agrees with Ibn ʿAbbās's explanation, for he said: We set its chiefs in power, and they transgressed in it.

farraa:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿عَجَّلْنَا لَهُ فِيهَا مَا نَشَآءُ لِمَن نُّرِيدُ﴾ (We hasten for him in it whatever We will, for whom We intend): i.e. that is from Us, for whom We intend.

farraa:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿أَلاَّ تَتَّخِذُواْ مِن دُونِي وَكِيلاً﴾ (that you take no guardian besides Me): it is said: a lord; and it is said: one who suffices.

farraa:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿كُلاًّ نُّمِدُّ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ﴾ (each We provide, these [and those]): "We provide" (نُمدّ) is made to fall on both, i.e. We provide for all of them; i.e. We sustain the believer and the disbeliever from the bounty of your Lord.

farraa:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿ذُرِّيَّةَ مَنْ حَمَلْنَا﴾ (O descendants of those We carried) is accusative on the basis of the nidāʾ (vocative). He addressed them: "O descendants of those We carried with Noah", meaning (those) in the loins of men and the wombs of women who had not yet been created.

farraa:4-5.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَضَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ (and We decreed for the Children of Israel): We informed them that they would cause corruption twice.
His saying: ﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ أُولاهُمَا﴾ (so when the promise of the first of them came): he says: the punishment for the first of the two times, which is the first of the two corruptions. ﴿بَعَثْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ عِبَاداً لَّنَآ﴾ (We sent against you servants of Ours) means Nebuchadnezzar (Bukhtanaṣṣar), who took captives and killed.
His saying: ﴿فَجَاسُواْ خِلاَلَ ٱلدِّيَارِ﴾ (and they probed through the homes) means: they killed you among your houses. (فجاسُوا) has the meaning of "they seized"; and حاسوا, with ḥāʾ, is also used in that meaning.

farraa:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَا لَكُمُ ٱلْكَرَّةَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ (then We gave you back the turn against them) means against Nebuchadnezzar: a man came whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent against Nebuchadnezzar and killed him, and Allah restored to them their kingdom and their affairs. So they lived on, then they caused corruption, and that was the last of the two corruptions.

farraa:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ ٱلآخِرَةِ لِيَسُوءُواْ وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾ (then when the final promise came, [We sent them] to disgrace your faces): someone may ask: where is the answer (jawāb) of (إذا)? There are two aspects to it. It is said: "So when the final promise came, We sent them, so that Allah might disgrace your faces" — for whoever reads it with yāʾ. It may also be: "so that the punishment might disgrace your faces". Ubayy ibn Kaʿb [98b] «[Translator's note: "98 ب" is a manuscript folio marker.]» read it (لِنَسُوءنْ وُجُوهَكُمْ) with the light form, meaning the nūn. If you made its lām take fatḥa, it would be the answer of إذا without a suppressed verb; you say: إذا أتيتنى لأسُوءَنَّكَ (when you come to me I shall certainly grieve you). The coming in of the wāw in what follows ﴿لنسوءن﴾ would then be like His saying ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ نُرِى إبراهيمَ مَلَكُوتَ السَّمَوَاتِ والأَرض ولِيَكُونَ من﴾ (and thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that he might be among …), i.e. "We showed him the dominion (so that he might be…)"; likewise the wāw in ﴿وليَدْخُلُوا﴾ (and that they might enter): you suppress a verb for it after it. It has also been read (لِيُسوءُوا وُجُوهَكُم) — (namely) those who enter.

farraa:9-10.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ يَِهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ﴾ (indeed this Qurʾān guides to that which is most upright).
He says: to the testimony that there is no god but Allah.
﴿وَيُبَشِّرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (and gives glad tidings to the believers): the glad tidings are made to fall upon His saying ﴿أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْراً كَبِيراً﴾ (that they will have a great reward). It is also possible that the believers were given glad tidings as well by His saying ﴿وأَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ أَعْتَدْنَا لَهُمْ عَذَاباً أَلِيماً﴾ (and that those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have prepared for them a painful punishment), because speech allows you to say: "I gave ʿAbdallāh the glad tidings that he will be given and that his enemy will be denied." And it may be: "and He gives those who do not believe in the Hereafter the tidings that We have prepared for them a painful punishment", even though He did not make the tidings fall upon them as He made them fall upon the believers before (أنَّ). It would then be like your saying in speech: "I announced that rain is coming", which contains the meaning "I announced to the people that rain is coming", even though you do not mention them. If you began afresh with ﴿وإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ﴾ (with kasra), that would be sound, but I have not heard anyone read it so.

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلاَّ تَعْبُدُوۤاْ﴾ (and your Lord has decreed that you worship none [but Him]) is like your saying "your Lord has commanded". In the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is (وَأَوْصى رَبُّك) (and your Lord has enjoined), and Ibn ʿAbbās said it is (وَوَصَّى), its wāw having become joined (to the ṣād). The Arabs say: "I left him deciding (يقضى) people's affairs", i.e. giving orders in them, and his order is carried out.
His saying ﴿وَبِٱلْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَاناً﴾ (and to parents, good treatment): its meaning is: and He enjoined good treatment of parents. The Arabs say: أُوصيك به خيراً (I enjoin you to do him good) and آمرك به خيراً (I command you to do him good). Its meaning was: I command you to do (good) to him; then you drop (أنْ) and attach "good" (الخير) directly to the enjoining and to the commanding. The poet said:
عجبتُ من دَهْماء إذ تشكُونَا * ومن أبى دَهماء إذ يوصينَا * خيراً بها كأننا جافونا *
(I marvelled at Dahmāʾ when she complained about us, and at Dahmāʾ's father when he enjoined us to treat her well, as though we were treating her harshly.)
His saying: ﴿إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلْكِبَرَ﴾ (if they reach old age with you): it is put in the dual because the two parents were mentioned before it, so the verb came to match their number; «[Translator's note: the remark about the dual refers to the reading يَبْلُغانِّ, although the text here quotes the verse as يَبْلُغَنَّ.]» then He said ﴿أَحَدُهُمَا أَوْ كِلاَهُمَا﴾ (one of them or both of them) as a fresh start (iʾtināf), like His saying ﴿ثمَّ عموا وصَمُّوا﴾ (then they became blind and deaf), after which He began afresh and said ﴿كَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ﴾ (many of them); and likewise His saying ﴿لاَهِيَةً قُلُوبُهُمْ وأسَرُّوا النَّجْوى﴾ (their hearts distracted, and they conferred in secret), after which He began afresh and said ﴿الذين ظَلَمُوا﴾ (those who did wrong). Many people read it ﴿إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلْكِبَرَ﴾, making ﴿يَبْلُغَنّ﴾ a verb belonging to "one of them", so you repeated «both of them» on it. «[Translator's note: the text has "فَكرَّرت ب فكرت", i.e. an editorial variant: manuscript B reads فكرت.]»
His saying ﴿فَلاَ تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفٍّ﴾ (then do not say to them "uff"): ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd and al-Aʿmash read it (أُفِّ), with the genitive vowel (khafḍ) and without nunation. The generality read (أُفٍّ). Those who gave it kasra with nunation took the view that it is a sound whose meaning is known only by uttering it, so they gave it kasra as sounds are given kasra. Among that is the Arabs' saying: "I heard ṭāqin ṭāqin" for the sound of striking, and they say: "I heard tighin tighin" for the sound of laughter. Those who did not nunate but gave it kasra said: أفّ has three letters, while most sounds have only two letters, like صَهْ, يَغْ and مَهْ; that is the kind which takes kasra and nunation, because its first letter is vowelled. We are not compelled to give a vowel to the second letter of particles (adawāt) and the like, so that it would take kasra with nūn; and أفَّ was likened to your saying مُدَّ and رُدَّ, since it consists of three letters. What indicates this is that some Arabs have given it ḍamma, saying: أفُّ لك. Similar is the saying of the rajaz poet:
سألتُها الوصلَ فقالت مِضَّ * وحَرَّكت لى رأسهَا بالنَغْض
(I asked her for union and she said "miḍḍ!", and shook her head at me in refusal.)
— like a speaker saying (لا) (no) with his molars. And it is said: "Your family taught you nothing but (مضِّ and مِضُّ)", and some of them: "nothing but مِضّا", making the verb fall on it. Some Arabs have said: "Do not say to him أُفّا or تُفّا", treating it like a noun, so it takes the genitive, the nominative [and the accusative] «[Translator's note: the text adds "ثبت فى ب", i.e. the bracketed word is found in manuscript B.]»; and the accusative without nūn is permitted, as they said رُدَّ. The Arabs say: "he began to say 'uff' (يتأفّف) at a smell he found", meaning he says: أفِّ أفِّ. The poet said, concerning what is nunated:
وقفنا فقلنا إِيهِ عن أمّ سالمٍ * وَمَا بالُ تكليم الديار البلاقع
(We halted and said: "Tell on about Umm Sālim!" — but what use is speaking to empty abodes?)
He dropped the nūn because it is like a particle; when it has three letters it is likened to their saying: جَيْرِ لا أفعل ذلك (indeed, I will not do that). The poet said:
فقُلْن عَلَى الفِردوس أوَّلُ مشرب * أَجَلْ جَيْرِ إِن كَانت أُبيحت دَعَاثرُهْ
(They said: "At al-Firdaws is the first watering-place." — Yes, indeed, if its old cisterns have been made free to use.)

farraa:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ﴾ (and lower to them the wing of humility): the generality read it with ḍamma. Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Hushaym told me, from Abū Bishr Jaʿfar ibn Iyās, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, that he read (وَاخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاح الذِّلّ) with kasra. He said: al-Farrāʾ told us: al-Ḥakam ibn Ẓuhayr told me, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, that he read it (الذِّلّ) with kasra. Abū Zakariyyā «[Translator's note: i.e. al-Farrāʾ himself.]» said: I asked Abū Bakr about it and he said: ʿĀṣim read it with ḍamma. الذُلّ (dhull), from الذلّة, is to humble oneself while not being lowly by nature. الذِّلَّة and الذُّلّ are the maṣdar (verbal noun) of الذليل (the lowly), and الذِّلّ (dhill) is the maṣdar of الذلول (the tractable), as with a riding animal and the ground. You say: a tractable camel (جَمَلٌ ذَلُول), a tractable riding animal, and tractable ground, clearly showing الذِّلّ.

farraa:28-28.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ ٱبْتِغَآءَ رَحْمَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾ (and if you turn away from them, awaiting mercy from your Lord): he says: when your relatives or other needy people come to you asking, and you turn away because you have nothing to give them, then say to them a gentle word (قولا ميْسُوراً), he says: make them a good promise. Then He forbade him to give away all he has, so that he would not be left مَحْسوراً (exhausted), with nothing left. The Arabs say of a camel: "it is محسور" when its going has given out; and "I exhausted (حَسرت) the riding animal" when you rode it until its going gave out. And His saying: ﴿يَنْقَلِبْ إليْكَ البَصَرُ خَاسِئاً وهو حَسِيرٌ﴾ (your sight will return to you humbled and fatigued): it becomes fatigued at the farthest reach of the view.

farraa:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿خِطْئاً كَبِيراً﴾ (a great sin): al-Ḥasan read خَطَاءً كبيراً, with the long vowel. Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read ﴿خَطَأْ كَبيراً﴾, short and with hamza. All are correct. It seems that الخِطْأ is sin; it may also have the meaning of خَطَأ (with the short vowel), as they said قِتْب and قَتَب (saddle), حِذُرٌ and حَذَرٌ (caution), نِجْسٌ and نَجَسٌ (impure). Similar is the reading of whoever read ﴿هُمْ أُولاَءَ عَلَى أَثَرِى﴾ (they are close upon my track) and ﴿إِثْرِى﴾.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن قُتِلَ مَظْلُوماً فَقَدْ جَعَلْنَا لِوَلِيِّهِ سُلْطَاناً﴾ (and whoever is killed unjustly, We have given his heir authority): in retaliation or in accepting blood-money. Then He said: ﴿فَلاَ يُسْرِف فِّي ٱلْقَتْلِ﴾ (but let him not exceed limits in killing): it has been read with tāʾ and with yāʾ. Whoever read it with yāʾ referred it to the heir, i.e. he must not kill anyone other than the killer; He says: so let the heir not exceed limits in killing. He said: al-Farrāʾ «[Translator's note: the text has "القراء"; evidently al-Farrāʾ is meant.]» told us: more than one person told me — among them Mindal, Jarīr and Qays — from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm, from Abū Maʿmar, from Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Yamān, that he read ﴿فَلاَ تُسْرِف﴾ with tāʾ. In the reading of Ubayy: (فلاَ يُسْرِفوا فىِ القتل) (so let them not exceed limits in killing).
His saying ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ مَنْصُوراً﴾ (indeed he has been supported): it is said: his heir has been supported. It is also said that the hāʾ (the pronoun) refers to the blood: the blood of the slain has been supported because he was wronged. The hāʾ may also refer to the slain person himself, or to the killing, since it is an act and so runs the same course as the blood. And Allah knows best which of that is right.

farraa:34-34.t: His saying: ﴿حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُ﴾ (until he reaches his maturity): Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Ḥibbān ibn ʿAlī told me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: الأشُدّ is between eighteen and thirty.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْفُ﴾ (and do not pursue): most readers take it from قفوت, the fāʾ being vowelled toward the wāw, so you say ﴿وَلاَ تَقْفُ﴾. Some said (وَلاَ تَقَفْ). The Arabs say قُفْت أثره and قَفَوته (I followed his track). Similar are يَعْتام and يَعْتمى (he chooses); قاع الجملُ الناقةَ قوعاً «[Translator's note: the text has "وقعا".]» when it mounts her; and عاث and عَثَى (of causing corruption). This is frequent; among it are شاكُ السلاح and شاكى السلاح (bristling with weapons), and جُرف هارٌ and هارٍ (a crumbling bank). I heard some of Quḍāʿa say: اجتحى ماله (he swept away his wealth), while the widespread usage is اجتاح ماله. The poet said:
ولو أنى رأيتك من بعيد * لعاقكَ من دعاء النِّيب عَاقى
(Had I seen you from afar, something hindering would have kept you from calling to the old she-camels.)
He means: عائق (a hindrance).
حَسِبت بُغَام راحلتى عَنَاقاً * وما هى وَيْبَ غَيرِكَ بالعَنَاق
(You took the moan of my riding camel for a young she-goat — woe to someone other than you — it is no young she-goat.)

farraa:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿كُلُّ ذٰلِكَ كَانَ سَيِّئُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ مَكْرُوهاً﴾ (all that — its evil is ever hateful with your Lord): some of the people of the Ḥijāz read (كَانَ سَيِّئةً عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ مَكْرُوهاً) (was an evil, hateful with your Lord).

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتُ ٱلسَّبْعُ﴾ (the seven heavens glorify Him): most readers have tāʾ. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is (سَبَّحتْ له السموات السبع) (the seven heavens glorified Him), and this strengthens those who read with tāʾ. Had it been read with yāʾ it would have been correct, just as they read ﴿تَكَادُ السَّمَوَاتْ﴾ (the heavens almost …) and ﴿يَكُاد﴾.
The yāʾ is good only because it is a small number; when the number of feminines or masculines is small, yāʾ is better in it than tāʾ. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said of a small feminine number: ﴿وَقَالَ نِسْوَةٌ فِى المَدِيِنَةِ﴾ (and women in the city said), and He said of the masculine: ﴿فإذا انْسَلَخَ الأشْهُرُ الحُرُمُ﴾ (and when the sacred months have passed), using the masculine. That is because the beginning of the verb of a feminine (subject), when it is few, is with yāʾ, so one says: النسوة يقمن (the women stand) [100b] «[Translator's note: "100 ب" is a manuscript folio marker.]». When the verb comes first, the nūn drops from its end because the noun is overt, and the verb keeps its beginning on yāʾ. Whoever uses the feminine takes the view that (هذه) (this, feminine) applies to the plural, so he uses the feminine on account of the femininity of (هذه); and the masculine is like the feminine in this: do you not see that you say: هذه الرجال (these men) and هذه النساء (these women)? Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ told me, from ʿAmmār al-Duhnī, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: every tasbīḥ (glorification) in the Qurʾān is prayer, and every sulṭān (authority) is proof; this is on account of «[Translator's note: so the text (هذا لقوله); the connection to what precedes is unclear, and some editions may read it as an exception.]» His saying ﴿وَإِن مِّن شَيْءٍ إِلاَّ يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ﴾ (and there is nothing but glorifies Him with praise).
His saying: ﴿عِظَاماً وَرُفَاتاً﴾ (bones and crumbled particles): الرُّفَات is dust; it has no singular, like الدُقَاق (fine fragments) and الحُطَام (debris).

farraa:51-51.t:
His saying: ﴿أَوْ خَلْقاً مِّمَّا يَكْبُرُ فِي صُدُورِكُمْ﴾ (or some creation of what is great in your breasts): they said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Tell us, if we were death itself, who would make us die?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿أَوْ خَلْقاً مِّمَّا يَكْبُرُ فِي صُدُورِكُمْ﴾, meaning death itself, i.e. Allah would send against you one who would make you die. «[Translator's note: the text has "فأنز", evidently فأنزل.]»
His saying ﴿فَسَيُنْغِضُونَ إِلَيْكَ رُؤُوسَهُمْ﴾ (then they will shake their heads at you): one says أَنغض رأسَه, i.e. he moved it upwards and downwards. Abū Zakariyyā showed us that: he gestured with his head, pressing it against his throat and then raising it as though looking at the ceiling. The head يَنْغَض and يَنْغِض (shakes). When a front tooth moves, it is said: نَغَضت سِنّه (his tooth became loose). The male ostrich is called نَغْض only because, when it hurries its walk, it rises and falls.
His saying: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هُوَ﴾ (and they say: "When is it?") means the resurrection.

farraa:54-54.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَكِيلاً﴾ (and We have not sent you over them as a guardian): he says: a keeper and a lord.

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿زَبُوراً﴾ (the Psalms): al-Farrāʾ said: Abū Bakr told me: ʿĀṣim used to read ﴿زَبُوراً﴾ with fatḥa throughout the Qurʾān, and Ḥamza read it with ḍamma.

farraa:57-57.t: His saying: ﴿أُولَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ يَبْتَغُونَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمُ ٱلْوَسِيلَةَ﴾ (those whom they invoke seek a means of access to their Lord) means the jinn whom Khuzāʿa used to worship. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿أُولَـٰئِكَ﴾, meaning the jinn whom (they invoke) seek (access) to Allah. Thus ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾ is a verb belonging to those who worship them, and ﴿يَبْتَغُونَ﴾ is a verb belonging to the jinn, by which they (أولئك) are made nominative.

farraa:58-58.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ إِلاَّ نَحْنُ مُهْلِكُوهَا﴾ (and there is no town but We shall destroy it): by death; ﴿أَوْ مُعَذِّبُوهَا عَذَاباً شَدِيداً﴾ (or punish it with a severe punishment): by the sword.

farraa:59-59.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا مَنَعَنَآ أَن نُّرْسِلَ بِٱلآيَاتِ﴾ (and nothing prevented Us from sending the signs): (أنْ) is in the position of the accusative. ﴿إِلاَّ أَن كَذَّبَ﴾ (except that [the former peoples] denied them): أنْ is in the position of the nominative; just as you say: ما منعهم الإيمانَ إلاّ تكذيبُهم (nothing kept them from faith except their denial).
His saying ﴿ٱلنَّاقَةَ مُبْصِرَةً﴾ (the she-camel as a visible sign): He made the verb (i.e. the participle) belong to her. Whoever read (مَبْصَرة) meant something like the saying of ʿAntara:
* والكفر مَخْبَثَة لنفس المنعم *
(And ingratitude is a cause of corruption to the soul of the benefactor.)
When you put mafʿala in the sense of an active participle, it does away with the plural and the feminine, so it is singular with fatḥa on its ʿayn, and kasra there is not permitted. The Arabs say: هَذا عُشْب مَلْبَنَة مَسْمنة (this is herbage that makes milk plentiful and makes fat), and: the child is مَبْخلة مَجْبنة (a cause of stinginess and cowardice). Whatever of this comes to you, produce it in this form. If it is from (a root with) yāʾ or wāw, make them overt; you say: هذا شراب مَبْوَلة (this is a drink that causes urination), هذا كلام مَهْيَبة للرجال (this is speech that makes men stand in awe), ومَتْيَهة (and a cause of going astray), and the like. The meaning of (مُبصِرة) is "giving light", as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿وَالنَّهَارَمُبْصِراً﴾ (and the day giving sight): giving light.

farraa:60-60.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ أَحَاطَ بِٱلنَّاسِ﴾ (indeed your Lord has encompassed the people) means the people of Mecca, i.e. that He will grant you victory (over them). ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا ٱلرُّؤيَا ٱلَّتِي أَرَيْنَاكَ إِلاَّ فِتْنَةً﴾ (and We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial): He means: what We showed you on the night of the Night Journey was only a trial for them, so that some of them said: "a sorcerer", "a soothsayer", and they said much (of that). ﴿وَٱلشَّجَرَةَ ٱلْمَلْعُونَةَ﴾ (and the accursed tree) is the tree of Zaqqūm; you make it accusative by جعلنا (We made). Were it made nominative, following the noun implied in "trial" from "the vision", it would be correct. Similar in ordinary speech: جَعلتك عَامِلاً وزيداً (I made you, and Zayd, an agent) and وزيدٌ.

farraa:62-62.t: His saying: ﴿لأَحْتَنِكَنَّ ذُرِّيَّتَهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾ (I will surely bridle his descendants, except a few): he says: I will surely gain mastery over them, ﴿إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾ (except a few), meaning those who are protected (from sin).

farraa:64-64.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱسْتَفْزِزْ﴾ (and incite): he says: make light of (them) (بِصَوْتِكَ) (with your voice): with your calling. ﴿وَأَجْلِبْ عَلَيْهِم بِخَيْلِكَ وَرَجِلِكَ﴾ (and assault them with your cavalry and your infantry) means the cavalry and the foot-soldiers of the idolaters.
His saying ﴿وَشَارِكْهُمْ فِي ٱلأَمْوَالِ وَٱلأَوْلادِ﴾ (and be a partner with them in wealth and children): every wealth mixed with what is unlawful is his share. His saying ﴿وَعِدْهُمْ﴾ (and make promises to them): i.e. tell them: there is no Paradise and no Fire. Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ إِلاَّ غُرُوراً﴾ (and Satan promises them nothing but delusion).

farraa:69-69.t: His saying: ﴿لاَ تَجِدُواْ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا بِهِ تَبِيعاً﴾ (you would find for yourselves no avenger against Us therein): it is said: an avenger and a claimant. تَبِيع is in the sense of تابع (one who follows up).

farraa:71-71.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ نَدْعُواْ كُلَّ أُنَاسٍ بِإِمَامِهِمْ﴾ (the day We will call every people by their leader): the generality read it with nūn; and (يَدْعُو) (He will call) also, referring to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Hushaym asked me: "Is (يَوْمَ يُدْعَواْ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ) permissible?" — they had transmitted it from al-Ḥasan. I told him I did not know it. He said: "I asked the experts in Arabic about it, and they did not know it."

farraa:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن كَانَ فِي هَـٰذِهِ أَعْمَىٰ﴾ (and whoever is blind in this) means: in the blessings of this world which We have recounted to you; ﴿فَهُوَ فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾ (then he in the Hereafter) — in the blessings of the Hereafter — ﴿أَعْمَىٰ وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلاً﴾ (will be more blind and further astray from the way).
When the Arabs say "he is more X than you" (أفعل منك), they say it of every fāʿil and faʿīl (pattern), and of whatever verb has nothing added beyond three letters. When it is of the faʿlaltu pattern, like زخرفت (I adorned), or of the ifʿalaltu pattern, like احمررت (I became red) and اصفررت (I became yellow), they do not say "he is more X than you" (أفعل منك); they only say: "he is more intensely red than you" (أشدّ حمرةً منكَ) and "more intensely adorned than you". It was permitted with blindness here only because He did not mean blindness of the eye; He meant — and Allah knows best — blindness of the heart. So one says: "so-and-so is blinder than so-and-so in heart", and (do not say): "he is blinder than him in the eye". That is because, since it (the eye sense) comes on the pattern of أحمر/حمراء (red, masc./fem.), أفعل منك is left out of it, as it is left out of most of that kind. You may find some grammarians saying: "I permit it with الأعمى (blind), الأعشى (night-blind), الأعرج (lame) and الأزرق (blue-eyed), because we say عمِى, زرِق, عرِج and عَشِى, but we do not say صَفِر, حمِر or بَيِض." That is worth nothing. One looks in this only at that in which its owner has some action, slight or great, so that أفعل indicates the smallness or greatness of the thing; do you not see that you may say: "so-and-so is more upright (أقْوَم) than so-and-so" and "more handsome", because this one's uprightness and beauty may exceed the other's uprightness and beauty; but you do not say of two blind men: "this one is blinder than that one", nor of two dead men: "this one is deader than that one". If something of this comes to you in poetry and you allow it, both kinds can bear being allowed. Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: an elder from the people of Basra told me that he heard the Arabs say: ما أسود شَعره (how black his hair is!). Al-Farrāʾ was asked about the elder and said: that is Bashshār al-Nāqiṭ. And the poet said:
أمَّا الملوكُ فأنت اليَوْمَ ألأَمُهم * لُؤماً وَأبيضُهم سِرْبالَ طبَّاخ
(As for kings, you are today the most base of them in baseness, and the whitest of them in a cook's shirt — i.e. your cook never uses it, out of stinginess.)
Whoever says this is bound to say: الله أبْيَضك (Allah made you white), والله أسْوَدك, and ما أسْوَدَك (how black you are!). There is a game of the Arabs in which they say: أَبِيضى حالا and أَسِيدى حالا. The Arabs say مُسْوِدة and مُبْيِضة (of a woman) when she gives birth to black and to white children; and mostly they say مُوضحة when she gives birth to white children, and they may say مُسِيدة. [101b] «[Translator's note: "101 ب" is a manuscript folio marker.]»

farraa:76-76.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِن كَادُواْ لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ مِنَ ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ (and indeed they were about to unsettle you from the land): when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Medina, the Jews envied him and his presence weighed on them. So they said: "You surely know that this land is not the land of the prophets; their land is only Syria. If you are a prophet, go out to it, for Allah will grant you victory." He said: so the Prophet ﷺ encamped some miles from Medina, and Allah revealed: ﴿وَإِن كَادُواْ لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ﴾ — to make light of you — «[Translator's note: the text here repeats "وَإِذاً لاَيَلْبَثُونَ" before continuing the verse.]» ﴿مِنَ ٱلأَرْضِ لِيُخْرِجوكَ مِنْهَا وَإِذاً لاَّ يَلْبَثُونَ خِلافَكَ إلاَّ قَليلاً﴾ (from the land, to expel you from it; and then they would not have remained after you except a little). He says: had you gone out while they did not believe, the punishment would have come down upon them.

farraa:77-77.t: His saying: ﴿سُنَّةَ مَن قَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ﴾ ([this is] the way of those We sent before you): "the way" (السنّة) is accusative on the basis of the suppressed (verb of) punishment, i.e. they will be punished according to the way of those We had sent; ﴿وَلاَ تَجِدُ لِسُنَّتِنَا تَحْوِيلاً﴾ (and you will not find in Our way any alteration).

farraa:78-78.t:
His saying: ﴿أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلاَةَ لِدُلُوكِ ٱلشَّمْسِ إِلَىٰ غَسَقِ ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾ (establish prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night): it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: it is its declining and its passing the meridian, for the noon prayer. Abū Zakariyyā said: I have seen the Arabs take الدلوك to mean the setting of the sun. One of them recited to me:
هذا مَقَام قدَمَىْ رَبَاحِ * ذبَّبَ حتى دَلكَتْ بِرَاحِ
(This is where the two feet of Rabāḥ stood: he kept (people) off until the sun set — "bi-rāḥ".)
He means the water-drawer; ذبَّب: he drove the people away. بِرَاح: he says: until he put his palm (al-rāḥa) over his eye to see whether it had set. He said: that is how they explained it.
His saying ﴿إِلَىٰ غَسَقِ ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾: the beginning of its darkness, for the sunset and evening prayers.
His saying ﴿وَقُرْآنَ ٱلْفَجْرِ﴾ (and the recitation at dawn): i.e. and establish the dawn recitation. ﴿إِنَّ قُرْآنَ ٱلْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُوداً﴾ (indeed the dawn recitation is ever witnessed) means the dawn prayer, which the angels of the night and the angels of the day attend.

farraa:79-79.t: His saying: ﴿نَافِلَةً لَّكَ﴾ (as an additional [prayer] for you): there is no nāfila (supererogatory act) for anyone except the Prophet ﷺ, because there is no one who does not fear for himself, whereas the Prophet ﷺ has been forgiven his past and future sins, so his (extra) deeds are a nāfila.

farraa:80-80.t: His saying: ﴿وَقُل رَّبِّ أَدْخِلْنِي مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ﴾ (and say: "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance"): He said it to him on the way back, when he returned from his camp to Medina, at the time he intended (to go to) Syria. ﴿وَأَخْرِجْنِي مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ﴾ (and cause me to exit a sound exit): to Mecca.

farraa:83-83.t: His saying: ﴿كَانَ يَئُوساً﴾ (he is despairing): if you drop the hamza of His saying ﴿يؤوساً﴾, the Arabs say يَوْساً and يَوْوْساً, combining two vowelless letters. Likewise ﴿وَلاَ يَؤودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا﴾ (and their preservation does not tire Him), and likewise ﴿بِعَذَابٍ بَئِيسٍ﴾ (with a wretched punishment): one says بَيْسِ and (بَيْيْسٍ), and (ويؤوده), combining two vowelless letters. This is the speech of the Arabs. The readers, however, say (يَوُوساً) and (يَوُوده), moving the wāw toward ḍamma, and (بَيِيْسٍ), moving the first yāʾ toward kasra. We have not found that in their speech, because vowelling the yāʾ and the wāw is heavier than dropping the hamza, and they would not go from something heavy to something heavier still.

farraa:84-84.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلَىٰ شَاكِلَتِهِ﴾ (say: each works according to his manner): (شاكلته is) his direction, and it is the way and the disposition (الجديلة). I heard some Arabs of Quḍāʿa say: "ʿAbd al-Malik at that time was on his course (جديلته), and Ibn al-Zubayr on his course." The Arabs say: "so-and-so is on a good way (طريقة)", "a good خَيْدَبة", and "سُرْجُوجة"; and ʿUkl say: سِرْجِيجة.

farraa:85-85.t: His saying: ﴿قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي﴾ (say: the spirit is of the affair of my Lord): he says: of the knowledge of my Lord, not of your knowledge.

farraa:87-87.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾ (except as a mercy from your Lord) is an istithnāʾ (exception), like His saying ﴿إلاَّ حَاجَةً فىِ نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ قَضَاهَا﴾ (except a need in Jacob's soul which he satisfied).

farraa:88-88.t:
His saying: ﴿عَلَىٰ أَن يَأْتُواْ بِمِثْلِ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنِ لاَ يَأْتُونَ﴾ (to produce the like of this Qurʾān, they could not produce): (لا يأتون) is the answer to His saying ﴿لئِن﴾ (if). When the Arabs answer (لئِن) with (لا), they make what comes after لا nominative, because (لئِن) is like an oath, and the answer of an oath with (لا) is nominative. Sometimes a poet uses the jussive, because (لئن) is the conditional إن with a lām added to it, so the verb in it is directed to (the past form) فَعَل; were the يفعل (imperfect) form brought, its being jussive would be permitted. Some poets used the jussive with لئِن, and some with the لا that is its answer. Al-Aʿshā said:
لئن منُيتَ بنا عن غِبّ معركَة * لا تُلْفِنا من دماء القوم نَنتفل
(If you meet us after a battle, you will not find us disowning the blood of the enemy.)
[102a] «[Translator's note: "102 ا" is a manuscript folio marker.]» An eloquent woman of ʿUqayl recited to me:
لئن كان ما حُدّثته اليومَ صَادقاً * أصُمْ فى نهارِ القيظ للشمس باديَا
وأَركبْ حماراً بين سرج وفَرْوَة * وأُعْرِ من الخاتام صُغْرى شماليا
(If what I was told today is true, I will fast on a summer day exposed to the sun, ride a donkey between a saddle and a fur, and strip the little finger of my left hand of its ring.)
He said: and al-Kisāʾī recited to me, by al-Kumayt ibn Maʿrūf:
لئِن تَكُ قد ضاقت عليكم بيوتُكم * لَيَعلمُ ربّى أنّ بيتىَ واسع
(If your houses have become too narrow for you, my Lord surely knows that my house is wide.)
And His saying ﴿لِبَعْضٍ ظَهِيراً﴾ (assistants to one another): الظهير is a helper.

farraa:90-90.t:
His saying: ﴿مِنَ ٱلأَرْضِ يَنْبُوعاً﴾ (a spring from the ground).
(It is) that which gushes (يَنْبَع); one also says يَنْبُعُ — two dialect forms. (تَفْجُر) (you cause to gush): Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and the companions of ʿAbdallāh read it with the light form; it is as though الفَجْر is a single time, while (تُفَجِّر) is as though the gushing is from several places. It is like فَتَحت الأبواب (I opened the doors) and فتَّحتها (I opened them, one after another).

farraa:92-92.t:
His saying: ﴿كَمَا زَعَمْتَ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفاً﴾ (as you have claimed, upon us in fragments).
And (كِسْفاً): الكِسَف (is) the collective. «[Translator's note: the text has "الجِمَاع".]» He said: I heard a Bedouin say to a cloth-merchant while we were on the road to Mecca: "Give me a كِسْفة", i.e. a piece. الكِسْف is a maṣdar (verbal noun). And الكِسْف may be the plural of كِسْفة, and كِسْف (as a singular).
His saying ﴿أَوْ تَأْتِيَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةِ قَبِيلاً﴾ (or you bring Allah and the angels before [us]): i.e. as a guarantor.

farraa:93-93.t: His saying: ﴿أَوْ تَرْقَىٰ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾ (or you ascend in the sky): the meaning is: to the sky. But what makes it permissible is that they said: "or you set up a ladder and climb on it to the sky", so (فى) (in) refers to the ladder.

farraa:94-94.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا مَنَعَ ٱلنَّاسَ أَن يُؤْمِنُوۤاْ﴾ (and nothing prevented the people from believing): أن is in the position of the accusative. ﴿إِلاَّ أَن قَالُوۤاْ﴾ (except that they said): (أن) is in the position of the nominative.
﴿أَوْيكُوَن لَكَ بَيْتٌ مِنْ زُخْرُفٍ﴾ (or you have a house of zukhruf): Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Ḥibbān told me, from al-Kalbī, who said: الزخرُف is gold.

farraa:102-102.t:
His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَآ أَنزَلَ﴾ (you have certainly known that none has sent down [these]): Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd read it (عَلِمْتَ), with fatḥa on the tāʾ. Muḥammad «[Translator's note: the text has "محد".]» told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Hushaym told me, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: (لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ), likewise with fatḥa on the tāʾ. Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Qays and Abū al-Aḥwaṣ both told me, from Abū Isḥāq, from an elder of Murād, from ʿAlī, that he said: "By Allah, the enemy of Allah did not know; only Moses knew." He used to read (علِمتُ) (I have known), with ḍamma on the tāʾ. Al-Kalbī, with his chain of transmission, explained it according to ʿAlī's reading and explanation. As for Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd, they said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said ﴿وَجَحَدُوا بِهَا وَاسْتَيْقَنَتْهَا أنْفُسُهُم﴾ (and they rejected them, though their souls were convinced of them). Al-Farrāʾ said: the fatḥa is dearer to me. Someone said: al-Kisāʾī read with ḍamma; and he said: "I disagree with him most strongly."
His saying: ﴿يٰفِرْعَونُ مَثْبُوراً﴾ (O Pharaoh, … doomed): barred from good. The Arabs say: ما ثَبَرك عن ذَا, i.e. what kept you from this and turned you away from it?

farraa:104-104.t: His saying: ﴿جِئْنَا بِكُمْ لَفِيفاً﴾ (We will bring you all together): from here and there and every side.

farraa:106-106.t: His saying: ﴿وَقُرْآناً فَرَقْنَاهُ﴾ (and a Qurʾān which We have divided): you make "Qurʾān" accusative by أرسلناك (We sent you), i.e. We sent you only as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, and (with) a Qurʾān as well, just as you would say: "and as a mercy", since the Qurʾān is a mercy. Its accusative may also be by فرقناه, on the basis of the pronoun that refers back to it; since the wāw comes before it, it was made accusative. Similar is ﴿وفَرِيقاً حَقَّ عَليهِمُ الضلالةُ﴾ (and a party — upon them error was deserved). As for (فرقناه) with the light form, the companions of ʿAbdallāh read it so. The meaning is: We made it firm and set it out in detail; as He said ﴿فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ﴾ (in it every wise matter is made distinct), i.e. set out in detail. It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: (فَرَّقناه), he says: it was not sent down in one day or two days. Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: al-Ḥakam ibn Ẓuhayr told me, from al-Suddī, from Abū Mālik, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَقُرْآناً فَرَقْنَاهُ﴾ with the light form.

farraa:110-110.t: His saying: ﴿أَيّاً مَّا تَدْعُواْ﴾ (whichever you call upon): (ما) may be a ṣila (i.e. redundant), as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿عَمَّا قَلِيلٍ ليُصْبِحُنَّ نَادِمِين﴾ (after a little while they will surely become regretful); and it may be in the sense of أىّ, repeated because their wording differs. His saying: ﴿وَٱبْتَغِ بَيْنَ ذٰلِكَ سَبِيلاً﴾ (and seek between that a way): i.e. a middle course.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «سبحان الذي»: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq), and the relative noun is muḍāf ilayhi. The genitive maṣdar (verbal noun) «لنريه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أسرى», and the clause «نريه» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative [أن]. «هو» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ, and the clause «إنه هو السميع» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «وآتينا» is conjoined to the preceding clause of glorification. «هدى» is a second object, and the preposition «لبني» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «هدى». The maṣdar (verbal noun) «ألا تتخذوا» is accusative by removal of the preposition: the lām. The preposition «من دوني» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «وكيلا».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «ذرية»: the postponed first object of {تَتَّخِذُوا}; «مَن» is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi. {وَكِيلا} is then among the words that occur singular in form while what is meant by them is plural, i.e.: do not take the offspring of those We carried with Noah as guardians (wukalāʾ). The clause «إنه كان عبدا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: (إلى بني إسرائيل في الكتاب) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The two prepositional phrases are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قضينا», and «قضى» is made to contain the sense of أوحى (to reveal). His words «لتفسدن»: the lām occurs in the apodosis of the oath; an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of like letters; the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil (agent); and the nūn is for emphasis. «مرتين» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). His words «ولتعلُنَّ» are like «لتفسدن».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The conditional clause is conjoined to the preceding apodosis of the oath. The preposition «لنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «عبادا»; «أُولي» is a naʿt of «عبادا»; and the clause «وكان وعدا مفعولا» is parenthetical between the two conjoined elements.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The preposition «عليهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الكرَّة»; «أكثر» is a second object; «نفيرا» is a tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: His words «فلها»: the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and the prepositional phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: فإساءتكم لها (then your evil-doing is against it). The second conditional clause is conjoined to the first. The lām in «ليسوءوا» is causal, and the genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to the omitted apodosis of «إذا», its implied form being: بعثنا عليكم عبادًا (We sent against you servants). The kāf in «كما» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and «ما» is maṣdariyya, i.e.: an entering like their entering. His words «ما عَلوا»: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e.: to destroy that which they overcame.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يرحمكم» is the khabar (predicate) of «عسى». The conditional clause is conjoined to the resumptive «عسى ربكم». «حصيرا» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «هي أقوم» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن لهم أجرا» is accusative by removal of the preposition, the bāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: (وأن الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is conjoined to the preceding maṣdar. The clause «أعتدنا» is the khabar (predicate) of أن.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The wāw was dropped from «يدعو» in the script, in keeping with its dropping in pronunciation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. «دعاءه» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the preposition «بالخير» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) (دعاءه). The clause «وكان الإنسان عجولا» is conjoined to the clause «ويدعو الإنسان».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «آيتين» is a second object, and so is «مبصرة». The maṣdar (verbal noun) «لتبتغوا» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جعلنا»; the preposition «من ربكم» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «فضلا». His words «وكل شيء»: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by what follows, and the clause «فصَّلْناه» is explicative.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: His words «وكل»: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by what follows. The preposition «في عنقه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «طائره». The implied clause «ألزمنا» is conjoined to the clause «فصَّلنا», and the clause «ألزمناه» is explicative. The clause «يلقاه» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كتابا». The clause «نُخْرِج» is conjoined to the clause «ألزمنا كل».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: «كفى بنفسك»: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida). «اليوم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كفى».
