5- They are formed from the non-triliteral on the pattern of the passive participle, such as: مدخل ومخرج ومنطلق ومستودع, as we have observed in the verse under discussion.
Remark: so the form of time, place, the mīm-maṣdar and the passive participle from the non-triliteral is on a single pattern, and likewise in some triliteral patterns; they are distinguished by context (qarīna).
6- A noun of place is frequently formed from the non-derived (jāmid) noun on «مفعلة», to indicate the abundance of a thing in a place, as in «مأسدة», «مسبعة» and «مقثأة», for the spot where lions, beasts of prey or cucumbers abound. Despite its frequent occurrence it is not regular (qiyāsī); rather most of it is aurally transmitted (samāʿī).
Remark: as we have seen, a tāʾ marbūṭa may attach to the nouns of time and place, as in مقبرة, مطبعة and مدرسة. All of that is aurally transmitted, not a basis for analogy.
2- If we open Mughnī al-Labīb we find that the genitive-governing «اللام» has twenty-two meanings; we mention them to you without illustration, to avoid lengthiness:
ownership, quasi-ownership, transitivization (taʿdiya), giving the reason, emphasis — which is the intrusive and inserted one — and the lām of the one whose help is sought (al-mustaghāth); then strengthening the governor, and agreement with إلى; the lām of oath, the lām of wonder, the lām of outcome (ṣayrūra) and transitivization, superiority (istiʿlāʾ), agreement with في, agreement with عند, agreement with من, the lām of conveying (tablīgh), agreement with عن, conferring ownership (tamlīk), giving the reason, the one entering the imperfect, the lām of emphasizing negation, and the lām of clarification (tabyīn), which is of three kinds: for clarifying the object, clarifying agency that is confused between two objects, and the reverse.

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(سبحان) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, accusative (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (أسرى) a past verb, indeclinable on the implied fatḥa on the alif, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", and it is the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) (بعبده) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أسرى), and (الهاء) is an attached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (ليلا) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (أسرى) (من المسجد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أسرى) (الحرام) naʿt of مسجد, genitive (إلى المسجد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أسرى) (الأقصى) naʿt of the second المسجد, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the implied kasra on the alif (الذي) a relative, in the position of the genitive, a second naʿt of المسجد (باركنا) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn.. and (نا) is an attached pronoun in the position of the nominative, agent (حوله) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (باركنا), and (الهاء) is like the first (اللام) for giving a reason (نريه) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām.. and (الهاء) is an attached pronoun in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "We", for magnification.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نريه) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (أسرى).
(من آياتنا) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نريه).. and (نا) is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (إنّ) a particle of emphasis and accusative, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of the accusative, the noun of inna (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ [Note: or in the position of the accusative — it being borrowed for that — as tawkīd (emphasis) of the attached pronoun of the third person, the noun of inna.] (السميع) khabar, nominative (البصير) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause « (يسبّح) سبحان ... » has no grammatical position; it is an inceptive clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «أسرى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «باركنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذي).
The clause «نريه ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «إنّه هو السميع ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «هو السميع ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of inna.

* Morphology:
(أسرى): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by substitution; its origin is أسري with a yāʾ; the yāʾ had a vowel after a fatḥa and was turned into an alif.
(الأقصى): in form an elative (ism tafḍīl) on the pattern أفعل, then the sense of description, not of comparison, was intended by it. It contains iʿlāl by substitution: its origin is الأقصى with a yāʾ at its end, and when what precedes the yāʾ came to have a fatḥa the yāʾ was turned into an alif.. and the lām of the word is a wāw or a yāʾ, because its verb is قصا يقصو, قصي يقصى, and its meaning is "to be far".

* Rhetoric:
«سُبْحانَ الَّذِي أَسْرى بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا» 1- Mention (al-dhikr): the isrāʾ (night journey) can only occur at night, so what is the meaning of mentioning the night?
The apparent point is that the purpose of mentioning the night, even though أسرى already conveys it, is to depict the journey in its form in the mind of the hearer: as if أسرى indicated two matters, one of them the travelling, the other its being at night, and it was desired to single out one of them for mention, to fix it in the mind of the addressee and to alert him that it is intended by the mention.
A parallel for singling out one of what the preceding expression indicates, together with another, is His saying, the Exalted:
«وَقالَ اللَّهُ لا تَتَّخِذُوا إِلهَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ إِنَّما هُوَ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ». The noun that bears the dual indicates the dual and the genus, and so too the singular; so alerting was intended, because one of the two meanings, namely the dual, is intended and meant; and likewise awakening was intended, because oneness is the aim in His saying:
(إِنَّما هُوَ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ). Had it been confined to «إنما هو إله», it would have suggested that the important matter was to establish divinity for Him, whereas the aim of the speech is only to establish oneness.
2- Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): in His saying «ليلا».
By «ليلا», in indefinite form, He intended to make the duration of the journey short, and that He made him journey in part of the night from Mecca to Syria, a journey of forty nights; for the indefiniteness here indicates something of the sense of partiality. The reading of ʿAbdallāh and Ḥudhayfa bears witness to this: «من الليل», i.e. "part of the night".
3- Iltifāt (shift of person): in His saying, the Exalted «الَّذِي بارَكْنا حَوْلَهُ لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ آياتِنا- إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ» the speech is turned from the third person in His saying, the Exalted «سُبْحانَ الَّذِي أَسْرى بِعَبْدِهِ» to the form of the magnifying first person in «باركنا- ونريه- آياتنا», to magnify the blessings and the signs; for just as it indicates the magnification of what the pronoun refers to, so it indicates the greatness of what is annexed to it and issues from it, as it is said: "only the great does the great". They have mentioned a particular point about this variation: that His saying, the Exalted «الَّذِي أَسْرى بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا» indicates his journey, upon him be blessings and peace, from the world of witnessing to the world of the unseen, so the third person is the more fitting for it. His saying, the Exalted «بارَكْنا حَوْلَهُ» indicates the sending down of blessings, which suits the magnification of the One who sends down, and the expression by the pronoun of majesty ensures that. His saying, Glorified is He, «لنريه» is in the sense of distance of connection and rarity of presence, so the speaker in direct address suits it. His saying, the Exalted «مِنْ آياتِنا»
is a return to magnification, as the indication has preceded. As for the third person in His saying, Mighty and Majestic, «إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ», on the assumption that the pronoun refers to Him, the Exalted — which is the more apparent and the view of most — it is so as to agree with His saying «بعبده»; and this is strengthened by the specification, which places this iltifāt in the best of places and fits the giving of reason most fully, since the meaning is: He brought him near and singled him out with this honour because He, Glorified, is aware of his states, knowing his worthiness of this station.

* Benefits:
- The grammarians agree that the principal meaning of the preposition (من) is ibtidāʾ al-ghāya (the beginning of the limit).
A question arises: is it for the beginning of the limit in both time and place?
The answer is that the grammarians agree that it is for the beginning of the limit in place, and differ about its being for the beginning of the limit in time.
The Kufans and some of the Basrans hold that it is, and that is the sound view; it has occurred in the Noble Book and in the noble Ḥadīth, and there is no proof beyond that:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said «مطرنا من الجمعة إلى الجمعة» ("It rained on us from Friday to Friday").
Al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī says:
تخيّرون من أزمان يوم حلية ... إلى اليوم قد جربن كل التجارب
(Gloss: "they have been chosen from the times of the day of Ḥilya to this day; they have tried every trial." [Translator's note: the source reads حلية; the usual form of the verse has حليمة.])
As for the preposition «إلى», the grammarians agree that it conveys the end of the limit, whether in time or place. An example of the temporal is His saying, the Exalted: «ثُمَّ أَتِمُّوا الصِّيامَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ» and an example of the spatial is His saying, the Exalted: «إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَى». Whoever wishes to exhaust the meanings of the two particles should consult the longer works, for in them is quenching for every thirsty one.

safi-cedvel:2-6.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction — or resumptive (آتينا) like باركنا [Note: in verse (1) of the sura], (موسى) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the implied fatḥa — and it is prevented from tanwīn because it is a proper name and foreign (الكتاب) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الواو) a conjunction (جعلناه) like باركنا.. and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (هدى) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: and if the verb is given the sense of "We made him" then (هدى) is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl.], the sign of the accusative being the implied fatḥa on the alif (لبني) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (هدى) [Note: or attached to (جعلناه)], the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, for it is appended to the sound masculine plural (إسرائيل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, because it is a proper name and foreign [Translator's note: i.e. a diptote] (أن) a particle of explanation [Note: what precedes it has the sense of saying without its letters, namely the word الكتاب, i.e. "We said in it: do not take…". It is also permissible that (أن) be a maṣdar particle that governs the accusative.], (لا) prohibitive [Note: or redundant if (أن) is a maṣdar particle, and the implied form then is: "We made it a guidance… lest you take…"; the interpreted maṣdar is then a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with an omitted muḍāf.], (تتّخذوا) an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. [Note: or accusative by أن, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the agent] and (الواو) is the agent (من دوني) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a second mafʿūl whose governor is تتّخذوا [Note: or it is attached to (تتّخذوا), the first mafʿūl being (ذرّيّة) and the second (وكيلا).. and it is permissible that the adverbial be attached to a ḥāl from (وكيلا)] and (الياء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (وكيلا) the first mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «آتينا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the inceptive [Note: or it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.].
The clause «جعلناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause آتينا..
The clause «تتّخذوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative.
3- (ذرّية) badal of (وكيلا), accusative [Note: concerning the accusative of (ذريّة) the exegetes have different views, among them: it is the first mafʿūl bihi of the verb تتّخذوا — as in note no. (1) — and the second mafʿūl is (وكيلا), i.e.: "do not take the offspring of those We carried with Noah as guardians". Among them: that it is a badal of (وكيلا) — as in the i'rab above. Or it is accusative as the object of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), the view of al-Zamakhsharī; or it is a vocative, the view of al-Suyūṭī.
(4, 5, 6) in verse (1) of the sura], (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (حملنا) like (باركنا) «4» (مع) an adverb, accusative, attached to (حملنا) (إنّه) like the preceding «5» (كان) an incomplete past verb (a governing verb), and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he" (عبدا) khabar of كان (شكورا) naʿt of (عبدا), accusative.
The clause «حملنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «إنّه كان ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «كان عبدا ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of inna.
4- (الواو) a conjunction (قضينا) like باركنا «6», (إلى بني إسرائيل) like لبني إسرائيل [Note: in verse (2) of the sura], attached to (قضينا) by its being given the sense of "We revealed" or "We carried out" (في الكتاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قضينا) (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath (تفسدنّ) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the persistence of the nūn, which has been dropped because of the succession of similar letters, and the omitted (الواو), dropped because of the meeting of two sākin letters, is the agent, and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تفسدنّ) (مرّتين) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, whose governor is تفسدنّ, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ (الواو) a conjunction (لتعلنّ) like (لتفسدنّ) and conjoined to it (علوّا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative (كبيرا) naʿt of (علوا), accusative.
The clause «قضينا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause آتينا.
The clause «تفسدنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to an implied oath [Note: or the response of an oath for His saying: وقضينا.. because it is given the sense of an oath; hence their saying قضى الله لأفعلنّ ("Allah decreed: I shall surely do…"), they treat decree and destiny as an oath.].
The clause «تعلنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تفسدنّ [Note: or it is the response of an implied oath conjoined to the first oath].
5- (الفاء) a conjunction (إذا) an adverb of future time, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, attached to (بعثنا) (جاء) a past verb (وعد) agent, nominative (أولاهما) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the implied kasra on the alif.. and (هما) is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (بعثنا) like باركنا [Note: in verse (1) of this sura], (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (بعثنا) (عبادا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (اللام) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a naʿt of (عبادا) (أولي) a second naʿt, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, for it is appended to the sound masculine plural (بأس) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (شديد) naʿt of بأس, genitive (الفاء) a conjunction (جاسوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the agent (خلال) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (جاسوا) (الديار) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) parenthetical — or circumstantial (كان) an incomplete past verb (a governing verb), and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "it", i.e. the ravaging or the promise mentioned (وعدا) khabar of كان, accusative (مفعولا) naʿt of (وعدا), accusative.
The clause «جاء وعد ... » is in the position of the genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «بعثنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «جاسوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause بعثنا.
The clause «كان وعدا ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical [Note: or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with an implied قد
(2, 3, 4) or attached to the maṣdar (الكرّة.. or to a ḥāl from it).].
6- (ثمّ) a conjunction (رددنا) like باركنا «2», (لكم) like عليكم, attached to (رددنا) (الكرّة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (عليهم) like عليكم, attached to (رددنا) «3» (الواو) a conjunction (أمددناكم) like باركنا «4», and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (بأموال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أمددناكم) (بنين) conjoined to أموال by the wāw and genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, for it is appended to the sound masculine plural (الواو) a conjunction (وجعلناكم) like أمددناكم (أكثر) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (نفيرا) tamyīz (specification), accusative.
The clause «رددنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause بعثنا.
The clause «أمددناكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause بعثنا.
The clause «جعلناكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause بعثنا.

* Morphology:
(تعلنّ): the wāw of the group was dropped because of the meeting of two sākin letters with the first nūn of the doubled nūn of emphasis.. It contains iʿlāl by omission; its origin is تعلوونّ: the weak letter, the lām of the word, met the wāw of the group, and the weak letter was dropped because both are sākin.. then the omission proceeds as it does in sound verbs attached to the wāw of the group and the yāʾ of the feminine addressee when they are emphasised with the nūn of emphasis.. Its pattern is تفعنّ, with a fatḥa on the tāʾ and a ḍamma on the ʿayn.
(علوّا): a maṣdar of علا يعلو, and it is samāʿī (by usage), on the pattern فعلّ with two ḍammas.
(الكرّة): originally a maṣdar of the triliteral verb كرّ, on the pattern فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn, and it is sometimes used to express victory.
(نفيرا): it is فعيل in the sense of فاعل, or the plural of نفر like عبد and عبيد, or it is a maṣdar meaning going out on an expedition.

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(إن) a conditional particle that jussively governs (أحسنتم) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of the jussive, being the protasis.. and (تم) is the pronoun of the agent (أحسنتم) like the first, the apodosis (لأنفسكم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the second (أحسنتم)..
and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (إن أسأتم) like إن أحسنتم (الفاء) linking the apodosis (اللام) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "your doing evil" (الفاء) a conjunction (إذا جاء وعد الآخرة) like إذا جاء وعد أولاهما [Note: in verse (5) of this sura], i.e. the last time (اللام) for giving a reason (يسوءوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn ... and (الواو) is the agent (وجوهكم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.. and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (ليدخلوا المسجد) like ليسوءوا وجوهكم (الكاف) a preposition, of comparison (ما) a maṣdar particle (دخلوه) a past verb and its agent, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (أوّل) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar [Note: or it is a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial) standing in for the adverb, accusative.] accusative (مرّة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يسوءوا..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to the implied apodosis, i.e. بعثنا ("We sent").
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يدخلوا..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to what the first maṣdar is attached to; so it is conjoined to it.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما دخلوه..) is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "an entering like their entering the first time".
(الواو) a conjunction (ليتبّروا) like ليسوءوا (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi [Note: it is permissible that (ما) be a maṣdar particle of time, interpreted with what follows as a maṣdar attached to (يتبّروا) ..
i.e. "that they may destroy utterly the duration of their dominion over the land".], (علوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the implied ḍamma on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two sākin letters.. and (الواو) is the agent (تتبيرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative.
The clause «إن أحسنتم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «أحسنتم (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a jussive condition not accompanied by the fāʾ.
The clause «أسأتم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.
The clause «لها (إساءتكم) ... » is in the position of the jussive, as the apodosis of the second condition, accompanied by the fāʾ.
The clause «جاء وعد ... » is in the position of the genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the apodosis of the first (إذا), the implied form being: "We sent upon you servants".
The clause «يسوءوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «يدخلوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second implied particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «دخلوه ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).
The clause «يتبّروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the third implied particle-type relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(علوا): it contains iʿlāl by omission because of the meeting of two sākin letters: the lām of the verb and the wāw of the group met, both sākin, so the lām of the verb, the weak letter alif, was dropped, and what precedes the wāw stayed with a fatḥa as an indication of it. Its pattern is فعوا with fatḥa on the fāʾ and the ʿayn.
(تتبيرا): a regular maṣdar of the verb يتبّروا, on the pattern تفعيل.

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(عسى) an incomplete past verb — a rigid (jāmid) one (ربّكم) the noun of عسى, nominative.. and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (أن) a maṣdar particle that governs the accusative (يرحمكم) an imperfect verb, accusative.. and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (الواو) resumptive (إن عدتم عدنا) like إن أحسنتم أحسنتم [Note: in verse (7) of this sura.] (الواو) resumptive (جعلنا) a past verb..
and (نا) is the pronoun of the agent (جهنّم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; it is prevented from tanwīn because it is a proper name and feminine (للكافرين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (حصيرا), which is a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «عسى ربّكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يرحمكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يرحمكم..) is in the position of the accusative, as khabar of عسى. The clause «إن عدتم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «عدنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis, not accompanied by the fāʾ.
The clause «جعلنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(عدتم): it contains iʿlāl by omission, to suit the construction on sukūn.. for the hollow verb loses its ʿayn when it is attached to a moving pronoun of the nominative and to the nūn of the feminine plural; its pattern is فلتم, with a ḍamma on the fāʾ. (عدنا) is treated like عدتم.
(حصيرا): a derived adjective; it is فعيل in the sense of فاعل, i.e. "encompassing"; and (حصيرا) may also be in the sense of a mat that is spread for them, and it is then rigid.

safi-cedvel:9-10.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (ها) a particle of alerting (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, the noun of inna (القرآن) badal of ذا — or ʿaṭf bayān — accusative (يهدي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the yāʾ, and the agent is "he" [Note: and its object is omitted, i.e. "guides all people…"], (اللام) a preposition (التي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to (يهدي), (هي) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (أقوم) khabar, nominative (الواو) a conjunction (يبشّر) like يهدي (المؤمنين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, naʿt of المؤمنين (يعملون) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the persistence of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent (الصالحات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra (أنّ) a particle of emphasis and accusative (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to the khabar of أنّ (أجرا) the noun of أنّ, accusative (كبيرا) naʿt of (أجرا), accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ لهم أجرا..) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, namely the bāʾ, i.e. بأنّ لهم أجرا ("that for them is a reward"), attached to (يبشّر).
The clause «إنّ هذا القرآن ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يهدي ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of inna.
The clause «هي أقوم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (التي).
The clause «يبشّر ... » is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause يهدي [Note: it is permissible that the clause be disconnected, as a resumption, and then it has no position.].
The clause «يعملون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
10- (الواو) a conjunction (أنّ) like the first (الذين) a relative, the noun of أنّ (لا) negative (يؤمنون) like يعملون (بالآخرة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يؤمنون) (أعتدنا) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn.. and (نا) is the pronoun of the agent (لهم) like the first, attached to (أعتدنا) (عذابا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (أليما) naʿt of (عذابا), accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الذين..) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to what the first interpreted maṣdar is attached to; so it is conjoined to it [Note: some allow the preposition to be attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "He informs that those who do not believe…"].
The clause «لا يؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أعتدنا ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of أنّ.

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (يدعو) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the wāw (الإنسان) agent, nominative (بالشرّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يدعو) (دعاءه) accusative by removal of the preposition (nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. كدعائه ("like his supplication") [Note: and the preposition is attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "he supplicates for evil a supplication like his supplication for good".], and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi, and it is the agent of the maṣdar, (بالخير) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (دعاء) (الواو) resumptive (كان) an incomplete past verb (الإنسان) the noun of كان, nominative (عجولا) khabar of كان, accusative.
The clause «يدعو الإنسان ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كان الإنسان عجولا ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption with the sense of giving a reason.

* Morphology:
(يدع): it was written in the muṣḥaf without the wāw, contrary to the analogy of the orthography, since the verb is nominative; but when it dropped out in recitation because of the meeting of two sākin letters, it dropped out in writing contrary to analogy, and a parallel is سندع الزبانية [Note: in Sura al-ʿAlaq, verse (18)].
(عجولا): an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) — or a form of intensification — from عجل يعجل of the intransitive bāb of فرح; its pattern is فعول, with a fatḥa on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:12-14.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (جعلنا) a past verb.. and (نا) is the pronoun of the agent (الليل) the first mafʿūl bihi (النهار) conjoined to الليل by the wāw, accusative (آيتين) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ (الفاء) a conjunction (محونا) like جعلنا, (آية) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الليل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) a conjunction (جعلنا آية النهار) like محونا آية الليل (مبصرة) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (اللام) of causation (تبتغوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent (فضلا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (من ربّكم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تبتغوا) [Note: or attached to a naʿt of (فضلا)].. and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (لتعلموا عدد) like لتبتغوا فضلا (السنين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, for it is appended to the sound masculine plural, (الواو) a conjunction (الحساب) conjoined to عدد, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تبتغوا..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to the second (جعلنا)..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تعلموا..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to the second (جعلنا) and conjoined to the first maṣdar.
(الواو) a conjunction (كلّ) mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb that what follows explains (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (فصّلناه) like جعلنا and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (تفصيلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative.
The clause «جعلنا الليل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «محونا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause جعلنا الليل.
The clause «جعلنا (the second) ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause محونا.
The clause «تبتغوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «تعلموا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second (أن).
The clause « (فصّلنا) كلّ شيء ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.
The clause «فصّلناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative.
13- (الواو) a conjunction (كلّ إنسان ألزمناه) like كلّ شيء فصّلناه (طائره) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.. and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi (في عنقه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl from طائره.. and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (نخرج) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the agent is "We", for magnification (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (نخرج) (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (نخرج) (القيامة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (كتابا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (يلقاه) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the alif.. and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the agent is "he", i.e. every human being (منشورا) ḥāl from the pronoun of the third person, accusative [Note: and if the agent of يلقى refers to الكتاب, and the pronoun of the third person refers to الإنسان, it is permissible to parse (منشورا) as a second naʿt of كتاب].
The clause « (ألزمنا) كلّ إنسان ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.
The clause «ألزمناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative.
The clause «نخرج ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ألزمنا كلّ..
The clause «يلقاه ... » is in the position of the accusative, as naʿt of (كتابا).
14- (اقرأ) an imperative verb, and the agent is "you" (كتابك) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الكاف) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (كفى) a past verb, indeclinable on the implied fatḥa (الباء) a redundant preposition (نفسك) genitive in form, nominative in position, agent of كفى, and (الكاف) is like the first (اليوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (كفى) (على) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (حسيبا), which is a tamyīz [Note: or an accusative ḥāl; the word is masculine because it is in the position of the witness, the judge and the trustee; so حسيب is in the sense of حاسب ("reckoner"), and it is permissible to interpret النفس as meaning the person], accusative.
The clause «اقرأ ... » is in the position of the accusative, as the reported speech of an implied saying which is a ḥāl from the agent of نخرج, i.e. "saying: read…".
The clause «كفى بنفسك ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.

* Morphology:
(طائره): the ṭāʾir is well known; its form is فاعل from طار; here it comes in the sense of deed, or the book of deeds, by istiʿāra (metaphor); or it is a kināya (allusion) for what Allah has decreed, which clings to a person and reaches him without deviating from him.
(عنقه): a rigid noun for the well-known organ; its pattern is فعل with two ḍammas.
(منشورا): a passive participle of the triliteral verb نشر; its pattern is مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
1- Majāz (figurative usage): in His saying, the Exalted «وَجَعَلْنا آيَةَ النَّهارِ مُبْصِرَةً».
It is majāz by the relation of causation, or the attribution is figurative, as in "his day is fasting"; the meaning is that its people see; and the attribution to the day is also figurative, being attribution to the customary cause, the real agent being Allah the Exalted.
2- Istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya (explicit metaphor): in His saying, the Exalted: «وَكُلَّ إِنسانٍ أَلْزَمْناهُ طائِرَهُ فِي عُنُقِهِ».
They used to take omens from birds and called it zajr; when they travelled and a bird passed them they would scare it off. If it passed them sāniḥan, passing from the left side to the right, they took it as a good omen; and if it passed bāriḥan, passing from the right side to the left, they took it as an evil omen. Hence it was called taṭayyur. When they ascribed good and evil to the bird, the word was borrowed, by explicit metaphor, for what resembles it of Allah's decree, the Exalted, and the deed of the servant, because it is a cause of good and evil. From this comes the saying "the ṭāʾir of Allah, the Exalted, not your ṭāʾir", i.e. the prevailing decree of Allah, mighty is His station, to which good and evil are ascribed, not your ṭāʾir by which you take ill omen or good omen.

safi-cedvel:15-16.t:
* I'rab:
(من) a conditional noun that jussively governs, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (اهتدى) a past verb, indeclinable on the implied fatḥa on the alif, in the position of the jussive, being the protasis, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he" (الفاء) linking the apodosis (إنّما) kāffa and makfūfa (يهتدي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the yāʾ, and the agent is "he" (لنفسه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl from the agent of يهتدي, and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (من ضلّ فإنّما يضلّ) like من اهتدى.. (على) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a ḥāl from the agent of يضلّ (الواو) a conjunction (لا) negative (تزر) an imperfect verb, nominative (وازرة) agent, nominative, and it is a naʿt of an omitted described noun, i.e. "a soul that bears" (وزر) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (أخرى) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the implied kasra on the alif, and it is a naʿt of an omitted described noun, i.e. "another soul" (الواو) a conjunction (ما) for negation (كنّا) an incomplete past verb (a governing verb) and (نا) is the noun of كان (معذّبين) khabar of كان, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ (حتّى) a particle of limit and of the genitive (نبعث) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after حتّى, and the agent is for magnification (رسولا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «من اهتدى ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «اهتدى ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «1».
The clause «يهتدي ... » is in the position of the jussive, as the apodosis accompanied by the fāʾ «2».
The clause «من ضلّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من اهتدى.
The clause «ضلّ.....» is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «3».
The clause «يضلّ ... » is in the position of the jussive, as the apodosis accompanied by the fāʾ «4».
The clause «لا تزر وازرة ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.
The clause «ما كنّا معذّبين ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to a clause with no position.
16- (الواو) a conjunction (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, in the position of the accusative, attached to (أمرنا) (أردنا) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn.. and (نا) is the agent (أن) a maṣdar particle that governs the accusative (نهلك) an imperfect verb, accusative, and the agent is "We", for magnification, (قرية) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (أمرنا) like أردنا (مترفيها) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.. and (ها) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الفاء) a conjunction (فسقوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the agent (في) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (فسقوا) (الفاء) a conjunction (حقّ) a past verb (عليها) like فيها, attached to (حقّ) (القول) agent, nominative (الفاء) a conjunction (دمّرناها) like أردنا.. and (ها) is mafʿūl bihi (تدميرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نهلك..) is in the position of the accusative, as mafʿūl bihi, whose governor is أردنا.
The clause «أردنا ... » is in the position of the genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «نهلك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «أمرنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «فسقوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «حقّ عليها القول» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause فسقوا.
The clause «دمّرناها ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause حقّ عليها القول.

* Morphology:
(مترفيها): plural of مترف, a passive participle of the quadriliteral أترف; its pattern is مفعل, with a ḍamma on the mīm and a fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(تدميرا): a regular maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb دمّر; its pattern is تفعيل.

* Rhetoric:
1- Ṭibāq (antithesis): in His saying, the Exalted: «مَنِ اهْتَدى - وَمَنْ ضَلَّ» ..
Ṭibāq occurs in the verse between guidance (al-hudā) and error (al-ḍalāl).
2- Iltizām, or luzūm mā lā yalzam (the obligation of what is not obligatory):
in His saying, the Exalted: «أَمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها فَفَسَقُوا فِيها».
Iltizām is the observing of one letter or two or more before the rawī (the rhyme letter), as far as the poet's or writer's capacity allows, without strain.
Here in «مترفيها» and «فيها» the fāʾ is observed before the yāʾ of the ridf (supporting letter), and the yāʾ is kept; much of it will come in the Noble Qur'an, and it is among the most elegant of usages.
3- Majāz (figurative usage): in His saying, the Exalted «أَمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها».
The original is "We commanded its affluent to dissipate, so they dissipated", but intending the literal sense is impossible, so it is taken as majāz, either by the way of istiʿāra tamthīliyya (representational metaphor), by likening their state, in their plunging into blessings together with their disobedience and arrogance, to the state of one who has been commanded to do so; or by the way of istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tabaʿiyya (explicit derivative metaphor), by likening the pouring out upon them of the blessings that make them arrogant to their being commanded to dissipate, the common ground being the driving to it and the causing of it.
4- Ḥadhf (omission): in His saying, the Exalted: «أَمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها فَفَسَقُوا فِيها».
The thing commanded is omitted, and He did not say what He commanded them, for brevity of speech and in reliance on the hearer's intuition, because His saying «ففسقوا» indicates it, and it is widespread speech. It is said:
"I commanded him and he stood", "I commanded him and he recited"; nothing is understood from it except that what was commanded was standing or reciting, and were you to go about supposing something else, you would have sought from your addressee knowledge of the unseen.

* Benefits:
Ishtighāl (preoccupation):
It is a noun that precedes a governor that would by right put it in the accusative, were it not that the governor is occupied with acting upon the noun's pronoun, as in خالد أكرمه ("Khālid, I honoured him"). The preferred view is that the preceding noun is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and the clause after it is in the position of the nominative as its khabar.
There are people who have allowed its being accusative.
There is a long discussion about its being accusative or nominative that we have passed over for the sake of brevity.

safi-cedvel:17-17.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (كم) khabariyya (declarative), a substitute for a number, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (أهلكنا) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn.. and (نا) is the agent (من القرون) tamyīz of كم (من بعد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أهلكنا) (نوح) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) resumptive (كفى بربّك.. خبيرا) like كفى بنفسك حسيبا [Note: in verse (14) of this sura], (بذنوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (خبيرا أو بصيرا) ("Aware or Seeing"), (عباده) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أهلكنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كفى بربّك ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

safi-cedvel:18-20.t:
* I'rab:
(من) like the preceding [Note: in verse (15) of this sura.], (كان) an incomplete past verb, in the position of the jussive, being the protasis, and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he" (يريد) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the agent is "he" (العاجلة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (عجّلنا) like أهلكنا [Note: in the preceding verse (17).. and the verb is in the position of the jussive, being the apodosis.], (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (عجّلنا), (في) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (عجّلنا), (ما) a relative noun in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi (نشاء) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the agent is "We", for magnification (اللام) a preposition (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to (عجّلنا); it is a badal of (له), with the preposition repeated (نريد) like نشاء (ثمّ) a conjunction (جعلنا له) like عجّلنا له, and the preposition is attached to an omitted second mafʿūl (جهنّم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; it is prevented from tanwīn because it is a proper name and feminine (يصلاها) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the alif..
and (ها) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the agent is "he" (مذموما) ḥāl from the agent, accusative (مدحورا) a second ḥāl, accusative.
The clause «من كان ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كان يريد ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: it is permissible that the khabar be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «يريد ... » is in the position of the accusative, as khabar of كان.
The clause «عجّلنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis, not accompanied by the fāʾ.
The clause «نشاء ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «نريد ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «جعلنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause عجّلنا..
The clause «يصلاها ... » is in the position of the accusative, as a ḥāl from the pronoun in (له), or from جهنّم.
19- (الواو) a conjunction (من أراد) like من كان, and the agent is "he" (الآخرة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الواو) a conjunction (سعى) a past verb, indeclinable on the implied fatḥa on the alif, in the position of the jussive, conjoined to أراد, and the agent is "he" (لها) like له, attached to (سعى) (سعيها) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative [Note: or a mafʿūl bihi by giving سعى the sense of أعطى ("gave"), and سعيها means its work.], and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl (هو) a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (مؤمن) khabar, nominative (الفاء) linking the apodosis (أولئك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ..
and (الكاف) is for address (كان) an incomplete past verb (سعيهم) the noun of كان, nominative..
and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi (مشكورا) khabar of كان, accusative.
The clause «من أراد ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من كان..
The clause «أراد الآخرة ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: it is permissible that the khabar be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «سعى لها ... » is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause أراد.
The clause «هو مؤمن ... » is in the position of the accusative, as a ḥāl from the agent of سعى.
The clause «أولئك كان سعيهم ... » is in the position of the jussive, as the apodosis accompanied by the fāʾ.
The clause «كان سعيهم مشكورا» is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
20- (كلّا) a fronted mafʿūl bihi, accusative (نمدّ) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the agent is "We", for magnification (ها) a particle of alerting (أولاء) a demonstrative, a badal of (كلا), in the position of the accusative (الواو) a conjunction (هؤلاء) like the first and conjoined to it (من عطاء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نمدّ) (ربك) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.. and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl [Note: or resumptive, and the clause after it has no position, being resumptive.] (ما) negative (كان عطاء ربّك محظورا) like كان سعيهم مشكورا.
The clause «نمدّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «ما كان عطاء ربّك ... » is in the position of the accusative, as a ḥāl.

* Morphology:
(العاجلة): feminine of العاجل, an active participle of عجل on the pattern فاعل; here the adjective is used as a noun, and its meaning is this world.
(مذموما): a passive participle of the triliteral verb ذمّ; its pattern is مفعول.
(مشكورا): a passive participle of the triliteral verb شكر; its pattern is مفعول.
(محظورا): a passive participle of the triliteral verb حظر; its pattern is مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
- Laff and nashr (folding and unfolding): in His saying, the Exalted: «كُلًّا نُمِدُّ هؤُلاءِ وَهَؤُلاءِ».
It is an ordered laff and nashr: the first «هؤلاء» is the first group, i.e. the one who desires this world, and the second «هؤلاء» is for the second group, i.e. the one who desires the Hereafter.

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab:
(انظر) an imperative verb, and the agent is "you" (كيف) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl whose governor is (فضّلنا), which is a past verb and its agent (بعضهم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.. and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi (على بعض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (فضّلنا) (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) (اللام) the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ) (الآخرة) mubtadaʾ, nominative (أكبر) khabar, nominative (درجات) tamyīz, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra (الواو) a conjunction (أكبر تفضيلا) like أكبر درجات.
The clause «انظر ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «فضّلنا ... » is in the position of the accusative, as mafʿūl bihi, whose governor is the verb of looking, suspended by the interrogative كيف, and its meaning is "reflect"; and the clause is bound by the omitted preposition.
The clause «الآخرة أكبر ... » is in the position of the accusative, as a ḥāl [Note: it is permissible that it be resumptive, with no position.].

* Morphology:
(تفضيلا) a regular maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb فضّل; its pattern is تفعيل.

* Rhetoric:
- We spoke earlier about «luzūm mā lā yalzam» ("the obligation of what is not obligatory"), which is the observing of one letter, two letters or more before the rawī (rhyme letter) in poetry, and a parallel may occur in prose, such as His saying, the Exalted: «وَإِذا أَرَدْنا أَنْ نُهْلِكَ قَرْيَةً أَمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها فَفَسَقُوا فِيها»
. In the Luzūmiyyāt of al-Maʿarrī there is a great deal of this art, such as his saying:
رويدك قد غررت وأنت حر ... بصاحب حيلة يعظ النساء

يحرم فيكم الصهباء صبحا ... ويشربها على عمد مساء

يقول لقد غدوت بلا كساء ... وفي لذاتها رهن الكساء
(Gloss: "Gently — you have been deceived, free man, by a crafty fellow who preaches to women; in the morning he forbids wine among you, and in the evening he drinks it deliberately; he says: 'I have gone out without a garment', while in its pleasures lies the pledge of the garment.")
And beware of this art, for going too far in it leads to hateful artificiality and rejected affectation.

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) a prohibitive that governs the jussive (تجعل) an imperfect verb, jussive, and the agent is "you" (مع) an adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl (الله) the sacred Name, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (إلها) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (آخر) naʿt of إله, accusative; it is prevented from tanwīn because of being a descriptive adjective and the pattern أفعل (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya) (تقعد) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ, and the agent is "you" (مذموما) ḥāl, accusative (مخذولا) a second ḥāl, accusative..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقعد) is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to a maṣdar gleaned from the preceding prohibition, i.e.: "let there not be from you a setting up of a god with Allah, and then a sitting in a state of blame and abandonment".
The clause «لا تجعل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «تقعد ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(مخذولا): a passive participle of the triliteral verb خذل; its pattern is مفعول.

safi-cedvel:23-24.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (قضى) a past verb, indeclinable on the implied fatḥa on the alif (ربّك) agent, nominative.. and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (أن) a maṣdar particle that governs the accusative [Note: or a particle lightened from the heavy (أنّ), its noun being an omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), i.e. "that it.."; (لا) is then a prohibitive that governs the jussive.], (لا) negative (تعبدوا) an imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent [Note: or jussive by the prohibitive لا, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn..] (إلّا) a particle of restriction [Note: or it is — on the second analysis — a particle of exception.], (إيّاه) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi [Note: or in the position of the accusative as the excepted, or a badal of the omitted object, i.e. "your Lord decreed that (it) you worship no one (أحدا) except Him".], (الواو) a conjunction (بالوالدين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "do good" (أحسنوا) (إحسانا) mafʿūl muṭlaq of the omitted verb, accusative [Note: see verses (83) of al-Baqara, (36) of al-Nisāʾ and (151) of al-Anʿām, for there is further detail about the i'rab of the word (إحسانا) and the place of attachment of the preposition (بالوالدين).]..
The interpreted maṣdar (ألا تعبدوا..) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e. بألّا تعبدوا.., attached to (قضى).
(إن) a conditional particle that jussively governs (ما) redundant (يبلغنّ) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the jussive of the condition.. and (النون) is for emphasis (عندك) an adverb, accusative, attached to (يبلغنّ), and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (الكبر) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (أحدهما) agent, nominative.. and (هما) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (أو) a conjunction (كلاهما) conjoined to أحدهما, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the alif, for it is appended to the dual, attached to the pronoun (الفاء) linking the apodosis (لا) a prohibitive that governs the jussive (تقل) an imperfect verb, jussive, and the agent is "you" (اللام) a preposition and (هما) an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (تقل) (أفّ) a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) of the imperfect, meaning "I am vexed", and the agent is "I" (الواو) a conjunction (لا تنهر) like لا تقل.. and (هما) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (الواو) a conjunction (قل) an imperative verb, and the agent is "you" (لهما) like the first, attached to (قل) (قولا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: in the sense of "speech"; had the maṣdar been intended, it would be an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq.], (كريما) naʿt of (قولا), accusative.
The clause «قضى ربّك ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «تعبدوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «إمّا يبلغنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «لا تقل ... » is in the position of the jussive, as the apodosis accompanied by the fāʾ.
The clause «لا تنهرهما» is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the clause لا تقل.
The clause «قل ... » is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the clause لا تقل.
24- (الواو) a conjunction (اخفض لهما جناح) like قل لهما قولا.. and the preposition is attached to (اخفض) (الذلّ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (من الرحمة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (اخفض) [Note: and مِن is causal or for the beginning of the limit, and it is permissible that the preposition be attached to an omitted ḥāl from جناح الذلّ.], (الواو) a conjunction (قل) like the first (ربّ) the one addressed (munādā), muḍāf, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on what precedes the yāʾ that is dropped for lightness, and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (ارحمهما) like قل, and (هما) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the command is a supplication (الكاف) a preposition (ما) a maṣdar particle (ربّياني) a past verb, and (الألف) is the agent, and (النون) is for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء) is mafʿūl bihi (صغيرا) ḥāl from the yāʾ of the object, accusative..
The interpreted maṣdar (ما ربّياني) is in the position of the genitive by the kāf — which here has the sense of giving a reason, not of comparison — attached to (ارحم) [Note: for some the kāf is for comparison, so it is attached to a mafʿūl muṭlaq, and the implied form is: "have mercy on them with a mercy like their mercy to me" or "like their rearing of me".].
The clause «اخفض ... » is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the clause لا تقل.
The clause «قل ... » is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the clause لا تقل.
The clause «the vocative and its response ... » is in the position of the accusative, as the reported speech.
The clause «ارحمهما ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «ربّياني ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(كلاهما): a noun indicating the dual whose form is singular, used for the masculine, always annexed.
(جناح): a rigid noun for the well-known organ; its pattern is فعال with a fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(الذلّ): a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral verb ذلّ; its pattern is فعل with a ḍamma then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- Istiʿāra makniyya and takhyīliyya (implicit and imaginative metaphor): in His saying, the Exalted: «وَاخْفِضْ لَهُما جَناحَ الذُّلِّ».
Humility is likened to a bird descending from on high, by an implicit simile; the wing is affirmed for it by imagination (takhyīl), and the lowering as a strengthening (tarshīḥ). For when a bird wants to fly and rise it spreads its wings and lifts them to ascend; when it leaves that, it lowers them. Also, when it sees a bird of prey it fears, it clings to the ground and presses its wings down, which is the extreme of its fear and humility. It has also been said that the lowering of them intended is what it does when it gathers its chicks, to rear them, and that this is more fitting to the context.

* Benefits:
1- Among the wonders of this language:
The grammarians differed about the verbal nouns (asmāʾ al-afʿāl) regarding their consideration and naming; the sound view is that they are verbal nouns and have no position in i'rab.
And «أف» is a verbal noun of the imperfect in the sense of «أتضجّر» ("I am vexed"). Its dialects are many, reaching, according to some, forty dialects, of which seven were recited, three of them mutawātir and four of the irregular (shādhdh) kind. In the reading of Ḥafṣ we read «أفّ» with kasra, tanwīn and shadda. If you are among the horsemen of this science, consult the longer works, for in them is what quenches the thirst of the thirsty.
2- Between contentment and disobedience (to parents):
After the reader has savoured the Qur'an's counsel to obey one's parents, it is fitting for us to mention a little of the story of those who were undutiful to their parents, for by contrast things are distinguished.
It is related that Jarīr was the most undutiful of people to his father. His son Bilāl was undutiful to him, and one day they reviled one another, and Bilāl was harsh to his father. His mother said to him: "O enemy of Allah, do you say this to your father?" Jarīr said: "Leave him; it is as though he heard it from me when I said it to my father."
Al-Ḥuṭayʾa was of notable undutifulness to parents; he said, satirising his father:
فنعم الشيخ أنت لدى المخازي ... وبئس الشيخ أنت لدى الفعال

جمعت اللؤم لا حياك ربي ... وأبواب السفاهة والضلال
(Gloss: "What a fine old man you are in disgraces, and what an evil old man you are in deeds; you have gathered baseness — may my Lord not greet you — and the doors of folly and error.")
And he said, satirising his mother:
لحاك الله ثم لحاك أمّا ... ولقاك العقوق من البنينا

أغربالا إذا استودعت سرّا ... وكانونا على المتحدثينا
(Gloss: "May Allah curse you, and again curse you as a mother, and may you meet undutifulness from sons; are you a sieve when entrusted with a secret, and a hearth over those who converse?")

semin-durr:77-77.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {سُنَّةَ}: there are three views on it. First: that it is accusative as an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun) [mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)], i.e. "Allah established that as a sunna (practice)", or "We established that as a sunna". Second — stated by al-Farrāʾ — that it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "like the sunna of Allah"; on this view one does not pause at His words «إلا قليلاً». Third: that it is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "follow the sunna".

semin-durr:78-78.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لِدُلُوكِ}: there are two views on this lām. First: that it means «بَعْد» (after), i.e. "after the declining (دُلوك) of the sun". Similar to it is the saying of Mutammim ibn Nuwayra:
309 - 0- فلمَّا تَفَرَّقْنا كأني ومالِكاً ... لطولِ اجتماعٍ لم نَبِتْ ليلةً معاً
(When we parted, it was as though Mālik and I — after [lām] a long time together — had never spent a single night together.)
And similar to it is their expression «كَتَبَتْه لثلاثٍ خَلَوْنَ» ("I wrote it after three [nights] had passed"). Second: that it has its basic meaning, i.e. "because of the declining". Al-Wāḥidī said: "Because it [the prayer] becomes obligatory only by the sun's passing the meridian."
Al-dulūk is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of دَلَكت الشمسُ, and there are three opinions about it. The best known: that it is the zawāl (the sun's passing the meridian), which is midday. Second: that it is [the period] from the zawāl to sunset. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its derivation is from al-dalk (rubbing), because a person rubs his eye when looking at it [the sun]." I say: this implies that it is not a maṣdar, since he made it derived from the maṣdar. Third: that it is sunset; al-Farrāʾ cited in support of this:
309 - 1- هذا مُقامُ قَدَمَيْ رَباحِ ... ذَبَّبَ حتى دَلَكَتْ بَِرَاحِ
(This is the standing-place of Rabāḥ's two feet; he kept [the herd] moving until Barāḥ declined.)
i.e. Barāḥ set, and that is the sun. Ibn Qutayba cited for this the verse of Dhū al-Rumma:
309 - 2- مصابيحُ ليسَتْ باللواتي تقودها ... نُجومٌ ولا بالآفلاتِ الدوالِكِ
(Lamps that are not of those led by stars, nor of those that vanish and set [الدوالك].)
i.e. the setting ones. Al-Rāghib said: "The dulūk of the sun is its inclining towards setting; it is from their expression دَلَكْتُ الشمسَ: 'I pushed it away with the palm [al-rāḥ]'. From it: دَلَكْتُ الشيءَ في الراحةِ ('I rubbed the thing in the palm'), and دَلَكْتُ الرجلَ: 'I put the man off [in paying a debt]'; al-dalūk: whatever perfume you rub on; and al-dalīk: a food made of butter and dates."
His words: {إلى غَسَقِ اليل}: there are two views on this preposition-phrase. First: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أَقِمْ», so it is for the terminal limit of the establishing [of the prayer]; likewise the lām in «لِدُلوك» is also attached to it. Second: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الصلاة», i.e. "establish it extended until the darkness of the night"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. There is reservation about this, in that he assumed the omitted element to be a specific (restricted) being, unless he intends an explanation of the meaning, not of the iʿrāb.
Al-ghasaq is the onset of the beginning of the night; Ibn Shumayl said this, and he cited:
309 - 3- إنَّ هذا الليلَ قد غَسَقا ... واشتكيْتُ الهَمَّ والأرقا
(This night has grown dark [غسق], and I have complained of care and sleeplessness.)
It is also said: it is the blackness of the night and its darkness. Its origin is from flowing: غَسَقَتِ العين, i.e. the eye's tears flowed; it is as though the darkness pours onto the world and flows over them. [The poet] said:
309 - 4- ظلَّتْ تجودُ يداها وهي لاهِيَةٌ ... حتى إذا هَجَمَ الإِظْلامُ والغَسَقُ
(Her two hands kept on giving while she was heedless, until darkness and ghasaq fell suddenly.)
And it is said: غَسَقَتِ العينُ: the eye filled with tears; غَسَقَ الجرحُ: the wound filled with blood; so it is as though darkness filled all existence. As for al-ghāsiq in His words {وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ} [al-Falaq: 3], it is said that what is meant is the moon when it is eclipsed and turns black; and it is said: the night. Al-ghasāq, with and without doubling [of the sīn], is the pus that flows from the people of the Fire. One says غَسَق الليلُ and أَغْسَقَ, ظَلَمَ and أَظْلَمَ, دَجَى and أَدْجَى, غَبَشَ and أَغْبَشَ; al-Farrāʾ transmitted this.
His words: {قُرْآنَ الفجر}: there are several views on it. First: that it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الصلاة», i.e. "and establish the recitation (qurʾān) of the dawn", what is meant being the morning prayer, expressed by one of its pillars. Second: that it is accusative by way of incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e. "and [hold to] — عليك — the recitation of the dawn"; al-Akhfash gave this implied form and Abū al-Baqāʾ followed him. The principles of the Basrans reject this, because verbal nouns (asmāʾ al-afʿāl) do not operate when implied. Third: that it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "make much recitation" or "keep to the recitation of the dawn".

semin-durr:79-79.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمِنَ اليل}: there are two views on this «منْ». First: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تَهَجَّدْ», i.e. "keep vigil with the Qurʾān for part of the night". Second: that it is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "and rise for a rising from the night", or "and stay awake for part of the night"; al-Ḥawfī mentioned both. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And [hold to] — عليك — part of the night, and keep vigil with it." If he meant an explanation of the meaning, it is close; but if he meant an explanation of the iʿrāb, it is not valid, because the thing incited to (al-mughrā bihi) cannot be a particle; and his making «مِنْ» mean "part" does not require it to be a noun — the proof being that the wāw of «مع» (accompaniment) is not a noun by consensus, even though it means an explicit noun, namely «مع». / The pronoun in «به»: the apparent view is that it refers back to the Qurʾān as such, without restriction to its being annexed to "the dawn". Second: that it refers back to the implied time, i.e. "and rise for a time of the night, and keep vigil in that time", so the bāʾ means «في» (in).
His words «نافِلَةً»: there are several views on it. First: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "you perform a supererogatory act as an extra (nāfila) for yourself beyond the obligatory prayers". Second: that it is accusative by «تَهَجَّدْ», because it carries the meaning of "perform supererogatory prayer", as though it were said: "perform supererogatory prayer as a nāfila". Al-nāfila is a maṣdar like al-ʿāqiba and al-ʿāfiya. Third: that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "[as] a prayer of nāfila"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this; it would then be a ḥāl of the hāʾ in «به» if you make it refer to the Qurʾān, not to an implied time. Fourth: that it is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); this is the apparent sense of al-Ḥawfī's statement, for he said: "«نافلةً» may be accusative by «تهجَّدْ» if you take it in the sense of: pray with it a nāfila, i.e. pray a nāfila for yourself."
Al-tahajjud is abandoning al-hujūd, which is sleep; the form tafaʿʿala comes for privation, as in تَحَرَّجَ and تَأَثَّمَ (to avoid sin), and in the ḥadīth: «كان يَتَحَنَّثُ بغارِ حراءٍ» ("He used to devote himself to worship [lit. avoid sin] in the cave of Ḥirāʾ"). There is disagreement among the lexicographers about al-hujūd. It is said: it is sleep. [The poet] said:
309 - 5- وبَرْكُ هُجودٍ قد أثارَتْ مَخافتي ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And many a herd of sleeping [هجود] camels my fearsomeness has roused …)
Another said:
309 - 6- ألا طَرَقَتْنا والرِّفاقُ هُجودُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Lo, she visited us by night while the companions were asleep [هجود] …)
Another said:
309 - 7- ألا زارَتْ وأهلُ مِنَىً هُجودُ ... وليت خيالَها بمِنَىً يعودُ
(Lo, she visited while the people of Minā were asleep [هجود] — would that her phantom might return to Minā.)
So hujūd means sleepers, plural of «هاجِد» like sājid and sujūd. It is also said: al-hujūd is shared between the sleeper and the one praying. Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: "تَهَجَّدَ: he prayed at night; and تَهَجَّدَ: he slept", and this is the view of Abū ʿUbayda and al-Layth.
His words: {عسى أَن يَبْعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقَاماً}: there are four views on the accusative of «مَقاماً». First: that it is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "He will raise you in a station". Second: that it is accusative by the meaning of «يَبْعَثُك», because it carries the meaning of "He will set you up"; one says "he was set up (أُقِيم) from his grave" and "he was raised (بُعِث) from it" with one meaning; so it is like "he sat (قعد) a sitting (جلوساً)". Third: that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "He will raise you possessing a praised station". Fourth: that it is an emphatic maṣdar whose governing word is implied, i.e. "so you will stand a standing".
On the first three views, but not the fourth, «عَسَى» must be the complete (tāmma) [verb], so it is predicated of «أنْ» and what is within its domain. For if it were the defective (nāqiṣa) one, with {أَن يَبْعَثَكَ} as a fronted khabar (predicate) and «ربُّك» as a postponed noun [of ʿasā], something forbidden would follow: namely separating, by something extraneous, between the ṣila (relative clause) of the [nominal-]relative and what it governs. For «مَقاماً», on the first three views, is accusative by «يَبْعَثُكَ», which is the ṣila of «أَنْ»; so if you make «رَبُّك» the noun of [ʿasā], it is extraneous to the ṣila and may not separate; but if you make it the fāʿil (agent) [of يبعث], it is not extraneous, so separation by it does not matter.
As for the fourth view, it may be the complete or the defective [ʿasā] with fronting and postponing, since nothing forbidden arises, because «مقاماً» is governed by something other than the ṣila. This is among the fine points of the craft of grammar, and you have had something close to it earlier in Sūrat Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, in the words of Allah the Exalted: {أَفِي الله شَكٌّ فَاطِرِ} [Ibrāhīm: 10].

semin-durr:80-80.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ}: it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), or an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), and the latter is the apparent view. The majority read with ḍamma on the mīm in both [مُدخل and مُخرج], because a quadriliteral verb precedes them. Qatāda, Abū Ḥaywa, Ibrāhīm ibn Abī ʿAbla and Ḥumayd read with fatḥa on the mīm in both: either because they are maṣdars with the augments removed, like {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17], or because they are accusative by an implied verb corresponding to them, its implied form being "so enter an entering (مَدْخَل) and go out a going out (مَخْرَج)". This was discussed fully earlier under the reading of Nāfiʿ in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, and that he read likewise in Sūrat al-Ḥajj.
«مُدْخَلُ صِدْقٍ» and «مُخْرَجُ صِدْقٍ» are an explanatory annexation (iḍāfat al-tabyīn); according to the Kufans, they are the annexation of the described to its adjective, because it [صدق] is used as an adjective for emphasis.
His words: «سُلْطاناً»: it is the first object of «جَعَل» (making), and the second is one of the two preceding preposition-phrases, while the other is attached to its being-settled (istiqrār). «نصيراً» may be converted from [the pattern] fāʿil for intensiveness, or it may have the meaning of mafʿūl (passive sense).

semin-durr:81-81.t:
Al-zuhūq is going away and vanishing. [The poet] said:
309 - 8- ولقد شَفَى نَفْسي وأبرَأَ سُقْمَها ... إقدامُه بمَزَالَةٍ لم يَزْهَقِ
(What healed my soul and cured its sickness was his advancing in a place of slipping without his perishing [يزهق].)
One says: زَهَقَتْ نَفْسي تَزْهَقُ زُهوقاً, with ḍamma. As for al-zahūq with fatḥa, it is an intensive form, as in his words:
309 - 9- ضَرُوْبٌ بنَصْلِ السَّيْفِ سُوقَ سِمانِها ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(One who strikes much [ضروب] with the sword's blade the shanks of the fat ones among them …)

semin-durr:82-82.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِنَ القرآن}: there are three views on this «مِنْ». First: that it is for clarifying the genus (bayān al-jins); al-Zamakhsharī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected this from them: the [مِن] of clarification must be preceded by what it clarifies, not precede it, whereas here it is found preceding it.
Second: that it is partitive. Al-Ḥawfī rejected this, saying: "Because it would then follow that part of it is not a healing." It was answered that its sending down is what is in parts. This answer is not evident. Abū al-Baqāʾ answered that part of it heals from illness. I say: this has indeed occurred, as proven by one of the Companions' reciting al-Fātiḥa as a ruqya (healing incantation) over the chief of the tribe who had been stung, and he was healed.
Third: that it is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), and this is clear.
The majority read «شِفاءٌ/ ورحمةٌ» nominative, as two khabars (predicates) of «هو», the clause being the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما». Zayd ibn ʿAlī read both accusative, and his reading was explained as their being accusative as ḥāls (circumstantials), the ṣila then being «للمؤمنين», with the ḥāl fronted before its abstract governing element, like His words {والسماوات مَطْوِيَّاتٌ بِيَمِينِهِ} [al-Zumar: 67] in the reading of those who make «مَطْوِيَّاتٍ» accusative, and the verse of al-Nābigha:
310 - 0- رَهْطُ ابنِ كُوْزٍ مُحْقِبي أَدراعَهم ... فيهم ورَهْطُ ربيعةَ بنِ حُذارِ
(The clan of Ibn Kūz, carrying their coats of mail behind them [محقبي], are among them, and the clan of Rabīʿa ibn Ḥudhār.)
It is also said: both are accusative by an implied verb; this is [the position of] those who forbid fronting it [the ḥāl] before its abstract governing element. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Al-Kisāʾī permitted «ورحمةً» in the accusative, conjoined to «ما»." The apparent sense of this is that al-Kisāʾī left «شفاء» in the nominative and made only «رحمة» accusative, conjoined to the relative «ما», as though it were said: "and We send down of the Qurʾān a mercy"; and there is nothing in his report indicating that he recited it as Qurʾān. The disagreement [over] «وننزل» with or without doubling was given earlier. The majority read with the nūn of majesty; Mujāhid read «ويُنْزِل» with the yāʾ of the absent [third person], i.e. Allah.

semin-durr:83-83.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَنَأَى}: the majority read with the hamza before the weak letter, from al-naʾy, which is distance. Ibn Dhakwān — and the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] transmitted it from Ibn ʿĀmir in full — read «ناءَ», with the alif before the hamza. There are two explanations for it. First: that it is from ناء يَنُوْءُ, i.e. "he rose (with effort)". The poet said:
310 - 1- حتى إذا ما التأَمَتْ مَفاصِلُهْ ... وناءَ في شِقِّ الشِّمالِ كاهلُهْ
(Until, when his joints had knit together and his shoulders rose heavily [ناء] on the left side.)
Second: that it is metathesized (maqlūb) from نأى, its pattern being falaʿa, as they say «راءَ» for «رأى», and other such cases; but whenever it is possible to avoid metathesis, that is preferable. This same disagreement also occurs in Sūrat Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda.
The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim inclined the alif with full imāla (inclination); al-Sūsī [read it] between the two (bayna bayna), with a disagreement reported from him; likewise in Fuṣṣilat, except Abū Bakr, who did not incline it [there].
Khalaf, Abū al-Ḥārith and al-Dūrī from al-Kisāʾī inclined the fatḥa of the nūn in both sūras.

semin-durr:84-84.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {على شَاكِلَتِهِ}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَعْمل». As for al-shākila, the best that has been said about it is what al-Zamakhsharī said: that it is his way which resembles (yushākilu) his state in guidance and misguidance, from their expression "a road with shawākil", which are the paths that branch off from it; and the proof of this is His words {فَرَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ هُوَ أهدى سَبِيلاً}. It is said: according to his religion; it is said: his character. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "his side". Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is the manner and way upon which he was created."
It is from «الشَّكْلِ», which is the like; one says: "you are not of my shakl nor of my shākila". As for «الشِّكْلُ» with kasra, it is the appearance; one says: "a girl of beautiful shikl". Imruʾ al-Qays said:
310 - 2- حَيِّ الحُمولَ بجانب العَزْلِ ... إذ لا يُلائم شَكلُها شَكْلي
(Greet the camel-borne litters beside al-ʿAzl, since her like [شكلها] does not suit my like [شكلي].)
i.e. her like does not suit my like.
[Translator's note: the text says «وأمَّا "الشَّكْلُ" بالكسر», writing the vowel of the first letter as fatḥa while stating "with kasra"; the intended word is الشِّكْل.]
His words: «أَهْدى»: it may be from «اهْتَدى» with the augments removed; or from the transitive «هَدَى»; or from the intransitive «هدى» meaning اهتدى. «سبيلاً» is a tamyīz (specification).

semin-durr:85-85.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِّن العلم}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أُوْتِيْتُم». It may not be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «قليلاً», because if it were placed after it, it would be an adjective; [and it cannot be fronted thus] because what is within the domain of «إلاَّ» does not precede it.
ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] and al-Aʿmash read «وما أُوْتُوا» ("and they were not given") with the pronoun of the absent [third person].

semin-durr:87-87.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِلاَّ رَحْمَةً}: there are two opinions about it. First: that it is a connected exception (muttaṣil), because it is included in His words «وكيلا». Second: that it is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ), so it is rendered by «لكن» (but) according to the Basrans and by «بل» (rather) according to the Kufans. «مِنْ ربِّك»: it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «رحمة», or attached to an omitted element as an adjective of it.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
The words of the Exalted: {سُبْحَانَ}: the discussion of it has preceded in full at the beginning of al-Baqara. And «أَسْرى» and «سَرَى» are two dialectal forms; the discussion of them has preceded in Sūrat Hūd, together with the fact that some restricted «أَسْرى» to the night. Al-Zamakhsharī said here: "If you say: the isrāʾ (night journey) is only by night, so what is the meaning of mentioning the night? I say: by His words «ليلاً», in indefinite form, He intended to make the duration of the night journey small, and that he was taken by night in part of the night from Mecca to Syria, a journey of forty nights; that is because the indefiniteness indicates partiality. The reading of ʿAbd Allāh and Ḥudhayfa, «من الليل» (of the night), i.e. part of it, bears witness to that, as in His words: {وَمِنَ الليل فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِ} [al-Isrāʾ: 79]." End of quote. So «سَرى» and «أسْرى» are like «سَقَى» and «أَسْقى», and the hamza is not for transitivity; the transitivity is only by the bāʾ in «بعبده». It has preceded in al-Baqara that, according to the majority, it does not entail the agent accompanying the object, contrary to al-Mubarrad.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya claimed that the object of «أَسْرى» is omitted and that the transitivity is by the hamza, saying: "It appears that «أَسْرى» is made transitive by the hamza to an omitted object, i.e. He made the angels journey by night with His servant, because it is awkward to ascribe «أسرى», when it is in the sense of «سرى», to Allah the Exalted, since it is an act that entails movement, like walking, running, coming and moving; so it is not good to ascribe any of this [to Him] while there is an alternative to it. If anything of that occurs in the revealed law, we interpret it, as in: 'I come to him running (harwala)'."
I say: all of this he built only on the belief that transitivity by the bāʾ entails the agent's accompanying the object in that; and the rebuttal of this position has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara, on His words {وَلَوْ شَآءَ الله لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ} [the verse: 20]. Then he allowed «أَسْرى» to be in the sense of «سَرَى» with the omission of a muḍāf, as in His words: {ذَهَبَ الله بِنُورِهِمْ} [al-Baqara: 17], meaning that the implied form would be: "He whose angels journeyed by night with His servant"; and what led him to that is the belief in accompaniment mentioned above.
His words: «لَيْلاً» is in the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and the benefit of its indefiniteness has preceded. And «من المسجد» is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya).
His words: «حولَه»: there are two views on it. The more apparent: it is in the accusative as an adverb, and the verification of the discussion of it has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. The second: it is an object. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "i.e. We made good and made to grow." He means that He made [بارَكْنا] include the meaning of a verb that is transitive by itself.
