The second: it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. «مِن طين», as He made explicit in the other verse: {وَخَلَقْتَهُ مِن طِينٍ} [Ṣād: 76]. The third: it is accusative as a tamyīz (specification); so said al-Zajjāj, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya followed him, but this is not apparent, as no vagueness of an entity or of an attribution has preceded.

semin-durr:62-62.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَرَأَيْتَكَ}: it has been treated fully in [Sūrat] al-Anʿām. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The kāf is for address, and «هذا» is the direct object, and the meaning is: 'Tell me about this one whom You have honored above me, i.e. preferred: why have You honored him when I am better than he?' So he abbreviated the discourse." This is close to al-Ḥawfī's statement.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The kāf in «أَرَأَيْتُكَ» is a particle of address with no position in the parsing, and the meaning of «أَرَأَيْتَ» is 'have you reflected' and the like, as if the speaker alerts the addressee so that he gathers himself for what is stated after. Sībawayh said: 'It means «أَخْبِرْني» (tell me),' and he exemplified it with «أَرَأَيْتك زيداً أبو من هو؟» ('Tell me about Zayd: whose father is he?'). Sībawayh's statement is sound where an interrogative follows it, as in his example, but in the verse it is as I said, and is not that which Sībawayh mentioned." I say: What he mentioned is not accepted; rather the verse is like his example, the most one can say being that the second object is omitted, namely the implied interrogative clause, since the discourse is constructed of mubtadaʾ and khabar, as if you said: «هذا الذي كَرَّمْتَه عليَّ لِمَ كرَّمته؟».
Al-Farrāʾ said: "The kāf is in the position of accusative, i.e. «أَرَأَيْتَ نفسَك», like your saying «أَتَدَبَّرْتَ أخرَ أمرِك فإني صانعٌ فيه كذا» ('Have you considered the outcome of your affair? for I shall do such-and-such about it'), and then he began anew: «هذا الذي كرَّمْتَ عليَّ»."
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The second object is omitted, its implied form being 'his preferment' or 'his honoring.'" I say: This is not permissible, because the second object in this category can only be a clause containing an interrogative.
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Had someone held that the oath clause is the second object, it would have been good." I say: What rejects that is the requirement that the second object be a clause containing an interrogative. All of this has been established in al-Anʿām, so take it into account here.
His saying: {لَئِنْ أَخَّرْتَنِ}: Ibn Kathīr read it retaining the first-person yāʾ in connection and in pause; Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr retained it in connection and dropped it in pause, which is the rule of those named regarding the yāʾs added beyond the written text; and the rest dropped it in connection and pause. All of this concerns the word in this sūra; as for the one in [Sūrat] al-Munāfiqūn, in His saying {لولا أخرتني} [verse 10], all retained it, because it is retained in the noble written text.
His saying: «لأحْتَنِكَنَّ»: the response to the oath, prepared for by the lām. The meaning of «لأحْتَنِكَنَّ» is "I shall surely take control of them, as one takes control who puts a rope on an animal's jaw (ḥanak) and leads it with it, so it neither balks nor bucks." One says «حَنَك فلانٌ الدابةَ» and «احْتَنَكها», i.e. he did that to it; and «احْتَنَكَ الجرادُ الأرض» means the locusts ate its vegetation. He said:
307 - 7- نَشْكُو إليك سَنَةً قد أَجْحَفَتْ ... جَهْداً إلى جَهْدٍ بنا فأضعفَتْ
واحتنكَتْ أموالَنا وجَلَّفَتْ ...
(Gloss: "We complain to You of a year that has wronged us, adding hardship to hardship, and weakened us, and consumed our wealth and stripped it bare.")
Sībawayh reported: «أحْنَكُ الشاتَيْن», i.e. the one of the two sheep that eats more.

semin-durr:63-63.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {اذهب فَمَن}: it has preceded that the bāʾ [i.e. the letter of «اذهب»] is assimilated into the fāʾ in certain expressions, among them this, according to Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥamza in the transmission of Khallād from him, with disagreement concerning His saying {وَمَن لَّمْ يَتُبْ فأولئك} [al-Ḥujurāt: 11].
His saying: «جزاؤُكم»: the address may be by predominance (taghlīb), because both an absent and an addressee preceded in His saying {فَمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ}, so the addressee predominated; or the address may be intended for «مَنْ» specifically, in which case it is by way of iltifāt.
His saying: «جَزاءً»: there are several analyses for its accusative. The first: it is accusative as a maṣdar, its governor being the maṣdar before it, and it is a maṣdar clarifying the type of the first maṣdar. The second: it is accusative as a maṣdar too, but by an implied verb, i.e. «يُجازَوْن جزاءً». The third: it is a prefatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa), like «جاء زيد رجلاً صالحاً». The fourth: it is a tamyīz, which is not comprehensible.
«مَوْفُوراً» is a passive participle from «وَفَرْتُه»; «وَفَرَ» is used transitively, as in Zuhayr's saying:
307 - 8- ومن يَجْعَلِ المعروفَ مِنْ دُوْنِ عِرْضِهِ ... يَفِرْه ومَنْ لا يَتَّقِ الشتم يُشْتَمِ
(Gloss: "Whoever places good deeds before his honor preserves it; and whoever does not guard against abuse is abused.")
and the noble verse is of this. It is also used intransitively; one says «وَفَرَ المالُ» (the wealth was abundant).

semin-durr:64-64.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {واستفزز}: an imperative clause conjoined to its like, His saying «اذهَبْ». {مَنِ استطعت}: two analyses are possible. The first: it is a relative in the position of accusative as the object of «الاستفزاز», i.e. "incite those of them whom you are able to incite." The second: it is interrogative, accusative in position by «استطعْتَ»; so said Abū l-Baqāʾ, but it is not apparent, because «اسْتَفْزِزْ» requires it as a direct object, so it is not cut off from it; and were we to make it interrogative it would be suspended from it, yet it is not a verb of the heart, so as to be suspended.
«الاسْتِفْزاز» is making light of; «استفزَّني فلانٌ» means so-and-so made light of me until he deceived me for what he wants. He said:
307 - 9- يُطيع سَفيهَ القوم إذ يستفزُّه ... ويَعْصي حليماً شَيَّبَتْه الهزاهِزُ
(Gloss: "He obeys the fool of the people when he incites him, and disobeys a forbearing man whom turmoils have turned gray.")
From it the calf of a cow is called «فزّاً». The poet said:
308 - 0- كما استغاثَ بسَيْءٍ فَزُّ غَيْطَلَةٍ ... خافَ العيونَ ولم يُنْظَرْ به الحَشَكُ
(Gloss: "…as the calf of a wild cow cried out at a stream, fearing the eyes [of hunters], its udder-milk not yet awaited.")
[Translator's note: this verse is difficult in the source text, and the gloss is tentative.] The original sense of «الفَزّ» is cutting; one says «تَفَزَّز الثوبُ», i.e. the garment was torn to pieces.
His saying: «وأَجْلِبْ», i.e. gather against them hosts from your soldiers. One says «أَجْلَبَ عليه» and «جَلَبَ», i.e. he gathered hosts against him. It is also said «أَجْلَبَ عليه» means he threatened him with evil; and it is said «أَجْلَبَ عليه» means he helped; and «أجلب» means he cried out loudly, from which comes «الجَلَبَة», i.e. clamor.
His saying: «وَرَجِلِك»: Ḥafṣ read it with kasra on the jīm and the rest with sukūn. In Ḥafṣ's reading, «رَجِل» means «رَجُل» with ḍamma, in the sense of «راجل» (pedestrian); one says «رَجِلَ يَرْجَلُ» when one becomes on foot; so it is like «حَذِر» and «حَذُر», «نَدِس» and «نَدُس», and it is a singular intended as a plural. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: it is an adjective; one says «فلان يمشي رَجِلاً» when he is not riding, and of it is the poet's saying:
308 - 1- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . رَجِلاً إلا بأصحابي
I say: He is alluding to the well-known verse, which is:
فما أُقاتلُ عن ديني على فَرَسي ... إلا كذا رَجِلاً إلا بأصحابي
(Gloss: "I do not fight for my religion on my horse, only thus, on foot, except with my companions" [i.e. "neither mounted nor on foot"].) He meant: neither a horseman nor a footman.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "on the basis that faʿil has the sense of fāʿil, as in «تَعِب» and «تاعب»; its meaning is: 'and your gathering of the footmen'; and its jīm may also take ḍamma, so it is like «حَذُر» and «حَذِر», «نَدُس» and «نَدِس», and other sisters of theirs."
As for the reading of the rest, it admits being a lightening of «رَجِل» with kasra or ḍamma on the jīm; the well-known view is that it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) for «راجِل», like «رَكْب» and «صَحْب» for «راكِب» and «صاحِب». Al-Akhfash makes this type a true plural.
ʿIkrima read «ورِجالك», the plural of «رَجِل» in the sense of «راجِل», or the plural of «راجِل», like «قائم» and «قيام». It has also been read «ورُجَّالك» with ḍamma on the rāʾ and tashdīd on the jīm, which is a plural of «راجِل», like «ضارِب» and «ضُرَّاب».
The bāʾ in «بخَيْلِك» may be circumstantial, i.e. "accompanied by your cavalry," or it may be redundant, as in the saying:
308 - 2- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . لا يَقْرَأْنَ بالسُّوَر
(Gloss: "…they do not recite the sūras [lit. 'with the sūras'].")
which has preceded in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.
His saying: {وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ الشيطان}: an instance of iltifāt and of placing the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, since had it followed the course of the earlier discourse, it would have said «وما تَعِدُهم» with the second-person tāʾ.
His saying: {إِلاَّ غُرُوراً}: there are several analyses. The first: it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, and is itself a maṣdar; the original: "except a deceiving promise," so what applies in «رجلٌ عَدْلٌ» applies here, i.e. "except a promise having deception," or for intensity, or "a deceiving promise," the deception being attributed to it figuratively. The second: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. "whatever he promises them of false hopes, he promises only for the sake of deception." The third: it is a direct object by extension (ittisāʿ), i.e. "he promises them nothing but deception itself."

semin-durr:67-67.t: His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ إِيَّاهُ}: there are two analyses. The first: it is a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because it was not included in what was mentioned, since what is meant by that is their gods besides Allah. The second: it is continuous, because they used to take refuge with their gods and with Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:68-68.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَفَأَمِنْتُمْ}: an interrogative of reproach and rebuke. Al-Zamakhsharī, by his rule, implied an element to which it is conjoined, i.e. "Did you escape, and so feel secure?"
His saying: {جَانِبَ البر}: there are two analyses, the more apparent being that it is a direct object, like His saying: {فَخَسَفْنَا بِهِ وَبِدَارِهِ الأرض} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 81]. The second: it is accusative as an adverbial. «بكم» may be circumstantial, i.e. "with you," or causal. It is said: his swallowing it up because of them does not necessarily entail their perishing. The answer is that the meaning is "the side of the land in which you are," so their perishing follows from His swallowing it up; and were it not for this implication there would be no benefit in the threat.
His saying: {أَن يَخْسِفَ}, «أو يُرْسِلَ», «أن يُعِيْدَكم», «فَيُرْسِلَ», «فَيُغرْقكم»: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read all of these with the nūn of grandeur, and the rest read them with the yāʾ of the third person. The first reading is by way of iltifāt from the third person in His saying {رَّبُّكُمُ} [al-Isrāʾ: 66] to another; the second reading follows the course of the third person mentioned earlier.
His saying: «حاصِباً», i.e. "a pelting wind"; He did not make it feminine, either because it is figuratively [feminine], or by attribution, i.e. "possessing pelting." «الحَصْب» is throwing pebbles, which are small stones. Al-Farazdaq said:
308 - 3- مُسْتَقْبِلين شَمالَ الشامِ تَضْرِبُهم ... حَصْباءُ مثلُ نَدِيْفِ القُطْنِ مَنْثُورِ
(Gloss: "Facing the north wind of Syria, pelted by pebbles like scattered carded cotton.")
«الحاصِب» is also the cloud that throws hail.

semin-durr:69-69.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَمْ أَمِنْتُمْ}: it may be the connected «أم» (muttaṣila), i.e. "which of the two matters is the case?"; it may be the disconnected one (munqaṭiʿa); and {أَن يُعِيدَكُمْ} is a direct object, like {أَن يَخْسِفَ}.
His saying «تارةً» means "once" and "a turn," so it is a maṣdar, and is pluralized as «تِيَرٍ» and «تاراتٍ». The poet said:
308 - 4- وإنسانُ عيني يَحْسِرُ الماءُ تارةً ... فَيَبْدُ وتارات يَجُمُّ فَيَغْرَقُ
(Gloss: "The pupil of my eye: at times the water recedes from it and it appears, and at times it fills and is submerged.")
Its alif may be from wāw or yāʾ. Al-Rāghib said: "It is, it is said, from «تارَ الجُرْحُ», the wound healed."
His saying: «قاصِفاً»: «القاصِف» may be from the transitive «قَصَفَ»; one says «قَصَفَتِ الريحُ الشجرَ تَقْصِفها قَصْفاً» (the wind broke the trees). Abū Tammām said:
308 - 5- إنَّ الرياحَ إذا ما أَعْصَفتْ قَصَفَتْ ... عَيْدانَ نَجْدٍ ولم يَعْبَأْنَ بالرَّتَمِ
(Gloss: "When the winds blow violently they break the tall palms of Najd and pay no heed to the broom shrubs.")
So the meaning is that it finds nothing but breaks and shatters it. The second: it is from the intransitive «قَصِفَ», i.e. it came to have a crash («قَصِيف»); one says «قَصِفَتِ الريحُ تَقْصَفُ», i.e. it made a sound. {مِّنَ الريح} is an adjective.
His saying: {بِمَا كَفَرْتُمْ}: «ما» may be maṣdarī (verbal-noun forming), and may mean «الذي»; the bāʾ is causal, i.e. "because of your disbelief," or "because of that which you disbelieved in"; then it was extended, so the bāʾ was dropped and the verb reached the pronoun; this was needed only because the attachment differs.
Abū Jaʿfar and Mujāhid read «فَتُغْرِقَكم» with the tāʾ (the two-dotted tāʾ from above), the verb being predicated of the pronoun of the wind. In the Shaykh's book: "«فتُغْرِقَكم» with the tāʾ of address, predicated of «الريح». Al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ [read] with yāʾ of the third person, fatḥa on the ghayn and tashdīd on the rāʾ, making it transitive by doubling, and the reciter (al-muqriʾ) for Abū Jaʿfar likewise, except with the tāʾ of address." I say: This is either an oversight or a corruption by copyists; how can he say "the tāʾ of address" when it is predicated of the pronoun of the wind? It seems he meant "the tāʾ of the feminine," and his pen slipped, or someone else corrupted it for him.
The majority read «الريحِ» in the singular, and Abū Jaʿfar read «الرياح» in the plural.
His saying: {بِهِ تَبِيعاً}: «به» may be attached to «تَجِدوا», or to «تبيع», or to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «تبيع». «التَّبِيْع» is the one who demands a right, the one who sticks to [the debtor]. Al-Shammākh said:
308 - 6- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كما لاذَ الغَريمُ من التَّبيعِ
(Gloss: "…as the debtor takes refuge from the pursuing creditor.")
And another said:
308 - 7- غَدَوْا وغَدَتْ غِزْلانُهم فكأنَّها ... ضوامِنُ مِنْ غُرْمٍ لهنَّ تَبيعُ
(Gloss: "They set out in the morning, and their gazelles set out, as if they were guarantors for a debt, each with a pursuer.")

semin-durr:70-70.t: His saying, the Exalted: {كَرَّمْنَا بَنِي آدَمَ}: He made it transitive by doubling; it is from «كَرُم» with ḍamma, like «شَرُف», and what is meant by nobility (karam) is not generosity with wealth.

semin-durr:71-71.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يَوْمَ نَدْعُواْ}: there are several analyses. The first: it is accusative as an adverbial, the governor being «فَضَّلْناهم», i.e. "We preferred them with reward on the day We call." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said in establishing it: "That is because the preference of mankind over the rest of the animals on the Day of Resurrection is clear, since they are the ones charged with obligations, favored, held to account, who have standing. But this is refuted by the fact that the disbelievers on that day are the greatest losers of all animals, because of their saying {ياليتني كُنتُ تُرَاباً} [al-Naba': 40]."
The second: it is accusative as an adverbial, the governor in it being «اذكر»; so said al-Ḥawfī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya. I say: This is an oversight; how can it govern it as an adverbial? Rather it is an object.
The third: it is nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ, and it is built only because of its annexation to a verbal clause, with the clause after it as the khabar. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said in establishing it: "It is valid that «يوم» be accusative by construction (building), since it is annexed to something not firmly established, and its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, its khabar being in the division that comes after it, in His saying {فَمَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ} up to His saying {وَمَن كَانَ}." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "His saying 'accusative by construction' should have been 'built on the fatḥa'; and his saying 'since it is annexed to something not firmly established' is not good, because 'firmly established' and 'not firmly established' apply to nouns and not to verbs, and this is annexed to an imperfect verb; and the school of the Basrans is that it is declinable, while the Kufans permit its being built. And his saying 'the khabar is in the division' etc.: the division has no link connecting the clause of the division with the mubtadaʾ." I say: The link is omitted because it is known, i.e. «فَمَنْ أُوتي كتابَه فيه».
The fourth: it is accusative by His saying «ثم لا تجدوا»; so said al-Zajjāj. The fifth: it is accusative by an implied «يُعيدكم», i.e. "He will bring you back on the day We call." The sixth: it is accusative by what {وَلاَ يُظْلَمُونَ} after it indicates, i.e. "and they will not be wronged on the day We call"; so said Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū l-Baqāʾ. The seventh: it is accusative by what {متى هُوَ} [al-Isrāʾ: 51] indicates. The eighth: it is accusative by what preceded it of His saying, the Exalted: {فَتَسْتَجِيبُونَ بِحَمْدِهِ} [al-Isrāʾ: 52]. The ninth: it is a badal of {يَوْمَ يَدْعُوكُمْ} [al-Isrāʾ: 52]. These last two views are very weak because of the many intervening elements. The tenth: it is a direct object with an implied «اذكر»; this, though the easiest of the implications, is more apparent than the preceding, since there is no remoteness in it and not much implying.
The majority read «نَدْعو» with the nūn of grandeur; Mujāhid read «يَدْعُو» with the yāʾ of the third person, i.e. Allah the Exalted or the angel. «كلَّ» is accusative as a direct object on both readings.
Al-Ḥasan read, in what al-Dānī reported from him, «يُدْعَى» as a passive, with «كلُّ» nominative as the deputy agent; and in what others reported from him, «يُدْعَو» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the ʿayn, followed by a wāw. It has been derived in two ways. The first: the original is «يُدْعَوْن», and the nūn of the nominative was dropped, as it was dropped in his saying, peace be upon him: "You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another," and in the saying:
308 - 8- أَبَيْتُ أَسْرِيْ وتَبِْيْتي تَدْلُكِيْ ... وَجْهَكِ بالعَنْبَرِ والمِسْكِ الذَّكي
(Gloss: "I spend the night journeying while you spend the night rubbing your face with ambergris and fragrant musk.")
and «كلٌّ» is nominative as a badal of the wāw that is a pronoun, or as the agent, with the wāw a mere sign, in the dialect of «يتعاقبون فيكمْ ملائكةٌ» ("angels take turns among you").
The second derivation: the original is «يُدْعَى», as al-Dānī reported from him, except that he turned the alif into a wāw in pause, which is the dialect of some people, who say «هذه أفْعَوْ وعَصَوْ», meaning «أَفْعى» and «عَصا», and then treated the connection like the pause. «كلُّ» is nominative on this only as standing in the place of the agent.
His saying: «بإمامِهم»: the bāʾ may be attached to the calling, i.e. "by the name of their imām," or it may be circumstantial, attached to an omitted element, i.e. "We call them accompanied by their record." «الإمام» is the one who is followed. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Among the innovations of exegeses is that «الإمام» is the plural of «أُمّ» (mother), and that people will be called on the Day of Resurrection by their mothers rather than their fathers, and that the wisdom in it is regard for the right of ʿĪsā, showing the nobility of al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, and that the children of fornication not be disgraced." He said: "I wish I knew which is the greater innovation: the soundness of its wording or the splendor of its meaning?"
I say: He is excused, because «أُمّ» is not pluralized as «إمام»; this is the statement of one who does not know the craft nor the language of the Arabs. As for the meaning they mentioned, Allah the Exalted called ʿĪsā by his name annexed to his mother in several places, as in {ياعيسى ابن مَرْيَمَ} [al-Māʾida: 110], and reported of him likewise, as in {وَإِذْ قَالَ عِيسَى ابن مَرْيَمَ} [al-Ṣaff: 6]; and in that there is a slight upon the Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him and honor his face.
His saying: {فَمَنْ أُوتِيَ}: it may be conditional, and it may be relative, with the fāʾ because of its resemblance to a condition. It is construed by form first in His saying {أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ}, so it is singular, and by meaning second in His saying «فأولئك», so it is plural.

semin-durr:72-72.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَن كَانَ فِي هذه}: what is permitted for «مَنْ» is what was permitted for the «مَنْ» before it. The two companions [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Abū Bakr [Shuʿba] applied imāla to «أعمى» in both places in this sūra; Abū ʿAmr applied imāla to the first and not the second; and the rest pronounced both with fatḥa. The imāla is because both are of the yāʾ-type (dhawāt al-yāʾ); the full pronunciation (tafkhīm) is because it is the original. As for Abū ʿAmr, he applied imāla to the first because it is not an elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl), so its alif is final in form and in implication, and final positions are generally the place of change; as for the second, it is an elative, and for this reason «وأَضَلَّ» is conjoined to it, so its alif is in the ruling of a medial one, because the preposition «مِن» for the one surpassed is as if pronounced, and it is very closely connected to the elative, so it is as if it occurred in the middle, and was protected from change.
I say: This is how al-Fārisī and al-Zamakhsharī established it. It has been rejected, in that they applied imāla in {وَلاَ أدنى مِن ذَلِكَ} [al-Mujādila: 7] despite the explicit «مِن»; so they should the more readily apply imāla to «أَعْمى» with «مِن» implied with it.
As for «أَعْمى» in [Sūrat] Ṭāhā, the two companions and Abū ʿAmr applied imāla to it, but Abū Bakr did not, although he applies it here; it is as if he combined the two matters, being bound by following the transmission. Some distinguished: «أعمى» in Ṭāhā is of blindness of the eyes, and in al-Isrāʾ of blindness of insight; for that reason they interpreted it here as ignorance, so imāla was applied here and not there, for the difference between the two meanings. I say: The question remains, since someone may ask: why was this one singled out for imāla? And had the matter been reversed, the distinction would have stood.

semin-durr:73-73.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِن كَادُواْ لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ}: this «إنْ» has the two well-known views: the school of the Basrans is that it is the lightened «إنّ», and the lām is the distinguishing lām (fāriqa) between it and the negative «إنْ», which is why it entered upon a verb of the abrogating class; and the school of the Kufans is that it means the negative «ما», with the lām meaning «إلا». «يَفْتِنُونَك» is made to include the meaning of «يَصْرِفُونك» (they turn you away), which is why it is made transitive with «عن»; its implied form: "they would turn you away by their trial." «لتفترِيَ» is attached to «الفتنة».
His saying: {وَإِذاً لاَّتَّخَذُوكَ}: «إذن» is a particle of response and requital, which is why the conditional particle can occur in its place; «لاتَّخذوك» is the response to an omitted oath, its implied form: "Then, by Allah, they would surely have taken you…"; it is future in meaning, because «إذَنْ» requires futurity, since its meaning is requital. This is like His saying: {وَلَئِنْ أَرْسَلْنَا رِيحاً فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرّاً لَّظَلُّواْ} [al-Rūm: 51], i.e. «ليَظَلُّنَّ». And al-Zamakhsharī's saying "i.e. had you followed their wish they would have taken you…" is an interpretation of meaning, not of parsing; he does not intend by it that «لاتَّخذوك» is the response of an omitted «لو», as there is no need for it.

semin-durr:74-74.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {تَرْكَنُ}: the majority [read] with fatḥa on the kāf, the imperfect of «رَكِنَ» with kasra; Qatāda, Ibn Muṣarrif and Ibn Abī Isḥāq [read] «تَرْكُن» with ḍamma, the imperfect of «رَكَنَ» with fatḥa; this is from the intermingling of dialects (tadākhul), and its verification has preceded at the end of [Sūrat] Hūd.
His saying: «شيئاً»: accusative as a maṣdar, its adjective omitted, i.e. "a little inclining."

semin-durr:75-75.t: His saying, the Exalted: {ضِعْفَ الحياة}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the reality of this discourse? I say: its origin is 'We would have made you taste the punishment of life and the punishment of death'; for punishment is of two kinds, a punishment in death, which is the punishment of the grave, and a punishment in the life of the Hereafter, which is the punishment of the Fire. «الضِّعْف» is used descriptively, as in His saying, the Exalted: {فَآتِهِمْ عَذَاباً ضِعْفاً مِّنَ النار} [al-Aʿrāf: 38], meaning a doubled punishment. So the original of the discourse is: 'We would have made you taste a double punishment in life and a double punishment in death'; then the described noun was omitted and the adjective, «الضَّعْف», put in its place, and then the adjective was annexed with the annexation of the described, so it was said «ضِعْفَ الحياة» and «ضِعْفَ المماتِ», as if it had been said «أليمَ الحياةِ» and «أليم الممات»." The discussion of «إذن» and «لأَذَقْناك» is as it was in its parallel.

semin-durr:76-76.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذاً لاَّ يَلْبَثُونَ}: the majority read the verb after «إذَنْ» in the nominative with the nūn retained, and it is written so in the copies of the majority. There are three explanations for its being nominative and «إذن» not governing it. [The first:] it stands between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the basis of the two readings? I say: as for the common one, meaning with the verb nominative, the verb is conjoined in it to a verb, and it is nominative because it occurs as the khabar of «كاد», and the khabar of «كاد» takes the place of a noun." I say: So «لا يَلْبِثُون» is conjoined to His saying «لِيَسْتَفِزُّونك».
The second: it stands between an omitted oath and its response, and so is cancelled (ulghiyat) for that reason; the implied form: "and, by Allah, then they would not remain."
The third: it stands between an omitted mubtadaʾ and its khabar, and so is cancelled for that reason; the implied form: "and they would then not remain."
Ubayy read it with the nūn dropped, so its being accusative is by «إذن» according to the majority, and by an implied «أَنْ» after it according to others; in ʿAbd Allāh's codex it is «لا يَلْبَثُوا», with it dropped. The basis for the accusative is that the verb was not made conjoined to what precedes, nor a response, nor a khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "As for Ubayy's reading, in it is an independent clause, namely «إذاً لا يَلْبثوا», conjoined to the clause of His saying {وَإِن كَادُواْ لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ}."
ʿAṭāʾ read {لاَّ يَلَبَثُونَ} with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the lām and bāʾ, the bāʾ doubled, passive, from «لَبَّثَه» with tashdīd. Yaʿqūb read it likewise except that he put kasra on the bāʾ, making it active.
His saying: «خِلافَك»: the two companions [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī], Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read «خِلافَك» with kasra on the khāʾ and an alif after the lām, and the rest read it with fatḥa on the khāʾ and sukūn on the lām [«خَلْفَك»]. The two readings have one meaning. They cited in this regard:
308 - 9- عَفَتِ الديارُ خِلافَهم فكأنما ... بَسَطَ الشَّواطِبُ بينهنَّ حََصِيْراً
(Gloss: "The abodes were effaced after them, as if the palm-leaf splitters had spread a mat among them.")
And the Exalted said: {خِلاَفَ رَسُولِ الله} [al-Tawba: 81], the meaning being "after his going out." The annexation of «قبل» and «بعد» and the like to the names of entities is frequent, with an omitted muḍāf, so it is implied: from your saying «جاء زيدٌ قبل عمروٍ», i.e. before his coming.
His saying: {إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً}: it may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar or of time, i.e. "a short stay," or "except a short time."

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي أَسْرَى بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَى الَّذِي بَارَكْنَا حَوْلَهُ لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ آيَاتِنَا إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ (١)).
The discussion of (سُبْحَانَ) has already preceded in the story of Adam, peace be upon him, in al-Baqara.
And (لَيْلًا): an adverb (ẓarf) for «أَسْرَى»; its indefiniteness indicates the shortness of the time in which the Night Journey and the return took place. (حَوْلَهُ): an adverb for «بَارَكْنَا». It has also been said: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "We made good" or "We made to grow". (لِنُرِيَهُ): with the nūn, because what precedes it is an account given of the speaker; and with the yāʾ [«لِيُرِيَهُ»], because the beginning of the surah is in the third person, and likewise the end of the verse is in the third person; it ended with it, and then in its middle returned to speaking of Himself, saying «بَارَكْنَا» and «مِنْ آيَاتِنَا». The hāʾ in (إِنَّهُ) is for Allah the Exalted; it has also been said: for the Prophet ﷺ, i.e. he is the one who hears Our speech and sees Our Essence.

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَآتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ وَجَعَلْنَاهُ هُدًى لِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ أَلَّا تَتَّخِذُوا مِنْ دُونِي وَكِيلًا ذُرِّيَّةَ مَنْ حَمَلْنَا مَعَ نُوحٍ إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَبْدًا شَكُورًا (٢)).
His saying, exalted is He: (أَلَّا تَتَّخِذُوا): it is read with the yāʾ in the third person [«أَلَّا يَتَّخِذُوا»], the implied form being: "We made it a guidance so that they not take", or "We gave Moses the Book so that they not take". And it is read with the tāʾ in the second person, and there are three views on it. The first: «أَنْ» means «أَيْ» (that is), and it is explicative (mufassira) of the command and prohibition that the Book contains.
The second: «أَنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "We said: do not take".
The third: «لَا» is redundant, the implied form being: "for fear that you take"; in this it has turned from the third person to the second person. And «تَتَّخِذُوا» here takes two objects. One of them is «وَكِيلًا»; regarding the second there are two views. The first: it is «ذُرِّيَّةَ», the implied form being: "do not take the descendants of those We carried as a guardian (وَكِيلًا)", i.e. a lord, or one to whom matters are entrusted. And «مِنْ دُونِي» may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «وَكِيل», or governed by it, or attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تَتَّخِذُوا». The second view: the second object is «مِنْ دُونِي». On this view there are three views regarding «ذُرِّيَّة». The first: it is vocative (munādā). The second: it is accusative by an implied «أَعْنِي» (I mean). The third: it is a badal (substitute) from «وَكِيل», or a badal from «مُوسَى», peace be upon him.
It was read irregularly (shādhdh) with the nominative [«ذُرِّيَّةُ»], on the implied form "it is the descendants", or as a badal from the pronoun in «يَتَّخِذُوا» on the reading with the yāʾ, since they are absent (third person).
And (مَنْ) means «الَّذِي», or is an indefinite noun qualified by a description (nakira mawṣūfa).

ukberi-tibyan:4-5.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَضَيْنَا إِلَى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ فِي الْكِتَابِ لَتُفْسِدُنَّ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَّتَيْنِ وَلَتَعْلُنَّ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا (٤) فَإِذَا جَاءَ وَعْدُ أُولَاهُمَا بَعَثْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ عِبَادًا لَنَا أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ فَجَاسُوا خِلَالَ الدِّيَارِ وَكَانَ وَعْدًا مَفْعُولًا (٥)).
His saying, exalted is He: (لَتُفْسِدُنَّ): it is read with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the sīn, from «أَفْسَدَ», the object being omitted, i.e. the religions, or the people. And it is read with ḍamma on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the sīn [«لَتُفْسَدُنَّ»], i.e. "and others will corrupt you".
And it is read with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the sīn [«لَتَفْسُدُنَّ»], i.e. "your affairs will become corrupt". (مَرَّتَيْنِ): a maṣdar (verbal noun), and what governs it is not from its own root. (وَعْدُ أُولَاهُمَا): i.e. what was promised for the first of the two times, i.e. what they were promised at the first time.
(عِبَادًا لَنَا): with the alif, which is the well-known reading. And it is read «عَبِيدًا», which is a rare plural; only a few words have come in it.
(فَجَاسُوا): with the jīm; and it is read with the ḥāʾ [«فَحَاسُوا»], the meaning being the same. (وَخِلَالَ): an adverb (ẓarf) for it. And it is read «خَلَلَ الدِّيَارِ» without an alif; it has been said: it is the singular, the plural being «خِلَال», like «جَبَل» and «جِبَال». (وَكَانَ): the noun of «كَانَ» is the pronoun of the maṣdar, i.e. "and the ravaging (الْجَوْسُ) was …".

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَا لَكُمُ الْكَرَّةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَمْدَدْنَاكُمْ بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ أَكْثَرَ نَفِيرًا (٦)).
His saying, exalted is He: (الْكَرَّةَ): it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun); one says: «كَرَّ كَرًّا وَكَرَّةً» (he returned to the attack).
And (عَلَيْهِمْ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to «رَدَدْنَا». It has also been said: to «الْكَرَّة», because one says «كَرَّ عَلَيْهِ». It has also been said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْكَرَّة».
(نَفِيرًا): a tamyīz (specification); it is of the pattern faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil, i.e. those who march out with you; it is a noun for a group.
It has also been said: it is the plural of «نَفْر», like «عَبْد» and «عَبِيد».

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَهَا فَإِذَا جَاءَ وَعْدُ الْآخِرَةِ لِيَسُوءُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ وَلِيَدْخُلُوا الْمَسْجِدَ كَمَا دَخَلُوهُ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَلِيُتَبِّرُوا مَا عَلَوْا تَتْبِيرًا (٧)).
His saying, exalted is He: (وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَهَا): it has been said: the lām means «عَلَى» (against), as in His saying: (وَعَلَيْهَا مَا اكْتَسَبَتْ).
It has also been said: it keeps its basic meaning, and this is the correct view, because the lām is for specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), and the doer is specifically assigned the recompense of his deed, its good and its evil.
(وَعْدُ الْآخِرَةِ): i.e. the last return (al-karra).
(لِيَسُوءُوا): with the yāʾ and the plural pronoun, i.e. so that the servants, or the marching host, may disgrace [your faces].
And it is read likewise but without the wāw [«لِيَسُوءَ»], i.e. so that the sending, or the one sent, or Allah may disgrace. And it is read with the nūn likewise [«لِنَسُوءَ»]. And it is read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the sīn, with a yāʾ after it and fatḥa on the hamza [«لِيُسِيئَ»], i.e. so that it may make your faces ugly.
(مَا عَلَوْا): accusative by «يُتَبِّرُوا», i.e. "and so that they may destroy their height and what they rose over". It may also be an adverb (ẓarf).

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (عَسَى رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ يَرْحَمَكُمْ وَإِنْ عُدْتُمْ عُدْنَا وَجَعَلْنَا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكَافِرِينَ حَصِيرًا (٨)).
His saying, exalted is He: (حَصِيرًا): i.e. «حَاصِرًا» (confining); it was not made feminine, because faʿīl here is in the sense of fāʿil.
It has also been said: the masculine is on the sense of the genus. It has also been said: it was made masculine because the femininity of «جَهَنَّم» is not real (ghayr ḥaqīqī).

ukberi-tibyan:9-10.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ وَيُبَشِّرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ الصَّالِحَاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا كَبِيرًا (٩) وَأَنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ أَعْتَدْنَا لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا (١٠)).
His saying, exalted is He: (أَنَّ لَهُمْ): i.e. «بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ» (with [the good news] that for them …).
And (أَنَّ الَّذِينَ): conjoined to it, i.e. He gives the believers good news of the two matters.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيَدْعُ الْإِنْسَانُ بِالشَّرِّ دُعَاءَهُ بِالْخَيْرِ وَكَانَ الْإِنْسَانُ عَجُولًا (١١)).
His saying, exalted is He: (دُعَاءَهُ): i.e. he calls for evil a calling like his calling for good; the maṣdar (verbal noun) is in a genitive construct with the fāʿil (agent). The implied meaning is: he seeks evil; so the bāʾ is for the ḥāl (circumstance), and it may also be in the sense of cause.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ آيَتَيْنِ فَمَحَوْنَا آيَةَ اللَّيْلِ وَجَعَلْنَا آيَةَ النَّهَارِ مُبْصِرَةً لِتَبْتَغُوا فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَلِتَعْلَمُوا عَدَدَ السِّنِينَ وَالْحِسَابَ وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَصَّلْنَاهُ تَفْصِيلًا (١٢)).
His saying, exalted is He: (آيَتَيْنِ): it has been said: the implied form is "possessors of two signs (ذَوِي آيَتَيْنِ)", and this is indicated by His saying «آيَةَ اللَّيْلِ» and «آيَةَ النَّهَارِ».
It has also been said: there is no omission in it; the night and the day are two signs, and they indicate something else; for that reason He used a genitive construct in one place and a description in another.
His saying, exalted is He: (وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ): accusative by an omitted verb, because it is conjoined to a noun on which a verb has acted; were it not for that, it would be preferable to make it nominative. Similar to it is: (وَكُلَّ إِنْسَانٍ).

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَكُلَّ إِنْسَانٍ أَلْزَمْنَاهُ طَائِرَهُ فِي عُنُقِهِ وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ كِتَابًا يَلْقَاهُ مَنْشُورًا (١٣)).
His saying, exalted is He: (نُخْرِجُ): it is read with ḍamma on the nūn; and it is read with a yāʾ with ḍamma [«يُخْرَجُ»], and with a yāʾ with fatḥa and ḍamma on the rāʾ [«يَخْرُجُ»].
And (كِتَابًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) on this [view], i.e. "and We bring out his omen", or "his deed, written".
And (يَلْقَاهُ): an adjective (ṣifa) of «الْكِتَاب»; and (مَنْشُورًا): a ḥāl from the pronoun «الْمَنُوب» [Translator's note: so written in the source; probably a misprint for «الْمَنْصُوب», i.e. the accusative pronoun in «يَلْقَاهُ»]. It may also be a naʿt (adjective) of «الْكِتَاب».

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (اقْرَأْ كِتَابَكَ كَفَى بِنَفْسِكَ الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيبًا (١٤)).
His saying, exalted is He: (اقْرَأْ): i.e. it will be said [to him].

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا أَرَدْنَا أَنْ نُهْلِكَ قَرْيَةً أَمَرْنَا مُتْرَفِيهَا فَفَسَقُوا فِيهَا فَحَقَّ عَلَيْهَا الْقَوْلُ فَدَمَّرْنَاهَا تَدْمِيرًا (١٦٥)).
His saying, exalted is He: (أَمَرْنَا): it is read short and without doubling, i.e. We commanded them to obey. It has also been said: We multiplied their blessings, and in this it has the meaning of the reading with the long vowel [«آمَرْنَا»].
And it is read with doubling and short [«أَمَّرْنَا»], i.e. We made them rulers. It has also been said: it has the meaning of the lengthened form, because it is sometimes made transitive with the hamza and sometimes with doubling; and the intransitive from it is «أَمِرَ الْقَوْمُ», i.e. the people became many.
And (أَمَرْنَا): the answer (jawāb) of «إِذَا». It has also been said: the clause is accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «قَرْيَة», and the answer is omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِنَ الْقُرُونِ مِنْ بَعْدِ نُوحٍ وَكَفَى بِرَبِّكَ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا بَصِيرًا (١٧)).
His saying, exalted is He: (وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا): «كَمْ» here is declarative (khabariyya), in the position of the accusative by «أَهْلَكْنَا».
(مِنَ الْقُرُونِ): its parallel was mentioned in His saying: (كَمْ آتَيْنَاهُمْ مِنْ آيَةٍ).

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ الْعَاجِلَةَ عَجَّلْنَا لَهُ فِيهَا مَا نَشَاءُ لِمَنْ نُرِيدُ ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَاهَا مَذْمُومًا مَدْحُورًا (١٨)).
His saying, exalted is He: (مَنْ كَانَ): «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is conditional; and «عَجَّلْنَا» is its apodosis (jawāb).
(لِمَنْ نُرِيدُ): it is a badal (substitute) from «لَهُ», with repetition of the preposition.
(يَصْلَاهَا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جَهَنَّمَ», or from the hāʾ in «لَهُ».
And (مَذْمُومًا): a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) in «يَصْلَى».

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَنْ أَرَادَ الْآخِرَةَ وَسَعَى لَهَا سَعْيَهَا وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَأُولَئِكَ كَانَ سَعْيُهُمْ مَشْكُورًا (١٩)).
His saying, exalted is He: (سَعْيَهَا): it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because the meaning is "he did its deed",
and «لَهَا» means "for its sake"; or it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كُلًّا نُمِدُّ هَؤُلَاءِ وَهَؤُلَاءِ مِنْ عَطَاءِ رَبِّكَ وَمَا كَانَ عَطَاءُ رَبِّكَ مَحْظُورًا (٢٠)).
His saying, exalted is He: (كُلًّا): it is accusative by «نُمِدُّ», the implied form being: "each party".
And (هَؤُلَاءِ وَهَؤُلَاءِ): a badal (substitute) from «كُلّ». And «مِنْ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «نُمِدُّ».
And «الْعَطَاءُ» is a noun for what is given.

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (انْظُرْ كَيْفَ فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ وَلَلْآخِرَةُ أَكْبَرُ دَرَجَاتٍ وَأَكْبَرُ تَفْضِيلًا (٢١)).
His saying, exalted is He: (كَيْفَ): accusative by «فَضَّلْنَا», as a ḥāl (circumstantial) or as an adverb (ẓarf).

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَضَى رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِنْدَكَ الْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَا أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُلْ لَهُمَا أُفٍّ وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا وَقُلْ لَهُمَا قَوْلًا كَرِيمًا (٢٣)).
His saying, exalted is He: (أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا): «أَنْ» may mean «أَيْ» (that is), being explicative (mufassira) of the meaning of «قَضَى», and «لَا» is a prohibition.
It may also be in the position of the accusative, i.e. "your Lord made obligatory the worship of Him", with «لَا» redundant (zāʾida).
It may also be that «قَضَى» means «أَمَرَ» (commanded), the implied form being: "that you not worship (بِأَنْ لَا تَعْبُدُوا)".
His saying, exalted is He: (وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا): it has been mentioned in al-Baqara.
(إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ): «إِنْ» is conditional and «مَا» is redundant for tawkīd (emphasis); «يَبْلُغَنَّ» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jazāʾ) is «فَلَا تَقُلْ».
And it is read «يَبْلُغَانِّ», the alif being the fāʿil (agent).
And (أَحَدُهُمَا أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا): a badal (substitute) from it. Abū ʿAlī said: it is a tawkīd (emphasis).
It is also possible that «أَحَدُهُمَا» is nominative by an omitted verb, i.e. "if one of them or both of them reaches"; its benefit is also emphasis.
It is also possible that the alif is a particle of the dual, and the fāʿil is «أَحَدُهُمَا».
(أُفٍّ): a verbal noun (ism fiʿl), and its meaning is irritation and dislike. The meaning is: do not say to them "Stop!" or "Leave off!".
It has also been said: it is a noun standing for a declarative clause, i.e. "I am averse to" or "I am weary of humouring you two".
Whoever reads it with kasra makes it indeclinable on the base; whoever reads it with fatḥa seeks lightness, like «رُبَ»; whoever reads it with ḍamma makes it follow [the preceding vowel]; whoever gives it nunation intends indefiniteness, and whoever does not intends definiteness; and whoever lightens the fāʾ drops one of the two identical letters for lightness.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ الذُّلِّ مِنَ الرَّحْمَةِ وَقُلْ رَبِّي ارْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرًا (٢٤)).
His saying, exalted is He: (جَنَاحَ الذُّلِّ): with ḍamma, which is the opposite of might; and with kasra [«الذِّلِّ»], which is compliance, the opposite of difficulty.
(مِنَ الرَّحْمَةِ): i.e. on account of your gentleness to them; so «مِنْ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «اخْفِضْ». It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جَنَاح».
(كَمَا): a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a mercy like their mercy".

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ ابْتِغَاءَ رَحْمَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكَ تَرْجُوهَا فَقُلْ لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَيْسُورًا (٢٨)).
His saying, exalted is He: (ابْتِغَاءَ رَحْمَةٍ): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(تَرْجُوهَا): it may be a description of «الرَّحْمَة», or a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent).
And (مِنْ رَبِّكَ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تَرْجُوهَا»; it may also be an adjective (ṣifa) of «رَحْمَة».

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلَى عُنُقِكَ وَلَا تَبْسُطْهَا كُلَّ الْبَسْطِ فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُومًا مَحْسُورًا (٢٩)).
His saying, exalted is He: (كُلَّ الْبَسْطِ): accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)], because it is in a genitive construct with it.

ukberi-tibyan:31-32.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا أَوْلَادَكُمْ خَشْيَةَ إِمْلَاقٍ نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُهُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ إِنَّ قَتْلَهُمْ كَانَ خِطْئًا كَبِيرًا (٣١) وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا الزِّنَا إِنَّهُ كَانَ فَاحِشَةً وَسَاءَ سَبِيلًا (٣٢)).
His saying, exalted is He: (خَطَأً): it is read with kasra on the khāʾ, sukūn on the ṭāʾ, and the hamza [«خِطْئًا»], and it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «خَطِئَ», like «عَلِمَ عِلْمًا».
And with kasra on the khāʾ and fatḥa on the ṭāʾ, without hamza [«خِطًا»]; there are three views on it.
The first: it is a maṣdar, like «شَبِعَ شِبَعًا», except that the hamza was replaced by an alif in the maṣdar, and by a yāʾ in the verb because of the kasra before it. The second: the vowel of the hamza was thrown onto the ṭāʾ, so it took fatḥa, and the hamza was dropped. The third: the hamza was lightened by changing it into an alif irregularly, so the ṭāʾ took fatḥa.
And it is read likewise but with the hamza [«خِطَأً»], like «عِنَب».
And it is read with fatḥa and the hamza [«خَطَأً»], like «نَصَب», and this is frequent. And it is read with kasra and the long vowel [«خِطَاءً»], like «قَامَ قِيَامًا».
(الزِّنَا): most use the short form; the long form is a dialectal variant, and it has been read with it.
It has also been said: it [the long form] is the maṣdar of «زَانَى», like «قَاتَلَ قِتَالًا», because it occurs between two parties.

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَمَنْ قُتِلَ مَظْلُومًا فَقَدْ جَعَلْنَا لِوَلِيِّهِ سُلْطَانًا فَلَا يُسْرِفْ فِي الْقَتْلِ إِنَّهُ كَانَ مَنْصُورًا (٣٣)).
His saying, exalted is He: (فَلَا يُسْرِفْ): the majority read with sukūn, because it is a prohibition.
And it was read with ḍamma on the fāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the ḍamma is evidently on the final letter, «يُسْرِفُ»], as a statement whose meaning is a prohibition.
And it is read with the yāʾ, the fāʿil (agent) being the pronoun of the guardian (al-walī). And with the tāʾ [«تُسْرِفْ»], i.e. do not be excessive, O you who exact retaliation, or you who initiate killing, i.e. do not be excessive by engaging in killing. It has also been said: the implied form is "it is said to him: do not be excessive".
(إِنَّهُ): there are six views on the hāʾ. The first: it refers back to the guardian. The second: to the one killed. The third: to the blood. The fourth: to the killing.
The fifth: to the right.
The sixth: to the killer, i.e. when he is killed [in retaliation], the punishment for killing is lifted from him in the Hereafter.

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَأَوْفُوا بِالْعَهْدِ إِنَّ الْعَهْدَ كَانَ مَسْئُولًا (٣٤)).
His saying, exalted is He: (إِنَّ الْعَهْدَ كَانَ مَسْئُولًا): there are two views on it.
The first: its implied form is "the possessor of the covenant", i.e. he will be questioned about his covenant. The second: the pronoun refers back to the covenant, and the questioning is attributed to it figuratively, as in His saying, exalted is He: (وَإِذَا الْمَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ). Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَوْفُوا الْكَيْلَ إِذَا كِلْتُمْ وَزِنُوا بِالْقِسْطَاسِ الْمُسْتَقِيمِ ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَحْسَنُ تَأْوِيلًا (٣٥)).
His saying, exalted is He: (بِالْقِسْطَاسِ): it is read with ḍamma on the qāf and with kasra; they are two dialectal forms.
And (تَأْوِيلًا): in the sense of "outcome" (مَآلًا).

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُولَئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا (٣٦)).
His saying, exalted is He: (وَلَا تَقْفُ): its past tense is «قَفَا», meaning "he followed". And it is read with ḍamma on the qāf and sukūn on the fāʾ [«وَلَا تَقُفْ»], like «تَقُمْ»; its past tense is «قَافَ يَقُوفُ», also meaning "he followed".
(كُلُّ): a mubtadaʾ (subject). «أُولَئِكَ» points to the hearing, the sight and the heart; they were pointed to with «أُولَئِكَ», though it is mostly for rational beings, because it is the plural of «ذَا», and «ذَا» is for rational and non-rational beings alike; and it came in poetry:
بَعْدَ أُولَئِكَ الْأَيَّامِ
(after those days)
And (كَانَ) with what it governs is the khabar (predicate). The noun of «كَانَ» refers back to «كُلّ»; the hāʾ in «عَنْهُ» also refers back to «كُلّ»; «عَنْ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «مَسْئُول»; and the pronoun in «مَسْئُول» is also for «كُلّ». The meaning is: the hearing will be questioned about itself, figuratively.
It is also possible that the pronoun in «كَانَ» is for the owner of these organs, since they indicate him.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «عَنْهُ» is in the position of the nominative by «مَسْئُول» [i.e. as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)], as in His saying: (غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ). This is a mistake, because the preposition and its genitive noun are made to stand in the place of the fāʿil (agent) when the verb, or what stands in its place, precedes. When it comes after, that is not valid, because a noun that precedes the verb becomes a mubtadaʾ, and a preposition that is required [by the verb] cannot be a mubtadaʾ. Its parallel is your saying: «بِزَيْدٍ انْطَلَقَ». What shows you this is that if you made it dual you would not say «بِالزَّيْدَيْنِ انْطَلَقَا». Rather, the correct analysis of the question is to make the pronoun in «مَسْئُولًا» refer to the maṣdar (verbal noun); then «عَنْهُ» is in the position of the accusative, just as it is construed in your saying «بِزَيْدٍ انْطَلَقَ».

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تَمْشِ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَحًا إِنَّكَ لَنْ تَخْرِقَ الْأَرْضَ وَلَنْ تَبْلُغَ الْجِبَالَ طُولًا (٣٧)).
His saying, exalted is He: (مَرَحًا): with kasra on the rāʾ [«مَرِحًا»] it is a ḥāl (circumstantial); with fatḥa it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl, or a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose).
(تَخْرِقَ): with kasra on the rāʾ and with ḍamma; two dialectal forms.
(طُولًا): a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) or from the object.
It may also be a tamyīz (specification), a mafʿūl lahu, or a maṣdar from the meaning of «تَبْلُغَ».

ukberi-tibyan:38-38.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كُلُّ ذَلِكَ كَانَ سَيِّئُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ مَكْرُوهًا (٣٨)).
His saying, exalted is He: (سَيِّئُهُ): it is read in the feminine and the accusative [«سَيِّئَةً»], i.e. all the prohibited things that have been mentioned; and «مَكْرُوهًا» is masculine following the wording of «كُلّ», or because the femininity is not real (ghayr ḥaqīqī).
And it is read in the nominative with the genitive construct [«سَيِّئُهُ»], i.e. the evil of what has been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ذَلِكَ مِمَّا أَوْحَى إِلَيْكَ رَبُّكَ مِنَ الْحِكْمَةِ وَلَا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ فَتُلْقَى فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَلُومًا مَدْحُورًا (٣٩)).
His saying, exalted is He: (مِنَ الْحِكْمَةِ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أَوْحَى»; or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted returning pronoun; or a badal (substitute) from «مَا أَوْحَى».

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَفَأَصْفَاكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ بِالْبَنِينَ وَاتَّخَذَ مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ إِنَاثًا إِنَّكُمْ لَتَقُولُونَ قَوْلًا عَظِيمًا (٤٠)).
His saying, exalted is He: (أَصْفَاكُمْ): the alif is a replacement of a wāw, because it is from «الصَّفْوَة» (the choice part).
(إِنَاثًا): the first object of «اتَّخَذَ»; the second is omitted, i.e. "as children".
It is also possible that «اتَّخَذَ» takes one object, as in (قَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا).
And (مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), or attached (mutaʿalliq) to «اتَّخَذَ».

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَا فِي هَذَا الْقُرْآنِ لِيَذَّكَّرُوا وَمَا يَزِيدُهُمْ إِلَّا نُفُورًا (٤١)).
His saying, exalted is He: (وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَا): the object is omitted, its implied form being: "We have varied the admonitions", and the like.

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ لَوْ كَانَ مَعَهُ آلِهَةٌ كَمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذًا لَابْتَغَوْا إِلَى ذِي الْعَرْشِ سَبِيلًا (٤٢)).
His saying, exalted is He: (كَمَا يَقُولُونَ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "a being like their saying".

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا (٤٣)).
His saying, exalted is He: (عُلُوًّا): it stands in the place of «تَعَالِيًا», because that is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of His saying «تَعَالَى»; and one maṣdar may stand in the place of another of the same meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ الْقُرْآنَ جَعَلْنَا بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ حِجَابًا مَسْتُورًا (٤٥)).
His saying, exalted is He: (مَسْتُورًا): i.e. veiled by another veil above it.
It has also been said: «مَسْتُور» is in the sense of «سَاتِر» (veiling).

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَجَعَلْنَا عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ وَفِي آذَانِهِمْ وَقْرًا وَإِذَا ذَكَرْتَ رَبَّكَ فِي الْقُرْآنِ وَحْدَهُ وَلَّوْا عَلَى أَدْبَارِهِمْ نُفُورًا (٤٦)).
His saying, exalted is He: (أَنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ): i.e. for fear that they understand it, or out of dislike … [Translator's note: the sentence breaks off thus in the source].
(نُفُورًا): the plural of «نَافِر»; it may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) like «الْقُعُود». If you wish, you make it a ḥāl (circumstantial); and if you wish, you make it a maṣdar of «وَلَّوْا», because it means "they fled".

ukberi-tibyan:47-49.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَسْتَمِعُونَ بِهِ إِذْ يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ وَإِذْ هُمْ نَجْوَى إِذْ يَقُولُ الظَّالِمُونَ إِنْ تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا رَجُلًا مَسْحُورًا (٤٧) انْظُرْ كَيْفَ ضَرَبُوا لَكَ الْأَمْثَالَ فَضَلُّوا فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَبِيلًا (٤٨) وَقَالُوا أَئِذَا كُنَّا عِظَامًا وَرُفَاتًا أَئِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ خَلْقًا جَدِيدًا (٤٩)).
His saying, exalted is He: (يَسْتَمِعُونَ بِهِ): it has been said: the bāʾ means the lām. It has also been said: it keeps its basic meaning, i.e. [whether] they listen with their hearts, or with the outward part of their hearing. And «إِذْ» is an adverb (ẓarf) for the first «يَسْتَمِعُونَ».
And «النَّجْوَى» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "people of secret talk".
It may also be the plural of «نَجِيّ», like «قَتِيل» and «قَتْلَى».
(إِذْ يَقُولُ): a badal (substitute) from the first «إِذْ». It has also been said: the implied form is "remember when he says".
And the tāʾ in «الرُّفَات» is a root letter. What governs «إِذْ» is what «مَبْعُوثُونَ» indicates, not «مَبْعُوثُونَ» itself, because what comes after «أَنْ» [Translator's note: so vocalized in the source; the verse has «أَئِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ», i.e. «إِنَّ»] does not govern what comes before it.
And (خَلْقًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial), in the sense of «مَخْلُوق» (created). It may also be a maṣdar, i.e. "we will be raised a new raising".

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَوْ خَلْقًا مِمَّا يَكْبُرُ فِي صُدُورِكُمْ فَسَيَقُولُونَ مَنْ يُعِيدُنَا قُلِ الَّذِي فَطَرَكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ فَسَيُنْغِضُونَ إِلَيْكَ رُءُوسَهُمْ وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَى هُوَ قُلْ عَسَى أَنْ يَكُونَ قَرِيبًا (٥١)).
His saying, exalted is He: (قُلِ الَّذِي فَطَرَكُمْ): i.e. "He who created you will bring you back"; it is an allusion to giving life, and «يُعِيدُكُمْ» has indicated it.
And (أَنْ يَكُونَ): in the position of the accusative by «عَسَى», its noun being latent (muḍmar) in it; it may also be in the position of the nominative by «عَسَى», with no pronoun in it.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَوْمَ يَدْعُوكُمْ فَتَسْتَجِيبُونَ بِحَمْدِهِ وَتَظُنُّونَ إِنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا (٥٢)).
His saying, exalted is He: (يَوْمَ يَدْعُوكُمْ): it is an adverb (ẓarf) for «يَكُونَ»; it may not be an adverb for the noun of «كَانَ», even though it is the pronoun of the maṣdar (verbal noun), because a pronoun does not govern.
It may also be an adverb for the raising (al-baʿth), which the meaning of the speech has indicated.
It is also possible that the implied form is: "remember the day He calls you".
(بِحَمْدِهِ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "and you will respond praising". The bāʾ may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَدْعُوكُمْ».
And (تَظُنُّونَ): i.e. "while you think", so the clause is a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقُلْ لِعِبَادِي يَقُولُوا الَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يَنْزَغُ بَيْنَهُمْ إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ كَانَ لِلْإِنْسَانِ عَدُوًّا مُبِينًا (٥٣)).
His saying, exalted is He: (يَقُولُوا): it has been mentioned in [Sūrat] Ibrāhīm.
(يَنْزَغُ): it is read with fatḥa on the zāy and with kasra; they are two dialectal forms.

ukberi-tibyan:55-55.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَرَبُّكَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَلَقَدْ فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَ النَّبِيِّينَ عَلَى بَعْضٍ وَآتَيْنَا دَاوُدَ زَبُورًا (٥٥)).
His saying, exalted is He: (زَبُورًا): it is read with fatḥa and with ḍamma, and it has been mentioned in al-Nisāʾ. There are two views on it. The first: it is a proper name; one says «زَبُور» and «الزَّبُور», just as one says «عَبَّاس» and «الْعَبَّاس».
The second: it is indefinite, i.e. "a book among the books".

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ يَبْتَغُونَ إِلَى رَبِّهِمُ الْوَسِيلَةَ أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ وَيَرْجُونَ رَحْمَتَهُ وَيَخَافُونَ عَذَابَهُ إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّكَ كَانَ مَحْذُورًا (٥٧)).
His saying, exalted is He: (أَيُّهُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أَقْرَبُ» is its khabar (predicate); it is interrogative, and the clause is in the position of the accusative by «يَدْعُونَ».
It is also possible that «أَيُّهُمْ» means «الَّذِي», being a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in «يَدْعُونَ», the implied form being "the one who is nearest". There is a long discussion about it that will be mentioned in [Sūrat] Maryam.

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا مَنَعَنَا أَنْ نُرْسِلَ بِالْآيَاتِ إِلَّا أَنْ كَذَّبَ بِهَا الْأَوَّلُونَ وَآتَيْنَا ثَمُودَ النَّاقَةَ مُبْصِرَةً فَظَلَمُوا بِهَا وَمَا نُرْسِلُ بِالْآيَاتِ إِلَّا تَخْوِيفًا (٥٩)).
His saying, exalted is He: (أَنْ نُرْسِلَ): i.e. "from sending (مِنْ أَنْ نُرْسِلَ)"; so it is in the position of the accusative, or of the genitive, according to the disagreement between al-Khalīl and Sībawayh; I have mentioned its parallels.
(أَنْ كَذَّبَ): in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of «مَنَعَنَا»; there is an omitted muḍāf in it, its implied form being: "except the destruction [incurred by] the denial". It was Allah's custom to destroy whoever denied the manifest signs, and He did not will to destroy the idolaters of Quraysh, because of His knowledge that some of them would believe and that some of those born of them would believe. (مُبْصِرَةً): i.e. possessing sight, i.e. by which insight is gained.
It has also been said: «مُبْصِرَةً» means "indicating", just as a guide is called «مُرْشِد».
And it is read with fatḥa on the mīm and the ṣād [«مَبْصَرَةً»], i.e. an enlightenment (تَبْصِرَة).
(تَخْوِيفًا): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لَكَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ أَحَاطَ بِالنَّاسِ وَمَا جَعَلْنَا الرُّؤْيَا الَّتِي أَرَيْنَاكَ إِلَّا فِتْنَةً لِلنَّاسِ وَالشَّجَرَةَ الْمَلْعُونَةَ فِي الْقُرْآنِ وَنُخَوِّفُهُمْ فَمَا يَزِيدُهُمْ إِلَّا طُغْيَانًا كَبِيرًا (٦٠)).
His saying, exalted is He: (وَإِذْ قُلْنَا): i.e. "remember".
And (الشَّجَرَةَ): conjoined to «الرُّؤْيَا», the implied form being: "and We did not make the tree except a trial".
It was read irregularly (shādhdh) in the nominative [«وَالشَّجَرَةُ»], the khabar (predicate) being omitted, i.e. "a trial"; it is also possible that the khabar is «فِي الْقُرْآنِ». Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ قَالَ أَأَسْجُدُ لِمَنْ خَلَقْتَ طِينًا (٦١)).
His saying, exalted is He: (طِينًا): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَنْ», or from the omitted returning pronoun. On the first view what governs it is «اسْجُدْ» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has «أَأَسْجُدُ»], and on the second «خَلَقْتَ».
It has also been said: the implied form is "from clay (مِنْ طِينٍ)"; when the preposition was dropped, it became accusative.

ukberi-tibyan:62-62.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ أَرَأَيْتَكَ هَذَا الَّذِي كَرَّمْتَ عَلَيَّ لَئِنْ أَخَّرْتِنِي إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ لَأَحْتَنِكَنَّ ذُرِّيَّتَهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا (٦٢)).
His saying, exalted is He: (هَذَا): it is accusative by «أَرَأَيْتَ».
And «الَّذِي» is a naʿt (adjective) of it; the second object is omitted, its implied form being: "his preference" or "his being honoured". The discussion of (أَرَأَيْتَكَ) has been given in al-Anʿām.

ukberi-tibyan:63-64.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ اذْهَبْ فَمَنْ تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ فَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ جَزَاؤُكُمْ جَزَاءً مَوْفُورًا (٦٣) وَاسْتَفْزِزْ مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ مِنْهُمْ بِصَوْتِكَ وَأَجْلِبْ عَلَيْهِمْ بِخَيْلِكَ وَرَجِلِكَ وَشَارِكْهُمْ فِي الْأَمْوَالِ وَالْأَولَادِ وَعِدْهُمْ وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ إِلَّا غُرُورًا (٦٤)).
His saying, exalted is He: (جَزَاءً): a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "you will be recompensed with a recompense".
It has also been said: it is a preparatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa). It has also been said: it is a tamyīz (specification).
(مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ): «مَنْ» is interrogative, in the position of the accusative by «اسْتَطَعْتَ», i.e. "whomever of them you are able to provoke". It may also mean «الَّذِي».
(وَرَجِلِكَ): it is read with sukūn on the jīm [«وَرَجْلِكَ»], meaning the foot-soldiers. And it is read with kasra on it, which is of the pattern faʿil, from «رَجِلَ يَرْجَلُ», when one becomes a walker.
And it is read «وَرِجَالِكَ», i.e. with your horsemen and your foot-soldiers.
(وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ): a turn from the second person to the third person.

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (رَبُّكُمُ الَّذِي يُزْجِي لَكُمُ الْفُلْكَ فِي الْبَحْرِ لِتَبْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِهِ إِنَّهُ كَانَ بِكُمْ رَحِيمًا (٦٦)).
His saying, exalted is He: (رَبُّكُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «الَّذِي» with its ṣila (relative clause) is the khabar (predicate).
It has also been said: it is an adjective (ṣifa) of His saying (الَّذِي فَطَرَكُمْ), or a badal (substitute) from it; and that is permissible even though the distance between them is great.

ukberi-tibyan:67-67.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا مَسَّكُمُ الضُّرُّ فِي الْبَحْرِ ضَلَّ مَنْ تَدْعُونَ إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ فَلَمَّا نَجَّاكُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ أَعْرَضْتُمْ وَكَانَ الْإِنْسَانُ كَفُورًا (٦٧)).
His saying, exalted is He: (إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ): a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). It has also been said: it is connected (muttaṣil), conforming to the basic rule of the chapter.

ukberi-tibyan:68-68.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَفَأَمِنْتُمْ أَنْ يَخْسِفَ بِكُمْ جَانِبَ الْبَرِّ أَوْ يُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكُمْ حَاصِبًا ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُوا لَكُمْ وَكِيلًا (٦٨)).
His saying, exalted is He: (أَنْ يَخْسِفَ): it is read with the nūn and with the yāʾ, and likewise «نُرْسِلَ», «نُعِيدَكُمْ» and «نُغْرِقَكُمْ».
(بِكُمْ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جَانِبَ الْبَرِّ», i.e. "We cause the side of the land to swallow up, with you [in it]".
It has also been said: the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «نَخْسِفَ», i.e. because of you.

ukberi-tibyan:69-69.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَمْ أَمِنْتُمْ أَنْ يُعِيدَكُمْ فِيهِ تَارَةً أُخْرَى فَيُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكُمْ قَاصِفًا مِنَ الرِّيحِ فَيُغْرِقَكُمْ بِمَا كَفَرْتُمْ ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُوا لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا بِهِ تَبِيعًا (٦٩)).
His saying, exalted is He: (بِهِ تَبِيعًا): the bāʾ may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تَبِيع», or to «تَجِدُوا», or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «تَبِيعًا».

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَوْمَ نَدْعُوا كُلَّ أُنَاسٍ بِإِمَامِهِمْ فَمَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَأُولَئِكَ يَقْرَءُونَ كِتَابَهُمْ وَلَا يُظْلَمُونَ فَتِيلًا (٧١)).
His saying, exalted is He: (يَوْمَ نَدْعُوا): there are several views on it.
The first: it is an adverb (ẓarf) for what His saying «وَلَا يُظْلَمُونَ فَتِيلًا» indicates, its implied form being: "they will not be wronged on the day We call".
The second: it is an adverb for what His saying (مَتَى هُوَ) indicates. The third: it is an adverb for His saying (فَتَسْتَجِيبُونَ). The fourth: it is a badal (substitute) from «يَدْعُوكُمْ». The fifth: it is an object, i.e. "remember the day We call".
Al-Ḥasan read it with a yāʾ with ḍamma and a wāw after the ʿayn, and with «كُلُّ» in the nominative [«يُدْعَوْ كُلُّ»]; there are two views on it. The first: he intended «يُدْعَى», but gave the alif a full (tafkhīm) pronunciation and so changed it into a wāw. The second: he intended «يُدْعَوْنَ» and dropped the nūn; and «كُلُّ» is a badal from the pronoun.
(بِإِمَامِهِمْ): there are two views on it.
The first: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «نَدْعُو», i.e. We say: "O followers of Moses", and "O followers of Muḥammad", blessings and peace be upon them both; or "O people of the Book", "O people of the Quran". The second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being: "mingled with their prophet", or "held to account".

ukberi-tibyan:72-72.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَنْ كَانَ فِي هَذِهِ أَعْمَى فَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ أَعْمَى وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا (٧٢)).
His saying, exalted is He: (أَعْمَى): the first is in the sense of fāʿil [i.e. an adjective: blind]. Regarding the second there are two views. The first: it is likewise, i.e. whoever was blind to His proof in this world will be likewise in the Hereafter.
The second: it is the afʿal [elative] form that calls for «مِنْ» (than), and for that reason He said «وَأَضَلُّ» (and further astray). Abū ʿAmr read the first with imāla (inclination of the vowel) but not the second, because he held that the second calls for «مِنْ», so it is as though the alif were in the middle of the word; «تُمَثِّلُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ» [Translator's note: so in the source; these words appear to be corrupt and give no clear sense here].

ukberi-tibyan:74-74.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَوْلَا أَنْ ثَبَّتْنَاكَ لَقَدْ كِدْتَ تَرْكَنُ إِلَيْهِمْ شَيْئًا قَلِيلًا (٧٤)).
His saying, exalted is He: (تَرْكَنُ): with fatḥa on the kāf, its past tense having kasra [«رَكِنَ»]. Some said: it has fatḥa in both the past and the imperfect, and that comes from the overlapping of two dialects: among the Arabs there are those who say «رَكِنَ يَرْكَنُ», and among them those who say «رَكَنَ يَرْكُنُ», with fatḥa in the past and ḍamma in the imperfect; so someone whose dialect had fatḥa in the past heard fatḥa in the imperfect from one whose dialect that was, or the reverse, and combined the two. What led the holder of this view to it was his belief that the pattern faʿala yafʿalu, with fatḥa on the middle radical in both, has not come down from them in verbs without guttural letters except «أَبَى يَأْبَى». And it has been read with ḍamma on the kāf [«تَرْكُنُ»].

ukberi-tibyan:76-76.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنْ كَادُوا لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ لِيُخْرِجُوكَ مِنْهَا وَإِذًا لَا يَلْبَثُونَ خِلَافَكَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا (٧٦)).
His saying, exalted is He: (لَا يَلْبَثُونَ): the well-known reading is with fatḥa on the yāʾ, without doubling, and with the nūn retained, on the basis that «إِذَنْ» is made inoperative (ilghāʾ), because the conjunctive wāw makes the clause «مُخْتَلِفَة» [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense required seems to be "connected"] with what precedes it, so «إِذَنْ» is an insertion (ḥashw).
And it is read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and with doubling [«لَا يُلَبَّثُونَ»], in the passive.
In some codices it is without the nūn [«لَا يَلْبَثُوا»], on the basis that «إِذَنْ» is made operative, no account being taken of the wāw, since it can come as resumptive.
(خِلَافَكَ) and «خَلْفَكَ»: two dialectal forms with one meaning, and it has been read with both.
(إِلَّا قَلِيلًا): i.e. a little time.

ukberi-tibyan:77-77.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (سُنَّةَ مَنْ قَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ مِنْ رُسُلِنَا وَلَا تَجِدُ لِسُنَّتِنَا تَحْوِيلًا (٧٧)).
His saying, exalted is He: (سُنَّةَ مَنْ قَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا): it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "We have laid down for you the way of the prophets who came before, the blessings of Allah be upon them".
It may also be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "follow the way of those We sent", as Allah the Exalted said: (فَبِهُدَاهُمُ اقْتَدِهِ).

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ لِدُلُوكِ الشَّمْسِ إِلَى غَسَقِ اللَّيْلِ وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا (٧٨)).
His saying, exalted is He: (إِلَى غَسَقِ اللَّيْلِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الصَّلَاة», i.e. "extended [to the darkness of night]".
It may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أَقِمْ», in which case it marks the end-point of the establishing [of prayer].
(وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ): there are two views on it.
The first: it is conjoined to «الصَّلَاة», i.e. "and establish the dawn prayer". The second: it is by way of incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e. "upon you is the recitation of dawn", or "hold to [it]".

ukberi-tibyan:79-79.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِ نَافِلَةً لَكَ عَسَى أَنْ يَبْعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقَامًا مَحْمُودًا (٧٩)).
His saying, exalted is He: (نَافِلَةً لَكَ): there are two views on it.
The first: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of «تَهَجُّدًا», i.e. "perform a supererogatory act (تَنَفَّلْ تَنَفُّلًا)"; and «فَاعِلُهُ» [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense is evidently «فَاعِلَة», i.e. the pattern fāʿila] here is a maṣdar, like «الْعَافِيَة».
The second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "as a supererogatory prayer".
(مَقَامًا): there are two views on it.
The first: it is a ḥāl, its implied form being "possessing a station". The second: it is a maṣdar, its implied form being: "that He raise you, so you stand".

ukberi-tibyan:82-82.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ مَا هُوَ شِفَاءٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلَا يَزِيدُ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا خَسَارًا (٨٢)).
His saying, exalted is He: (مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ): «مِنْ» is for clarifying the genus (bayān al-jins), i.e. all of it is guidance from misguidance.
It has also been said: it is partitive (tabʿīḍ), i.e. part of it is what heals from illness. Al-Kisāʾī permitted «وَرَحْمَةً» in the accusative, conjoined to «مَا».

ukberi-tibyan:83-83.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا أَنْعَمْنَا عَلَى الْإِنْسَانِ أَعْرَضَ وَنَأَى بِجَانِبِهِ وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ كَانَ يَئُوسًا (٨٣)).
His saying, exalted is He: (وَنَأَى): it is read with an alif after the hamza, i.e. he drew away from obedience.
And it is read with a hamza after the alif [«وَنَاءَ»], and there are two views on it.
The first: it is the metathesis of «نَأَى». The second: it means «نَهَضَ» (rose up), i.e. he raised himself above accepting obedience, or rose up in disobedience and arrogance.

ukberi-tibyan:84-84.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلَى شَاكِلَتِهِ فَرَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ هُوَ أَهْدَى سَبِيلًا (٨٤)).
His saying, exalted is He: (أَهْدَى سَبِيلًا): it may be an afʿal [elative] from «هَدَى» [in the sense of] guiding another; or from «اهْتَدَى», with the augment letters dropped; or from «هَدَى» in the sense of «اهْتَدَى» (was guided), in which case it is intransitive.

ukberi-tibyan:85-85.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الرُّوحِ قُلِ الرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي وَمَا أُوتِيتُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا (٨٥)).
His saying, exalted is He: (مِنَ الْعِلْمِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أُوتِيتُمْ»; it cannot be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «قَلِيلًا», because that would involve placing what is governed before «إِلَّا».

ukberi-tibyan:87-87.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِلَّا رَحْمَةً مِنْ رَبِّكَ إِنَّ فَضْلَهُ كَانَ عَلَيْكَ كَبِيرًا (٨٧)).
His saying, exalted is He: (إِلَّا رَحْمَةً): it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), the implied form being: "We preserved it for you out of mercy".
It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: "but We had mercy on you with a mercy".

ukberi-tibyan:88-88.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ لَئِنِ اجْتَمَعَتِ الْإِنْسُ وَالْجِنُّ عَلَى أَنْ يَأْتُوا بِمِثْلِ هَذَا الْقُرْآنِ لَا يَأْتُونَ بِمِثْلِهِ وَلَوْ كَانَ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ ظَهِيرًا (٨٨)).
His saying, exalted is He: (لَا يَأْتُونَ) is not the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition, but the answer to an omitted oath, indicated by the preparatory lām (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa) in His saying «لَئِنِ اجْتَمَعَتِ».
It has also been said: it is the apodosis of the condition, and it was not made jussive because the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) is a past verb.

ukberi-tibyan:90-90.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَالُوا لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّى تَفْجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ يَنْبُوعًا (٩٠)).
His saying, exalted is He: (حَتَّى تَفْجُرَ): it is read with doubling [«تُفَجِّرَ»], for intensiveness; and with fatḥa on the tāʾ, ḍamma on the jīm, and without doubling.
And the yāʾ in «يَنْبُوعًا» is augmentative, because it is from «نَبَعَ»; so it is like «يَعْبُوب» from «عَبَّ».

ukberi-tibyan:92-92.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَوْ تُسْقِطَ السَّمَاءَ كَمَا زَعَمْتَ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفًا أَوْ تَأْتِيَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ قَبِيلًا (٩٢)).
His saying, exalted is He: (كِسَفًا): it is read with fatḥa on the sīn, and it is the plural of «كِسْفَة», like «قِرْبَة» and «قِرَب». And with sukūn on it [«كِسْفًا»], and there are two views on it.
The first: it is lightened from the form with fatḥa, or it is like «سِدْرَة» and «سِدْر». The second: it is a singular of the pattern fiʿl in the sense of mafʿūl, and its accusative is as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السَّمَاء»; it was not made feminine because the femininity of «السَّمَاء» is not real (ghayr ḥaqīqī), or because «السَّمَاء» is in the sense of «السَّقْف» (the roof). The kāf in (كَمَا) is an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a causing to fall like your claim". And (قَبِيلًا): a ḥāl from «الْمَلَائِكَة», or from «اللَّه» and «الْمَلَائِكَة». (نَقْرَؤُهُ): an adjective of «كِتَاب», or a ḥāl from the genitive noun. (قُلْ): as an imperative; and «قَالَ» as a report about him.

ukberi-tibyan:94-94.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا مَنَعَ النَّاسَ أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا إِذْ جَاءَهُمُ الْهُدَى إِلَّا أَنْ قَالُوا أَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ بَشَرًا رَسُولًا (٩٤)).
His saying, exalted is He: (أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا): the object of «مَنَعَ»; and «أَنْ قَالُوا» is its fāʿil (agent).

ukberi-tibyan:95-95.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ لَوْ كَانَ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَلَائِكَةٌ يَمْشُونَ مُطْمَئِنِّينَ لَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَلَكًا رَسُولًا (٩٥)).
His saying, exalted is He: (يَمْشُونَ): an adjective (ṣifa) of «الْمَلَائِكَة».
And (مُطْمَئِنِّينَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun.

ukberi-tibyan:97-97.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَنْ يَهْدِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الْمُهْتَدِي وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُمْ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِهِ وَنَحْشُرُهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ عُمْيًا وَبُكْمًا وَصُمًّا مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ كُلَّمَا خَبَتْ زِدْنَاهُمْ سَعِيرًا (٩٧)).
His saying, exalted is He: (عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ): a ḥāl (circumstantial). And «عُمْيًا» is another ḥāl: either a badal (substitute) from the first, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in the preposition phrase. (مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ): it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf), or a projected ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). (كُلَّمَا خَبَتْ …): the clause to the end of the verse is a ḥāl from «جَهَنَّم», and what governs it is the meaning of «الْمَأْوَى»; it may also be resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:98-98.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ذَلِكَ جَزَاؤُهُمْ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِنَا وَقَالُوا أَئِذَا كُنَّا عِظَامًا وَرُفَاتًا أَئِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ خَلْقًا جَدِيدًا (٩٨)).
His saying, exalted is He: (ذَلِكَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); «جَزَاؤُهُمْ» is its khabar (predicate), and «بِأَنَّهُمْ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «جَزَاء». It has also been said: «ذَلِكَ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is that"; «جَزَاؤُهُمْ» is a mubtadaʾ and «بِأَنَّهُمْ» the khabar.
It is also possible that «جَزَاؤُهُمْ» is a badal (substitute) or an explicative (bayān), and «بِأَنَّهُمْ» is the khabar of «ذَلِكَ».

ukberi-tibyan:100-100.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ لَوْ أَنْتُمْ تَمْلِكُونَ خَزَائِنَ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّي إِذًا لَأَمْسَكْتُمْ خَشْيَةَ الْإِنْفَاقِ وَكَانَ الْإِنْسَانُ قَتُورًا (١٠٠)).
His saying, exalted is He: (لَوْ أَنْتُمْ): in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb; it is not a mubtadaʾ (subject), because «لَوْ» calls for a verb just as the conditional «إِنْ» calls for it. The implied form is "if you possessed (لَوْ تَمْلِكُونَ)"; when the verb was omitted, the attached pronoun became detached. And the overt «تَمْلِكُونَ» is an explanation (tafsīr) of the omitted one.
(لَأَمْسَكْتُمْ): its object is omitted, i.e. "you would have withheld the wealth". It has also been said: it is intransitive, in the sense of "you would have been miserly".
(خَشْيَةَ): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:101-101.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى تِسْعَ آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍ فَاسْأَلْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ إِذْ جَاءَهُمْ فَقَالَ لَهُ فِرْعَوْنُ إِنِّي لَأَظُنُّكَ يَا مُوسَى مَسْحُورًا (١٠١)).
His saying, exalted is He: (بَيِّنَاتٍ): an adjective (ṣifa) of «آيَات», or of «تِسْع».
(إِذْ جَاءَهُمْ): there are two views on it.
The first: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «اسْأَلْ» according to the meaning, because the meaning is "mention to the Children of Israel when he came to them". It has also been said: the implied form is "remember when he came to them", which is something other than what «اسْأَلْ» was construed as.
The second: it is an adverb (ẓarf), and regarding what governs it there are several views. The first: «آتَيْنَا». The second: an implied «قُلْنَا», i.e. "and We said to him: ask". The third: «قُلْ», its implied form being: "say to your adversary: ask the Children of Israel", the one meant being Pharaoh, i.e. "say, O Moses". The [expected] way would have been to say "when you came to them (إِذْ جِئْتَهُمْ)", but it turned from the second person to the third person.

ukberi-tibyan:102-102.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا أَنْزَلَ هَؤُلَاءِ إِلَّا رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ بَصَائِرَ وَإِنِّي لَأَظُنُّكَ يَا فِرْعَوْنُ مَثْبُورًا (١٠٢)).
His saying, exalted is He: (لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ): with fatḥa, in the second person, i.e. "you knew that, but you were obstinate"; and with ḍamma [«عَلِمْتُ»], i.e. "I am not in doubt about what you have brought".
(بَصَائِرَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «هَؤُلَاءِ»; it came after «إِلَّا» while being a ḥāl from what precedes it, for the reason we mentioned in [Sūrat] Hūd at His saying (وَمَا نَرَاكَ اتَّبَعَكَ).

ukberi-tibyan:104-104.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقُلْنَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ لِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ اسْكُنُوا الْأَرْضَ فَإِذَا جَاءَ وَعْدُ الْآخِرَةِ جِئْنَا بِكُمْ لَفِيفًا (١٠٤)).
